aspendos.t: Aspendos, a wealthy Pamphylian city on the Eurymedon river, near which Athens defeated Persia and later the Romans built a famous theatre.
aspendos.o: Aspendos rose on a hill by the [[e:eurymedon-river|Eurymedon]] river, a few kilometres from the sea, in the 7th century BCE. Its people claimed descent from settlers from [[s:argos|Argos]], but its coins were inscribed in the local Pamphylian Greek dialect with the name Estwediiys.
aspendos.r: The city prospered from [[e:horse-breeding|horse breeding]], farming and salt and river trade, and minted [[e:silver|silver]] coins. Around 466 BCE the Athenian general [[e:cimon|Cimon]] defeated a Persian fleet and army near the [[e:eurymedon-river|Eurymedon]]. In 333 BCE Aspendos submitted to Alexander, who demanded tribute and horses after it reneged on terms.
aspendos.e: Aspendos passed under [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] and [[e:pergamenes|Pergamene]] influence, then Roman rule, joining the province of [[s:galatia|Galatia]] in 25 BCE. Its [[e:theatre|theatre]], built in the 2nd century CE, is one of the best preserved from antiquity.

ayyubid-emirate-of-mayyafariqin.t: The Ayyubid principality of Diyar Bakr, whose last prince died resisting the Mongols after a long siege in 1260.
ayyubid-emirate-of-mayyafariqin.o: [[e:saladin|Saladin]] took [[e:mayyafariqin|Mayyafariqin]] in 1185 from the Shah-Armens' sphere; after a period under his nephew [[e:taqi-al-din-umar|Taqi al-Din]] it passed to his brother [[e:al-adil|al-Adil]], whose son [[e:al-awhad-ayyub|al-Awhad Ayyub]] ruled it and in 1207 took [[e:ahlat|Ahlat]]. It became a hereditary Ayyubid principality in the [[e:upper-mesopotamia|Jazira]].
ayyubid-emirate-of-mayyafariqin.r: The principality passed to al-[[e:al-ashraf-musa-sultan-of-damascus|Ashraf Musa]] and then to al-Muzaffar [[e:ghazi|Ghazi]], sons of [[e:al-adil|al-Adil]], and then to Ghazi's son [[e:al-kamil-muhammad-of-mayyafariqin|al-Kamil Muhammad]]. Its rulers controlled the old [[e:marwanids|Marwanid]] capital, rich farmland north of the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] and roads to [[e:ahlat|Ahlat]]. They faced the [[e:khwarazmians|Khwarazmians]], the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]] and finally the [[e:mongols|Mongols]]. [[e:al-kamil|Al-Kamil]] Muhammad defied [[e:hulagu-khan|Hulagu]].
ayyubid-emirate-of-mayyafariqin.e: Mongol forces besieged [[e:mayyafariqin|Mayyafariqin]] from 1259; in 1260 the city fell after famine, [[e:al-kamil-muhammad-of-mayyafariqin|al-Kamil Muhammad]] was killed and his head was paraded in Syrian cities.

archbishopric-of-riga.t: Ecclesiastical principality that led the Christian conquest of Livonia and governed much of Latvia for nearly four centuries.
archbishopric-of-riga.o: The missionary [[e:saint-meinhard|Meinhard]] became [[e:bishop|bishop]] of the [[e:livonians|Livs]] at [[e:ikskile|Üxküll]] in 1186. His successor [[e:albert-of-riga|Albert of Buxhoeveden]] founded Riga in 1201 and moved the see there, directing the [[e:crusade|crusade]] with the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]]. In 1255 Riga was raised to an archbishopric under [[e:albert-suerbeer|Albert Suerbeer]], with authority over the bishoprics of [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].
archbishopric-of-riga.r: The archbishops were princes of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]], ruling lands along the [[e:western-dvina|Daugava]] and [[e:gauja|Gauja]] through [[e:vassal|vassals]] and castles such as [[s:turaida|Turaida]] and [[s:principality-of-koknese|Kokenhusen]]. Their rule was marked by long conflicts with the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] and with the citizens of Riga over control of the city. The cathedral chapter and vassals sat in the Livonian diets.
archbishopric-of-riga.e: The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] reached Riga in the 1520s, weakening the archbishops. During the [[e:livonian-war|Livonian War]] the last archbishop, [[e:wilhelm-of-brandenburg|Wilhelm of Brandenburg]], placed his lands under Polish-Lithuanian protection, and in 1561-1562 they were secularised and incorporated into the [[s:duchy-of-livonia|Duchy of Livonia]] under [[e:sigismund-ii-augustus|Sigismund II Augustus]].

ancient-shu.t: The early kingdom of the Sichuan basin, heir to the astonishing bronze culture of Sanxingdui, conquered by Qin in 316 BCE.
ancient-shu.o: Shu emerged in the [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] plain from a long local tradition: the Sanxingdui culture, with its giant bronze masks and standing figure, and the later [[e:jinsha-site|Jinsha site]] in Chengdu. Later legends name a series of kings, [[e:cancong|Cancong]], Yufu and [[e:du-yu-king-of-shu|Duyu]], followed by the [[e:kaiming-dynasty|Kaiming dynasty]], but these accounts were written centuries afterwards.
ancient-shu.r: Shu developed largely independently of the Zhou states, and its bronze art, sun worship and burial customs, including boat-shaped coffins, differ sharply from those of northern [[e:china|China]]. Under the [[e:kaiming-dynasty|Kaiming]] kings it was centred on [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] and was rich in [[e:rice|rice]], salt and [[e:copper|copper]]. It had no widely used script; the so-called [[e:ba-shu-script|Ba-Shu]] signs remain undeciphered.
ancient-shu.e: Quarrels between Shu and the neighbouring [[s:state-of-ba|State of Ba]] gave the [[s:state-of-qin|State of Qin]] a pretext; in 316 BCE the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] general [[e:sima-cuo|Sima Cuo]] conquered Shu. Qin settled colonists there, and the governor [[e:li-bing|Li Bing]] built the Dujiangyan irrigation system, making [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] the granary that fuelled Qin's unification of [[e:china|China]].

areopagus-of-eastern-continental-greece.t: Regional revolutionary government of eastern mainland Greece in 1821-1822, set up at Salona under Theodoros Negris.
areopagus-of-eastern-continental-greece.o: Eastern mainland [[e:greece|Greece]], including [[e:attica|Attica]], [[e:boeotia|Boeotia]], [[e:phocis|Phocis]] and [[e:locris|Locris]], joined the revolution in 1821. In November 1821 an assembly of local representatives met at [[e:amfissa|Salona]] ([[s:county-of-salona|Amfissa]]) and, under the guidance of the [[e:phanariotes|Phanariot]] diplomat [[e:theodoros-negris|Theodoros Negris]], adopted a legal charter and created a governing council named after the ancient [[e:areopagus|Athenian Areopagus]].
areopagus-of-eastern-continental-greece.r: The [[e:areopagus|Areopagus]] was made up of local notables and was meant to run the administration, justice and war effort in the region. It struggled to control powerful armed chieftains, above all [[e:odysseas-androutsos|Odysseas Androutsos]], with whom it was in open conflict. Its authority over the scattered and contested territory was limited.
areopagus-of-eastern-continental-greece.e: After the First [[e:national-assembly-of-france|National Assembly]] at [[s:epidaurus|Epidaurus]] created the [[s:first-hellenic-republic|First Hellenic Republic]] in January 1822, the regional bodies were subordinated to central government. The [[e:areopagus|Areopagus]] continued for a time but lost its role during 1822 and 1823.

akusha-dargo-union.t: A powerful union of self-governing Dargin communities in central Dagestan, led by the qadi of Akusha, which long resisted both khans and Russia.
akusha-dargo-union.o: The [[e:dargins|Dargin]] highlands of central [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]] were home to free communities, called jamaats, that governed themselves without princes. By the 17th century the largest of them formed a union around the village of [[e:akusha|Akusha]], whose qadi, a religious judge, served as its leading authority.
akusha-dargo-union.r: The union was a confederation of village communities with their own assemblies and customary law, coordinated by the qadi and councils of elders. It could field several thousand warriors and was among the strongest forces in [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]]. Its people farmed terraced fields, herded sheep and were known for metalworking in villages such as Kubachi nearby.
akusha-dargo-union.e: [[e:aleksey-yermolov|General Yermolov]] defeated the [[e:akusha|Akusha]] forces at Levashi in 1819 and imposed Russian authority. The union was finally incorporated into the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] in 1844 amid the wars of the [[s:caucasian-imamate|Caucasian Imamate]].

andecavi.t: Gallic people of Anjou whose leader Dumnacus fought one of the last campaigns against Rome in 51 BCE.
andecavi.o: The Andecavi, called Andes by Caesar, lived on the lower [[e:loire|Loire]] around [[e:angers|Angers]]. Caesar quartered legions among them in 57 BCE and records that they joined the revolt of 52 BCE.
andecavi.r: Little is known of their institutions beyond their war leaders.
andecavi.e: In 51 BCE [[e:dumnacus|Dumnacus]] besieged the pro-Roman [[s:pictones|Pictones]] in [[e:poitiers|Lemonum]], but was defeated by Caesar's legate Gaius Fabius and fled. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town was [[e:angers|Juliomagus]], later called Andecavi, the origin of Angers and of the name [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]].

archchancellors-electorate.t: State created for Karl Theodor von Dalberg, the last Archbishop of Mainz, to keep the imperial archchancellor's office alive.
archchancellors-electorate.o: When the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] passed to [[e:france|France]], the [[s:electorate-of-mainz|Electorate of Mainz]] lost its capital. The [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]] kept its archbishop, [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Karl Theodor von Dalberg]], as elector and archchancellor of the Empire, and gave him the [[s:principality-of-aschaffenburg|Principality of Aschaffenburg]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] and the County of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-wetzlar|Wetzlar]], with the archiepiscopal seat moved to Regensburg.
archchancellors-electorate.r: [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Dalberg]] was an [[e:age-of-enlightenment|Enlightenment]] churchman who governed from [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]], seat of the [[e:imperial-diet|Perpetual Imperial Diet]]. His state was scattered and Catholic, with [[e:aschaffenburg|Aschaffenburg]] as its richest part. He cultivated [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], praising him as a new [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]], and in 1806 became Prince-Primate of the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]], adding [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] to his lands.
archchancellors-electorate.e: In 1810 [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Dalberg]] ceded [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] and in exchange received [[s:county-of-hanau-munzenberg|Hanau]] and Fulda, creating the [[s:grand-duchy-of-frankfurt|Grand Duchy of Frankfurt]]. Dalberg remained its ruler until 1813, and Regensburg has belonged to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] ever since.

anconine-republic.t: A short-lived French-backed republic in the Adriatic port of Ancona, carved from the Papal States in 1797 and merged into the Roman Republic.
anconine-republic.o: French troops occupied [[s:republic-of-ancona|Ancona]], the main Adriatic port of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], in February 1797, and the [[e:treaty-of-tolentino|Treaty of Tolentino]] left them in control of it. In November 1797 local patriots, with French encouragement, proclaimed the Anconine Republic, with jurisdiction over Ancona and nearby towns of the [[e:marche|Marche]].
anconine-republic.r: The republic was governed by a provisional administration of local [[e:jacobin-club|Jacobins]] under French military control. It abolished the old papal institutions, freed the city's [[e:jews|Jews]] from the ghetto restrictions and adopted French-style laws and symbols. It also served as a base for French plans against the rest of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].
anconine-republic.e: When French troops occupied [[e:rome|Rome]] and created the [[s:roman-republic-1798-1799|Roman Republic]] (1798–1799) in February 1798, the Anconine Republic was absorbed into it in March 1798.

assaka.t: The only mahajanapada south of the Vindhya mountains, an early kingdom on the Godavari river in the northern Deccan.
assaka.o: Assaka, Ashmaka in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]], is named in Buddhist lists of the sixteen great states and by the grammarian [[e:panini|Panini]]. It lay on the Godavari river, with its capital at Potali or Potana, often identified with [[e:bodhan|Bodhan]] in modern [[e:telangana|Telangana]]. Its origins are obscure, and later tradition linked its kings to the [[e:ikshvaku|Ikshvaku]] line.
assaka.r: Little is known of its government. The [[e:sutta-nipata|Sutta Nipata]] tells of the [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] teacher Bavari, who lived on the Godavari in the Assaka country and sent his pupils north to meet the [[e:gautama-buddha|Buddha]], which shows the kingdom's links along the southern trade route, the [[e:dakshinapatha|Dakshinapatha]], to the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] valley. Its neighbour Mulaka lay around [[e:paithan|Pratishthana]].
assaka.e: Assaka appears to have come under the influence of the [[s:kingdom-of-avanti|Kingdom of Avanti]] and was later absorbed into the [[e:nanda-dynasty|Nanda]] and [[e:maurya-empire|Maurya]] empires. After the Mauryas its region formed part of the heartland of the [[s:satavahana-dynasty|Satavahana dynasty]].

astures.t: The peoples of Asturias and León, last in Iberia to fall to Rome in 19 BCE, whose land became the empire's great gold-mining district.
astures.o: The Astures occupied the lands between the Cantabrian coast and the [[e:douro|Douro]], in modern [[e:asturias|Asturias]], León and northern [[e:zamora|Zamora]], from about the 4th century BCE. [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] divided them into the Transmontani north of the mountains and the Augustani on the plateau to the south.
astures.r: They lived in castros, fortified hilltop villages of round stone houses, in many independent communities grouped by kinship. Herding, farming and metalworking supported them, and their mountains held rich gold deposits. Their main stronghold on the plain was [[e:lancia|Lancia]], near León. They spoke a Celtic language.
astures.e: The Astures fought alongside the [[s:cantabri|Cantabri]] in Augustus' [[e:cantabrian-wars|Cantabrian Wars]] of 29 to 19 BCE. After conquest [[e:rome|Rome]] founded [[e:asturica-augusta|Asturica Augusta]] ([[e:astorga|Astorga]]) and exploited the gold of [[e:las-medulas|Las Médulas]] on a vast scale. Their name survives in [[e:asturia|Asturias]] and in the later [[s:kingdom-of-asturias|Kingdom of Asturias]].

argungu-emirate.t: The successor of the Hausa Kingdom of Kebbi, which resisted the Sokoto Caliphate for most of the 19th century from its fortified capital at Argungu.
argungu-emirate.o: The [[s:kingdom-of-kebbi|Kingdom of Kebbi]] lost its capital, [[e:birnin-kebbi|Birnin Kebbi]], to [[e:fula|Fulani]] jihadists in 1805, but its rulers kept fighting from the marshes and towns to the north. Around 1831 they made Argungu, on the [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] river, their base, and from there the Kebbawa continued the war against the [[s:gwandu-emirate|Gwandu Emirate]] and Sokoto.
argungu-emirate.r: Argungu was a fortified [[e:hausa|Hausa]] state that kept old [[s:kingdom-of-kebbi|Kebbi]] titles and institutions. Its rulers were Muslims who rejected the political claims of the [[e:caliphate|caliphate]], and they allied with other Hausa refugees in [[s:kingdom-of-gobir|Gobir]] and [[s:sultanate-of-maradi|Maradi]]. The wars brought frequent raids and counter-raids, interrupted by truces, and the [[e:emirate|emirate]]'s people farmed and fished in the river valley.
argungu-emirate.e: British forces occupied Argungu in 1902, and it became an [[e:emirate|emirate]] of the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]]. Its emir still reigns, and the town is famous for the Argungu Fishing Festival, held annually since the 1930s.

alba-longa.t: Legendary mother city of the Latins in the Alban Hills, remembered by the Romans as the home of Romulus and Remus and the seat of the Latin festival.
alba-longa.o: Roman tradition held that [[e:ascanius|Ascanius]], son of the Trojan hero [[e:aeneas|Aeneas]], founded Alba Longa about thirty years after [[e:lavinium|Lavinium]], and placed its foundation in the 12th century BCE. Archaeology shows [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] villages and cemeteries around the [[e:lake-albano|Alban Lake]] and [[e:monte-cavo|Monte Cavo]] from about 1000 BCE, but no single city has been firmly identified.
alba-longa.r: The [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] described a line of Alban kings, from [[e:silvius|Silvius]] to [[e:numitor|Numitor]] and his usurping brother [[e:amulius|Amulius]], but these are legendary. What is more secure is the role of the [[e:alban-hills|Alban Hills]] as a religious centre for the [[e:latin|Latin]] peoples: the sanctuary of [[e:jupiter-latiaris|Jupiter Latiaris]] on [[e:monte-cavo|Monte Cavo]] hosted the [[e:feriae-latinae|Feriae Latinae]], a shared festival that [[e:rome|Rome]] kept celebrating long after Alba disappeared.
alba-longa.e: According to [[e:livy|Livy]], [[e:rome|Rome]] under [[e:tullus-hostilius|Tullus Hostilius]] defeated Alba after the duel of the [[e:horatii-and-curiatii|Horatii and Curiatii]] in the mid-7th century BCE, razed the city and moved its people to the [[e:caelian-hill|Caelian Hill]]. Leading Roman families such as the Julii claimed Alban descent, and the [[s:latin-league|Latin League]] inherited its religious role.

antes.t: An early Slavic people between the Dniester and the Dnieper, known from Byzantine writers as raiders and allies of the 6th-century empire.
antes.o: The Antes appear in the 6th century in [[e:procopius|Procopius]] and [[e:jordanes|Jordanes]], who describe them as a people related to the Sclaveni living east of the [[e:dniester|Dniester]]. Archaeologists usually connect them with the [[e:penkovka-culture|Penkovka culture]]. Jordanes also tells how an Antian leader named [[e:boz-king-of-the-antes|Boz]] was killed by the [[e:goths|Goths]], but the story is hard to date.
antes.r: [[e:procopius|Procopius]] says the Antes were not ruled by one man but lived in a kind of democracy, deciding matters in common, and worshipped a god of lightning as lord of all. They farmed, kept livestock and lived in scattered villages. From the 530s they raided the [[e:balkans|Balkans]], but Justinian also hired them as allies to guard the [[e:danube|Danube]].
antes.e: The [[e:avars|Avars]] attacked them in the 560s, and an Avar expedition sent against them in 602 is the last time the Antes are mentioned. Their people were absorbed into the [[e:east-slavs|East Slavic]] tribes of later centuries, while the title Anticus lingered for a time in the Byzantine emperor's style.

argentine-republic.t: The republic reunited under Buenos Aires in 1861, which became one of the world's richest countries by 1900 before a century of political turmoil.
argentine-republic.o: After [[e:bartolome-mitre|Bartolomé Mitre's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-pavon|Pavón]] in 1861 over the [[s:argentine-confederation|Argentine Confederation]], [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] and the provinces were reunited under the Constitution of 1853, as amended in 1860, which adopted the name Argentine Republic. Mitre became president in 1862.
argentine-republic.r: [[e:bartolome-mitre|Mitre]], [[e:domingo-faustino-sarmiento|Domingo Sarmiento]] and [[e:nicolas-avellaneda|Nicolás Avellaneda]] built national institutions and schools. [[e:argentina|Argentina]] fought [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]] from 1865 to 1870, and [[e:julio-argentino-roca|Julio Argentino Roca's]] [[e:conquest-of-the-desert|Conquest of the Desert]] seized the pampas and [[e:patagonia|Patagonia]]. Mass immigration from [[e:italy|Italy]] and [[e:spain|Spain]] and exports of beef and wheat made it among the world's richest countries by 1914. A military coup in 1930 began decades of instability. [[e:juan-peron|Juan Perón]] led a powerful labour-based movement from 1946.
argentine-republic.e: The dictatorship of 1976 to 1983 killed thousands in the [[e:dirty-war|Dirty War]] and lost the [[e:falklands-war|Falklands War]]. Democracy returned in 1983 under [[e:raul-alfonsin|Raúl Alfonsín]]. Repeated economic crises, including a default in 2001, followed, and [[e:javier-milei|Javier Milei]] was elected in 2023.

aram-zobah.t: Aram-Zobah, an Aramaean kingdom of the 10th century BCE, the main rival of King David in the Bible.
aram-zobah.o: Zobah was an Aramaean kingdom probably centred on the [[e:beqaa-valley|Beqaa]] valley and the region north of [[e:damascus|Damascus]]. It is known almost entirely from the [[e:hebrew-bible|Hebrew Bible]], which describes its king [[e:hadadezer-of-zobah|Hadadezer son of Rehob]] as a powerful ruler whose influence reached the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]].
aram-zobah.r: According to the [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]], [[e:hadadezer-of-zobah|Hadadezer]] commanded [[e:chariot|chariots]] and allied Aramaean kingdoms, and rich towns of his land produced bronze. Little else is known, since no inscriptions from Zobah have been found.
aram-zobah.e: The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] says [[e:david|David]] of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]] defeated [[e:hadadezer-of-zobah|Hadadezer]] and took his gold shields to [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]], and that [[e:rezon|Rezon]], a former officer, founded [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]], which soon replaced Zobah as the leading Aramaean power.

anglo-egyptian-sudan.t: Sudan under a joint British and Egyptian condominium from 1899, in practice a British colony, until independence in 1956.
anglo-egyptian-sudan.o: After [[e:herbert-kitchener|Kitchener]]'s reconquest destroyed the [[s:mahdist-state|Mahdist State]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:egypt|Egypt]] signed the [[e:anglo-egyptian-condominium|Condominium Agreement]] in January 1899. [[e:sovereignty|Sovereignty]] was formally shared, but a British governor-general, appointed on British advice, held supreme authority.
anglo-egyptian-sudan.r: British officials governed through native administration, using tribal chiefs and sultans. The [[e:gezira-scheme|Gezira Scheme]], opened in 1925, made irrigated [[e:cotton|cotton]] the main export. The south was administered separately under a Southern Policy that excluded northern influence and favoured Christian missions. After the assassination of governor-general [[e:lee-stack|Lee Stack]] in 1924, Egyptian troops were expelled.
anglo-egyptian-sudan.e: An Anglo-Egyptian agreement in 1953 provided for self-government and self-determination. [[e:sudan|Sudan]] became independent on 1 January 1956, but the separate treatment of the south contributed to a civil war that had already begun in 1955.
anglo-egyptian-sudan.re: Sunni Islam (north); traditional religions and Christianity (south)

ainu-chiefdoms.t: The self-governing communities of the Ainu, the indigenous people of Hokkaido, Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands, before Japanese annexation in 1869.
ainu-chiefdoms.o: [[e:ainu|Ainu]] culture took recognisable form around the 13th century in [[e:hokkaido|Hokkaido]], growing out of the earlier [[e:satsumon-culture|Satsumon culture]] with influences from the [[e:okhotsk-culture|Okhotsk culture]]. Ainu also lived in southern [[e:sakhalin|Sakhalin]], the Kurils and northern [[e:honshu|Honshu]]. They called their land Ainu Mosir, the land of humans.
ainu-chiefdoms.r: There was no single state. Villages (kotan) led by elders formed regional groupings under powerful chiefs, who built hilltop forts called chashi. [[e:ainu|Ainu]] lived by hunting, fishing and trade, exchanging salmon, [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and hawks for Japanese [[e:rice|rice]], iron and lacquer and for Chinese [[e:silk|silks]] via the Amur. Religion centred on kamuy spirits, honoured in rites such as the bear-sending ceremony.
ainu-chiefdoms.e: An uprising against Japanese traders under [[e:koshamain|Koshamain]] in 1457 failed, and after the [[s:matsumae-domain|Matsumae Domain]] imposed a trade monopoly, so did [[e:shakushain|Shakushain's]] war of 1669. [[e:empire-of-japan|Meiji Japan]] annexed [[e:hokkaido|Hokkaido]] in 1869 and pursued assimilation. [[e:japan|Japan]] recognised the [[e:ainu|Ainu]] as an indigenous people in 2019.

ardalan.t: A Kurdish principality in western Iran that ruled for more than five centuries and made Sanandaj a centre of Kurdish literature.
ardalan.o: The Ardalan family traced its descent to a semi-legendary Baba Ardalan and emerged as rulers of the Kurdish lands around [[e:shahrizor|Sharazur]] and the [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]] by the 14th century. The principality lay on the frontier between the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] and the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]], and the Ardalans shifted between them before settling mostly under Iranian overlordship.
ardalan.r: The Ardalan walis ruled a [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] Kurdish population of farmers and tribes, sending troops and tribute to the shahs. [[e:soleyman-khan-ardalan|Soleyman Khan Ardalan]] founded [[e:sanandaj|Sanandaj]] (Sinneh) in the 1630s as his capital. The court patronised poetry in [[e:gorani-language|Gorani]], the literary Kurdish of the region, and in the 19th century [[e:mastoureh-ardalan|Mastoureh Ardalan]] wrote a history of the dynasty, one of the first by a Kurdish woman. [[e:amanullah-khan|Amanullah Khan]] built palaces and gardens in Sanandaj.
ardalan.e: [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]] steadily reduced Ardalan autonomy, and in 1867 [[e:naser-al-din-shah-qajar|Naser al-Din Shah]] replaced the last wali with a royal governor, ending the principality.

alash-autonomy.t: The Kazakh national government of the Alash party, which sought autonomy during the Russian Civil War and whose leaders were later killed in Stalin's purges.
alash-autonomy.o: The [[e:alash-party|Alash]] party was founded by [[e:kazakhs|Kazakh]] intellectuals including [[e:alikhan-bukeikhanov|Alikhan Bukeikhanov]], [[e:akhmet-baitursynov|Akhmet Baitursynov]] and [[e:mirzhakip-dulatov|Mirzhakip Dulatov]]. In December 1917 the [[e:second-all-kazakh-congress|Second All-Kazakh Congress]] in [[e:orenburg|Orenburg]] proclaimed the Alash Autonomy and formed a government, the Alash Orda.
alash-autonomy.r: [[e:alash-party|Alash]] Orda, led by [[e:alikhan-bukeikhanov|Bukeikhanov]], sought a [[e:kazakhs|Kazakh]] autonomy within a democratic Russian federation and governed from [[e:semey|Semey]] (Semipalatinsk) with an eastern branch, while a western wing operated in Zhympity. It tried to build a militia and promoted Kazakh education and a reformed Arabic script. It allied with the [[e:white-movement|Whites]] at times while negotiating with the Bolsheviks.
alash-autonomy.e: Disillusioned with the [[e:white-movement|Whites]], [[e:alash-party|Alash]] leaders accepted Soviet power in 1919 and 1920, when the government was dissolved and the [[e:kazakhs|Kazakh]] lands became the Kirghiz, later [[s:kazakh-assr|Kazakh ASSR]]. Most of its leaders were executed in the purges of the 1930s; they were rehabilitated in the late Soviet period.

ah-kin-chel.t: A Maya province of north-central Yucatán, ruled by the priestly Chel lineage and including the old pilgrimage centre of Izamal.
ah-kin-chel.o: According to [[e:diego-de-landa|Bishop Diego de Landa]], a priest of the Chel lineage at [[s:league-of-mayapan|Mayapan]] foresaw its fall and, after its destruction around 1441, founded a new realm. The province took his title, Ah Kin (priest) Chel, and its capital was at Tecoh.
ah-kin-chel.r: Ah Kin Chel covered a large area of north-central [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]] reaching the coast, with salt beds and fishing grounds. It included [[e:izamal|Izamal]], a pilgrimage centre of the god [[e:itzamna|Itzamna]] with massive ancient pyramids. Its ruler governed through the batabs of local towns, and the province maintained rivalries with [[s:sotuta|Sotuta]] and [[s:cupul|Cupul]].
ah-kin-chel.e: Ah Kin Chel submitted to the Spanish in the early 1540s and was absorbed into the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]]. The [[e:franciscans|Franciscans]] built a great convent on a pyramid at [[e:izamal|Izamal]] in the 1550s.

andros.t: Northernmost large island of the Cyclades, coloniser of the Chalcidice and remembered for defying Themistocles's demand for money in 480 BCE.
andros.o: Andros, just south-east of [[e:euboea|Euboea]], was settled by [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]] in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. The fortified Geometric town of [[e:zagora-andros|Zagora]] flourished in the 8th century BCE. Andros was long linked with [[s:eretria|Eretria]], and c. 655 BCE Andrians founded colonies in the [[e:chalcidice|Chalcidice]], including [[e:acanthus-greece|Acanthus]], [[e:stagira|Stagira]] and [[e:argilus|Argilus]].
andros.r: The island lived from farming, wine and seafaring. It sent ships to [[e:xerxes-i|Xerxes]] in 480 BCE; when [[e:themistocles|Themistocles]] demanded money, the Andrians replied that their gods were Poverty and Helplessness. Andros later paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]], and [[s:athens|Athens]] planted a colony there c. 450 BCE. The marble [[e:hermes-of-andros|Hermes of Andros]] shows its later prosperity.
andros.e: Under Hellenistic kings Andros changed hands often. [[e:rome|Rome]] captured it in 199 BCE and handed it to [[e:attalus-i|Attalus I]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-pergamon|Kingdom of Pergamon]], and it passed to direct Roman control after 133 BCE.

ajuran-sultanate.t: A Somali Muslim state that controlled the wells and rivers of southern Somalia and the Benadir coast, fighting off the Portuguese in the 16th century.
ajuran-sultanate.o: The Ajuran rose in the 13th century among [[e:somalis|Somali]] clans of the inter-riverine region between the [[e:shebelle-river|Shabelle]] and [[e:jubba-river|Jubba]] rivers. Under the Garen dynasty, which claimed a holy Arab lineage, it extended its authority over pastoral clans of the interior and coastal cities such as [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]], [[e:marka|Merca]] and [[s:barawa|Barawa]]. Most of its history comes from oral tradition, supported by coins and ruins.
ajuran-sultanate.r: The Ajuran is often called a hydraulic state: it controlled [[e:well|wells]] and river water and taxed their use, as well as levying tribute in grain, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and goods. A governing hierarchy of governors and military commanders ran the provinces. It joined the coastal trade in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], cloth and grain, and in the 1580s cooperated with the Ottoman corsair [[e:mir-ali-bey|Mir Ali Bey]] against the Portuguese.
ajuran-sultanate.e: Heavy taxation and the rule of a narrow elite provoked revolts in the late 17th century, and the sultanate broke up. The [[s:hiraab-imamate|Hiraab Imamate]] took over the [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] region and the [[s:sultanate-of-the-geledi|Sultanate of the Geledi]] much of the [[e:shebelle-river|Shabelle]] valley. [[e:well|Wells]], forts and tombs attributed to the Ajuran survive across southern [[s:somalia|Somalia]].

aenus.t: Aeolian city at the mouth of the Hebrus river in Thrace, a gateway for trade with the Thracian interior.
aenus.o: Aenus was founded by Aeolian settlers from [[s:mytilene|Mytilene]] and Cyme on a hill at the mouth of the [[e:maritsa|Hebrus]], the modern Maritsa or Evros, on the Thracian coast. [[e:homer|Homer]] mentions a Thracian named from Aenus, and the city flourished from the 6th century BCE.
aenus.r: Aenus traded salt fish and goods with the Thracian interior along the [[e:maritsa|Hebrus]], including the [[s:odrysian-kingdom|Odrysian Kingdom]]. It struck fine [[e:silver|silver]] coins with the head of [[e:hermes|Hermes]]. Aenus paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] and fought on the Athenian side at [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]] in 413 BCE.
aenus.e: In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] Aenus was held in turn by the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]] and the [[s:antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia|Antigonid Kingdom of Macedonia]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] declared it free in 167 BCE, and it came under Roman control by 146 BCE. It is today the Turkish town of Enez.

arcadian-league.t: Short-lived federation of the Arcadian cities created after Leuctra, which built Megalopolis and helped break Spartan power in the Peloponnese.
arcadian-league.o: [[e:sparta|Sparta's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-leuctra|Leuctra]] in 371 BCE freed the Arcadians to act together. Led by [[e:lycomedes-of-mantinea|Lycomedes of Mantinea]] and backed by [[s:thebes|Thebes]], they formed a federal state in 370 BCE, and [[s:mantinea|Mantinea]] was refounded. A new federal capital, [[s:megalopolis|Megalopolis]], was built by uniting dozens of villages in south-western [[e:arcadia|Arcadia]].
arcadian-league.r: The league had an assembly known as the [[e:ten-thousand|Ten Thousand]], a federal council and magistrates, and a standing elite force, the eparitoi, paid from federal funds. It joined [[s:thebes|Thebes]] in invading [[e:laconia|Laconia]] and supported the refounding of [[s:messene|Messene]]. Arcadian pride and a sense of common identity were expressed in federal coins and dedications.
arcadian-league.e: Quarrels with [[s:elis|Elis]] led the Arcadians to seize [[e:olympia|Olympia]], and disputes over using the sanctuary's treasure to pay the eparitoi split the league in 363 BCE, with [[s:mantinea|Mantinea]] siding with [[s:sparta|Sparta]] and [[s:tegea|Tegea]] with [[s:thebes|Thebes]]. The [[e:battle-of-mantinea-362-bce|Battle of Mantinea]] in 362 BCE left the federation broken, though [[s:megalopolis|Megalopolis]] endured.

ahmadili-dynasty.t: A line of Turkish atabegs that ruled Maragheh in Azerbaijan in the 12th century, rivals of the Eldiguzids for power in north-western Iran.
ahmadili-dynasty.o: [[e:ahmadil-ibn-ibrahim|Ahmadil ibn Ibrahim]], a Kurdish emir of the Rawwadid family, held [[e:maragha|Maragheh]] under the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] until he was killed by the [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizari Ismailis]] in 1116. His Turkish mamluk [[e:aq-sunqur-ahmadili|Aq Sunqur Ahmadili]] succeeded him around 1122 and founded a dynasty named after his former master.
ahmadili-dynasty.r: The Ahmadilis governed [[e:maragha|Maragheh]] and its region as atabegs, nominally guardians of Seljuk princes, and took part in the struggles of the [[s:seljuk-sultanate-of-iraq|Seljuk Sultanate of Iraq]]. Aq Sunqur and his son [[e:aq-sunqur-ii|Aq Sunqur II]] backed rival sultans against the [[s:eldiguzids|Eldiguzids]]. Maragheh flourished as a regional city with fine brick tomb towers, such as the [[e:gonbad-e-sorkh|Gonbad-e Sorkh]] of 1147.
ahmadili-dynasty.e: The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] sacked [[e:maragha|Maragheh]] in 1221, and around 1225 the [[e:khwarazmshah|Khwarazmshah]] [[e:jalal-al-din-mangburni|Jalal al-Din Mangburni]] took the city from the last representative of the dynasty, a woman ruler.

aequi.t: Mountain people east of Rome whose raids threatened Latium in the 5th century BCE, the enemies defeated by the legendary Cincinnatus.
aequi.o: The Aequi lived in the upper valleys of the [[e:aniene|Aniene]], Turano and Salto rivers in the [[e:apennines|Apennines]] east of [[e:latium|Latium]]. They were probably a Sabellic people, though their language is unknown. They appear in Roman history in the early 5th century BCE, pushing into the [[e:latin|Latin]] plain through the pass of [[e:mount-algidus|Mount Algidus]].
aequi.r: Known only from Roman sources, the Aequi lived in small fortified hill settlements and raided the farmland of [[e:latium|Latium]], often in alliance with the [[s:volsci|Volsci]]. Their most famous episode is [[e:cincinnatus|Cincinnatus's]] rescue of a trapped Roman army at [[e:mount-algidus|Mount Algidus]] in 458 BCE.
aequi.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] gradually drove them back. In 304 BCE, [[e:livy|Livy]] says, Rome captured 31 of their towns in 50 days and almost wiped out the people. Roman colonies were planted at [[e:alba-fucens|Alba Fucens]] in 303 BCE and Carseoli in 298 BCE, and surviving Aequian communities became Roman.

alupa-dynasty.t: The long-lived rulers of Tulu Nadu on the Karnataka coast, who survived for more than a thousand years as vassals of greater powers.
alupa-dynasty.o: The Alupas ruled the coastal strip of [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]] between the [[e:western-ghats|Western Ghats]] and the [[e:arabian-sea|Arabian Sea]]. Ptolemy may refer to their land as Olokhoira in the 2nd century, and they appear in inscriptions from the 7th century as feudatories of the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]]. Earlier they probably served the [[s:kadamba-dynasty|Kadamba dynasty]].
alupa-dynasty.r: Their capitals moved from Udyavara to [[e:mangalore|Mangalore]] and later [[e:barkur|Barkur]]. Alupa kings issued distinctive gold and [[e:copper|copper]] coins and ruled through local chiefs, profiting from the trade of the [[e:kanara|Kanara]] ports with [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and the [[e:persian-gulf|Persian Gulf]]. They acknowledged the supremacy in turn of the [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukyas]], the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]] and the [[s:hoysala-empire|Hoysala Empire]], and patronised [[e:shaivism|Shaiva]] and [[e:jainism|Jain]] temples. Their inscriptions are among the earliest in [[e:kannada|Kannada]].
alupa-dynasty.e: From the 14th century the Alupas came under the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]], and their line ends in the records around 1444, when [[e:tulu-nadu|Tulu Nadu]] was absorbed into Vijayanagara administration. The region kept its distinct Tulu language and culture.

apalachee-chiefdom.t: A maize-farming chiefdom of the Florida Panhandle that met de Soto, became the heart of Spain's mission system and was destroyed by English-led raids in 1704.
apalachee-chiefdom.o: The Apalachee emerged from the [[e:fort-walton-culture|Fort Walton culture]], the Mississippian tradition of the region between the [[e:aucilla-river|Aucilla]] and [[e:ochlockonee-river|Ochlockonee]] rivers around modern [[e:tallahassee|Tallahassee]], from around 1100. The [[e:lake-jackson-mounds|Lake Jackson]] mounds were an early centre. When [[e:panfilo-de-narvaez|Pánfilo de Narváez]] arrived in 1528 and [[e:hernando-de-soto|Hernando de Soto]] wintered at their capital, [[e:anhaica|Anhaica]], in 1539 to 1540, the Apalachee were populous and warlike.
apalachee-chiefdom.r: Chiefs ruled from towns with mounds and plazas, and the fertile red clay hills produced large [[e:maize|maize]] surpluses. The Apalachee were famous for a ball game with ritual meaning. Franciscan missions began in 1633, and many Apalachee became Catholic, sending maize and labour to [[e:st-augustine-florida|St Augustine]]. [[e:mission-san-luis-de-talimali|Mission San Luis de Talimali]], founded in 1656, became the capital of western [[s:spanish-florida|Spanish Florida]], housing Apalachee leaders alongside Spanish soldiers.
apalachee-chiefdom.e: In 1704 Carolina's former governor [[e:james-moore-carolina-governor|James Moore]] and [[e:muscogee|Muscogee]] allies destroyed most missions, killing or enslaving thousands. Survivors scattered to [[e:pensacola|Pensacola]], to Mobile in [[s:french-louisiana|French Louisiana]], or joined the Muscogee. Descendants survive in [[e:louisiana|Louisiana]] as the [[e:talimali-band-of-apalachee|Talimali Band of Apalachee]].

athmallik-state.t: A princely state on the Mahanadi in central Odisha, ruled from Kaintragarh until 1948.
athmallik-state.o: Tradition dates the ruling family to around 1500, but little is reliably known of its founding. The name refers to the eight mallis, or divisions, of its territory.
athmallik-state.r: Athmallik was a forested, thinly populated state on the south bank of the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]]. It was linked with the [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur]] group of chiefships under the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and passed under British supervision in the 19th century, joining the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary States]] in 1905. Its history is poorly recorded.
athmallik-state.e: Athmallik merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now in [[e:angul-district|Angul district]].

aghlabid-emirate.t: The Aghlabid emirs of Ifriqiya, who ruled Tunisia for the Abbasids, built Kairouan's Great Mosque and conquered Sicily.
aghlabid-emirate.o: In 800 the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:harun-al-rashid|Harun al-Rashid]] granted [[e:ibrahim-i-ibn-al-aghlab|Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab]], an Arab army commander, the governorship of [[e:ifriqiya|Ifriqiya]] as a hereditary office in return for annual tribute. The [[e:aghlabid-dynasty|Aghlabids]] ruled from [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] and their palace city al-Abbasiyya, and later [[e:raqqada|Raqqada]], as autonomous [[e:emir|emirs]] of the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]].
aghlabid-emirate.r: Relying on an Arab military elite and slave soldiers, they faced frequent army revolts. [[e:ziyadat-allah-i|Ziyadat Allah I]] launched the conquest of [[s:theme-of-sicily|Byzantine Sicily]] in 827, and [[e:aghlabid-dynasty|Aghlabid]] fleets raided [[e:italy|Italy]] and took [[e:malta|Malta]] in 870. They rebuilt the [[e:great-mosque-of-kairouan|Great Mosque of Kairouan]], built the [[e:ribat|ribat]] of [[e:sousse|Sousse]] and great water cisterns, and [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] became a centre of [[e:maliki-school|Maliki]] law under the jurist [[e:sahnun|Sahnun]].
aghlabid-emirate.e: In the 890s the [[e:kutama-berbers|Kutama Berbers]], mobilised by the [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] missionary [[e:abu-abdallah-al-shii|Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i]], rose against them. In 909 the last emir, [[e:ziyadat-allah-iii|Ziyadat Allah III]], fled to the east, and the [[s:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimid Caliphate]] was proclaimed in [[e:ifriqiya|Ifriqiya]].

cr.a: The original uploader was Nanoxyde at French Wikipedia.

akyem-abuakwa.t: Akan kingdom of the eastern Gold Coast forest, rich in gold and later a stronghold of the cocoa economy, ruled by the Okyenhene from Kyebi.
akyem-abuakwa.o: The Akyem peoples moved into the forest of the Birim valley by the 16th century, and Akyem Abuakwa became the largest of their states. It lay across the routes from the coast to the interior, near rich gold deposits.
akyem-abuakwa.r: The Okyenhene ruled with divisional chiefs, queen mothers and the councils typical of [[e:akan|Akan]] states. Akyem Abuakwa mined gold and traded it to the coast. In 1730 it joined with [[s:kingdom-of-akyem-kotoku|Akyem Kotoku]] and the Ga to overthrow [[s:akwamu|Akwamu]]. It then fought the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] for decades, sometimes as its tributary and sometimes as a rebel.
akyem-abuakwa.e: Akyem Abuakwa allied with the British against [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] and came under British rule with the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]] in 1874. In the 20th century it became a heartland of cocoa farming, and the Okyenhene still reigns at [[e:kyebi|Kyebi]].

ara-gaya.t: A major Gaya kingdom at Haman, known for its flame-pattern stoneware and as host of diplomatic conferences between Baekje, Silla and Japan.
ara-gaya.o: Ara Gaya, the Anra of Japanese sources, developed from Anya-guk, a [[s:byeonhan|Byeonhan]] statelet in the Haman basin southwest of the [[e:nakdong-river|Nakdong]]. According to Korean chronicles it was attacked in the early 3rd century by the eight port states of the coast and saved by [[s:silla|Silla]].
ara-gaya.r: After [[s:geumgwan-gaya|Geumgwan Gaya]] declined around 400, Ara Gaya became, with [[s:daegaya|Daegaya]], one of the two leading Gaya states. Hilltop tombs at Malisan hold armour, horse gear and distinctive stoneware with flame-shaped openings. In the 6th century it convened talks with envoys of [[s:baekje|Baekje]], [[s:silla|Silla]] and [[s:yamato|Yamato]] as the Gaya states tried to survive between their neighbours.
ara-gaya.e: Caught between [[s:baekje|Baekje]] and [[s:silla|Silla]], Ara Gaya was taken by Silla around 560, shortly before the fall of [[s:daegaya|Daegaya]], and became a Silla county.

alipura-state.t: A small Parihar Rajput state of the Bundelkhand Agency in central India.
alipura-state.o: Alipura became a separate chiefship in the mid-18th century under a [[e:parihar|Parihar]] [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family, during the break-up of [[e:bundela|Bundela]] power in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]]. It was confirmed by a British sanad in the early 19th century.
alipura-state.r: Its ruler governed a small rural territory as a non-salute state. Little else is recorded about its internal history.
alipura-state.e: After independence Alipura was merged with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]], and its lands were absorbed into the Indian administration by 1950; the town is in [[s:chhatarpur-state|Chhatarpur]] district of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]].

albanian-kingdom-1939-1943.t: Albania under Italian occupation, joined to Italy in a personal union under King Victor Emmanuel III and used as a base for the invasion of Greece.
albanian-kingdom-1939-1943.o: [[e:italy|Italy]] invaded [[s:albania|Albania]] on 7 April 1939, forcing [[e:zog-i|King Zog]] of the [[s:albanian-kingdom|Albanian Kingdom]] into exile. A constituent assembly summoned in [[e:tirana|Tirana]] offered the crown to [[e:victor-emmanuel-iii|Victor Emmanuel III]], creating a personal union with Italy. [[e:shefqet-verlaci|Shefqet Vërlaci]], a large landowner and rival of Zog, became prime minister under an Italian lieutenant-general, [[e:francesco-jacomoni|Francesco Jacomoni]].
albanian-kingdom-1939-1943.r: Real power lay with Italian officials: Albania's army and foreign service were merged into [[e:italy|Italy's]] and an [[e:albanian-fascist-party|Albanian Fascist Party]] was created. Italy launched its [[e:second-persian-invasion-of-greece|invasion of Greece]] from Albanian soil in October 1940, and after the conquest of [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]] in 1941 [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] and western Macedonia were added, forming a Greater [[s:albania|Albania]]. Resistance grew, including [[e:enver-hoxha|Enver Hoxha's]] [[e:party-of-labour-of-albania|Communist Party]], founded in 1941.
albanian-kingdom-1939-1943.e: When [[e:italy|Italy]] capitulated in September 1943, German troops occupied [[s:albania|Albania]] and created the [[s:albanian-kingdom|Albanian Kingdom]] (1943-1944), a nominally independent state under German control. [[e:victor-emmanuel-iii|Victor Emmanuel III]] formally renounced the Albanian crown in 1943, and the union with Italy was never restored.
albanian-kingdom-1939-1943.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

cr.a: F l a n k e r

arevaci.t: The strongest of the Celtiberian peoples, defenders of Numantia, whose siege by Scipio Aemilianus in 134 to 133 BCE became a byword for resistance.
arevaci.o: The Arevaci occupied the upper [[e:douro|Douro]] basin in modern [[e:soria|Soria]] and [[e:segovia|Segovia]] from about the 4th century BCE. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] called them the most powerful of the [[s:celtiberians|Celtiberians]], and their towns included [[e:numantia|Numantia]], [[e:tiermes|Termes]] and [[e:uxama-argaela|Uxama]].
arevaci.r: They lived in large fortified towns with grid-like streets, governed by councils and elected war leaders. [[e:numantia|Numantia's]] pottery shows painted horses and warriors. Herding, cereal growing and iron working sustained them, and their warriors were renowned in Roman sources for courage and skill with the sword.
arevaci.e: From 153 BCE they led resistance to [[e:rome|Rome]], defeating several consuls. In 134 BCE [[e:scipio-aemilianus|Scipio Aemilianus]] surrounded [[e:numantia|Numantia]] with walls and starved it; [[e:retogenes|Retogenes]] broke out to seek aid, but the town fell in 133 BCE. The Arevaci later backed [[e:quintus-sertorius|Sertorius]] before becoming part of [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]].

alirajpur-state.t: A Rathore Rajput state in the Bhil hills of western Madhya Pradesh, birthplace of the revolutionary Chandra Shekhar Azad.
alirajpur-state.o: The ruling [[e:rathore|Rathore]] family established itself in the hills south of the [[e:malwa|Malwa]] plateau; tradition dates the state to 1437. Its early history is poorly recorded.
alirajpur-state.r: Alirajpur was a hilly, forested state whose people were mostly [[e:bhils|Bhils]] and [[e:bhilala|Bhilalas]], known for the [[e:bhagoria|Bhagoria]] spring festival. It paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and later came under the [[e:bhopawar-agency|Bhopawar Agency]] of British central [[e:india|India]]. [[e:chandra-shekhar-azad|Chandra Shekhar Azad]] was born in the state's village of Bhabhra in 1906.
alirajpur-state.e: Alirajpur merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948, which became part of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. It is now a district of Madhya Pradesh.

arakkal-kingdom.t: The only Muslim royal house of Kerala, the Ali Rajas of Cannanore, who ruled a coastal principality and the Lakshadweep islands.
arakkal-kingdom.o: The Arakkal family were [[e:mappila|Mappila]] Muslim ministers and admirals of the Kolathiri rulers of [[s:kolathunadu|Kolathunadu]], based at [[e:kannur|Cannanore]]. By the 16th century, as the Portuguese disrupted the coast, they became an autonomous power, holding the title Ali Raja, lord of the sea, and ruling the town and the [[e:lakshadweep|Lakshadweep]] islands.
arakkal-kingdom.r: The Arakkal rulers followed matrilineal succession, so that the eldest member of the family, male or female, reigned; several women ruled with the title Arakkal Beevi. Their wealth came from trade in [[e:pepper|pepper]], coir and [[e:cowrie-shell|cowries]] and from the islands. They opposed the Portuguese and later allied with [[e:hyder-ali|Hyder Ali]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799|Kingdom of Mysore]].
arakkal-kingdom.e: The British [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] captured [[e:kannur|Cannanore]] in 1790, and the kingdom is conventionally dated to end in 1819. The family kept its [[e:lakshadweep|Laccadive]] islands until the British sequestrated them in 1875; they were formally surrendered for a pension in 1908. The Arakkal family survives in Kannur and maintains a museum in its old palace.

appenzell-innerrhoden.t: The Catholic half of Appenzell, created by the canton's division in 1597, which still governs itself by an open-air assembly.
appenzell-innerrhoden.o: In 1597 the [[s:canton-of-appenzell|Canton of Appenzell]], divided by the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], was split in two with the mediation of the other Swiss cantons. The Catholic inner districts around the village of Appenzell formed Innerrhoden, keeping the old seat and archives.
appenzell-innerrhoden.r: Innerrhoden governed itself through its [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]], meeting in the square at [[s:canton-of-appenzell|Appenzell]], which elected the [[e:landammann|Landammann]] and passed laws. It shared a single vote in the federal [[e:tagsatzung|Diet]] with Ausserrhoden. The economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and dairy farming and later on embroidery done at home. [[e:capuchins|Capuchin]] friars strengthened the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]].
appenzell-innerrhoden.e: The French invasion of 1798 merged [[s:canton-of-appenzell|Appenzell]] into the canton of [[e:canton-of-santis|Säntis]] of the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. Restored in 1803, Innerrhoden still holds its [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]]; it was the last canton to give women the vote, in 1990, after a federal court ruling.

aland.t: Demilitarised, Swedish-speaking island autonomy within Finland, created by a League of Nations decision in 1921 and still self-governing today.
aland.o: The Åland Islands, between [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]], passed to [[e:russia|Russia]] with [[e:finland|Finland]] in 1809 and were demilitarised after the [[e:crimean-war|Crimean War]] in 1856. When Finland became independent, most Ålanders, who speak Swedish, wanted to join Sweden. The [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] ruled in 1921 that the islands belonged to Finland, but with guaranteed autonomy and protection of the Swedish language.
aland.r: Åland governs itself through its own parliament, the [[e:parliament-of-aland|Lagting]], first convened in 1922 under [[e:julius-sundblom|Julius Sundblom]], and a government in [[e:mariehamn|Mariehamn]], with powers over education, culture, policing and local economy. Swedish is the only official language, and the right of domicile restricts land ownership to residents. The islands remain demilitarised and neutral, and their economy rests on shipping, ferries and tourism.
aland.e: Autonomy has been widened by later acts, and Åland gained its own flag in 1954 and its own stamps in 1984. When [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]] joined the EU in 1995, Åland kept a special status outside the EU tax area. It remains an autonomous region of the Republic of [[e:finland|Finland]].

ahhiyawa.t: A Late Bronze Age power named in some thirty Hittite texts, widely identified with the Mycenaean Greeks, the Achaeans of Homer.
ahhiyawa.o: The name Ahhiyawa, close to [[e:homer|Homer's]] [[e:achaeans-homer|Achaeans]], appears in Hittite records from c. 1400 BCE, when a 'man of Ahhiya' named [[e:attarissiya|Attarissiya]] raided western [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] and [[s:kingdom-of-alashiya|Alashiya]]. Most scholars now accept that it denotes a Mycenaean Greek kingdom, or a coalition of them, though its centre is debated, with [[s:kingdom-of-mycenae|Mycenae]], [[s:thebes|Thebes]] and [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] all proposed.
ahhiyawa.r: In the 13th century BCE a Hittite king addressed the king of Ahhiyawa as a '[[e:great-king|Great King]]' and 'brother', ranking him with [[e:egypt|Egypt]], [[e:babylon|Babylon]] and [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]]. Ahhiyawa held [[s:millawanda|Millawanda]] on the Anatolian coast and backed rebels such as [[e:piyamaradu|Piyamaradu]]. Hittite texts mention ships from Ahhiyawa and a dispute over [[s:wilusa|Wilusa]], often linked with [[e:troy|Troy]].
ahhiyawa.e: In a treaty of [[e:tudhaliya-iv|Tudhaliya IV]], c. 1230 BCE, the king of Ahhiyawa was struck from the list of great kings, suggesting its power had waned. References cease soon after, as the Mycenaean palaces collapsed c. 1200 BCE.

cr.a: Sosias (potter, signed). Painting attributed to the Sosias Painter (name piece for Beazley, overriding attribution) or the …

ayyubid-emirate-of-hama.t: The longest-surviving Ayyubid principality, which lasted under Mamluk overlordship and was ruled by the historian and geographer Abu al-Fida.
ayyubid-emirate-of-hama.o: In 1178 [[e:saladin|Saladin]] granted [[e:hama|Hama]] on the [[e:orontes-river|Orontes]] to his nephew [[e:taqi-al-din-umar|Taqi al-Din Umar]], whose descendants kept it as a hereditary principality within the Ayyubid family confederation.
ayyubid-emirate-of-hama.r: [[e:hama|Hama's]] rulers usually sided with the sultans in [[e:egypt|Egypt]] against their cousins in [[e:damascus|Damascus]] and [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]]. [[e:al-mansur-muhammad-ii-of-hama|Al-Mansur Muhammad II]] joined the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] against the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1260 and was allowed to keep his throne as a [[e:vassal|vassal]]. The principality was known for its learned princes: [[e:abu-al-fida|Abu al-Fida]], appointed ruler in 1310 by the Mamluk sultan [[e:al-nasir-muhammad|al-Nasir Muhammad]], wrote a universal history and the geographical work [[e:taqwim-al-buldan|Taqwim al-Buldan]]. The great waterwheels of the [[e:orontes-river|Orontes]] irrigated its gardens.
ayyubid-emirate-of-hama.e: After [[e:abu-al-fida|Abu al-Fida's]] death in 1331, his son [[e:al-afdal|al-Afdal]] Muhammad was deposed in 1341, and [[e:hama|Hama]] became an ordinary [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] province.

arjunayanas.t: A small republic of north-eastern Rajasthan, known from its coins, which claimed descent from the epic hero Arjuna.
arjunayanas.o: The Arjunayanas are known mainly from coins and from one inscription. They took their name from [[e:arjuna|Arjuna]], the [[e:pandavas|Pandava]] hero of the [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]], and appear to have emerged as an independent gana in the [[s:bharatpur-state|Bharatpur]] and [[s:alwar-state|Alwar]] region after the fall of the [[s:maurya-empire|Maurya Empire]].
arjunayanas.r: Their [[e:copper|copper]] coins, dated to around the 1st century BCE, bear the legend Arjunayananam jayah, victory of the Arjunayanas, which shows they were governed as a republic rather than by a king. Nothing more is known of their society.
arjunayanas.e: In the 4th century the Arjunayanas were among the peoples that submitted to [[e:samudragupta|Samudragupta]] of the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]], according to his [[e:prayagraj|Allahabad]] pillar inscription, after which they disappear from the record.

antigua-and-barbuda.t: Two-island Leeward state independent since 1981, long dominated by the Bird family and now reliant on tourism.
antigua-and-barbuda.o: The [[s:colony-of-antigua|Colony of Antigua]], with [[e:barbuda|Barbuda]] and [[e:redonda|Redonda]], became independent on 1 November 1981. [[e:vere-bird|Vere Bird]], the trade unionist who had led the [[e:antigua-labour-party|Antigua Labour Party]] since the 1940s, became the first prime minister, with the British monarch as head of state. Barbudans had sought separate status and remained uneasy partners.
antigua-and-barbuda.r: The [[e:antigua-labour-party|Antigua Labour Party]] under [[e:vere-bird|Vere Bird]] and then his son [[e:lester-bird|Lester Bird]] governed until 2004, amid scandals including the shipment of Israeli arms through [[s:colony-of-antigua|Antigua]] to the [[e:medellin-cartel|Medellín cartel]] in 1989 to 1990. Tourism, with beaches and the restored [[e:nelsons-dockyard|Nelson's Dockyard]], replaced [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], and the country also developed offshore finance and online gambling. The collapse of [[e:allen-stanford|Allen Stanford's]] banking empire in 2009 was a severe blow.
antigua-and-barbuda.e: [[e:baldwin-spencer|Baldwin Spencer's]] [[e:united-progressive-party-antigua-and-barbuda|United Progressive Party]] ruled from 2004 to 2014, and [[e:gaston-browne|Gaston Browne]] has led governments since 2014. [[e:hurricane-irma|Hurricane Irma]] forced the evacuation of [[e:barbuda|Barbuda]] in 2017, and disputes over communal land on Barbuda have continued.

cr.a: Original: Sir Reginald Samuel Vector: David Benbennick

archbishopric-of-magdeburg.t: Otto the Great's favoured archbishopric on the Elbe, head of the church in the Slavic east, which became a Protestant territory and then part of Brandenburg-Prussia.
archbishopric-of-magdeburg.o: Otto I founded a monastery at [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] in 937 and, after years of negotiation with the Pope and the Archbishop of [[e:mainz|Mainz]], raised it to an archbishopric in 968, with suffragans at [[e:merseburg|Merseburg]], [[e:meissen|Meissen]], [[e:zeitz|Zeitz]] (later [[e:naumburg|Naumburg]]), [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and [[e:havelberg|Havelberg]]. Otto and his first wife, [[e:eadgyth|Edith of England]], are buried in the cathedral.
archbishopric-of-magdeburg.r: The archbishops ruled a territory along the middle [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and [[e:saale|Saale]]. Archbishop [[e:wichmann-von-seeburg|Wichmann]] granted [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] its town law around 1188, a model copied across central and eastern [[e:europe|Europe]]. The Gothic cathedral, begun in 1209, was the first in [[e:germany|Germany]]. [[e:albert-of-brandenburg|Albert of Brandenburg's]] sale of indulgences as archbishop prompted [[e:martin-luther|Luther]]'s theses in 1517.
archbishopric-of-magdeburg.e: [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] became Lutheran, ruled by Protestant administrators, and the city was sacked by imperial troops in 1631. The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] assigned the archbishopric to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] on the death of its administrator, which happened in 1680, when it became the [[s:duchy-of-magdeburg|Duchy of Magdeburg]] within [[e:brandenburg-prussia|Brandenburg-Prussia]].

abdera-800.t: A Phoenician trading port on the coast of Almería, at modern Adra, that later minted coins under Carthaginian and Roman rule.
abdera-800.o: Phoenician settlers founded [[s:abdera|Abdera]] in the 8th century BCE on the hill of Montecristo at modern Adra, at the mouth of the river Adra. It was one of a chain of Phoenician harbours along the southern coast of [[e:iberia|Iberia]], with [[s:sexi|Sexi]] and [[s:malaka|Malaka]], linking [[s:gadir|Gadir]] with the eastern [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
abdera-800.r: Little is known of its government. Like its neighbours, [[s:abdera|Abdera]] lived from trade with the Iberian hinterland, fishing and the salting of fish. In the Punic period it fell under the influence of [[e:carthage|Carthage]], and its later coins, inscribed in Punic letters, showed a temple facade with tuna fish.
abdera-800.e: After the Roman victory over [[e:carthage|Carthage]] in [[e:hispania|Hispania]] in 206 BCE [[s:abdera|Abdera]] came under [[e:rome|Rome]], keeping its coinage into the early empire. It continued as a small Roman town, and [[e:strabo|Strabo]] listed it among the Phoenician foundations of the coast.

argos.t: Ancient city of the Argolid, Sparta's enduring rival in the Peloponnese, famed for the sanctuary of Hera and the sculptor Polykleitos.
argos.o: [[e:argo|Argos]] lies in the Argive plain below the [[s:larissa|Larisa]] and Aspis hills and was inhabited from the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]]. In the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] Dorian settlers made it the leading city of the [[e:argolid|Argolid]]. In the 7th century BCE King [[e:pheidon-of-argos|Pheidon]], credited with standard measures, made it the strongest power in the [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]], and Argos beat [[s:sparta|Sparta]] at Hysiai c. 669 BCE.
argos.r: [[e:argo|Argos]] controlled the great [[e:argive-heraion|Heraion]] between it and [[s:kingdom-of-mycenae|Mycenae]] and was a centre of bronze sculpture, home of [[e:ageladas|Hageladas]] and [[e:polykleitos|Polykleitos]]. Its power was broken when [[e:cleomenes-i|Cleomenes I]] of [[s:sparta|Sparta]] destroyed its army at [[e:battle-of-sepeia|Sepeia]] c. 494 BCE. Argos stayed neutral in 480 BCE, then destroyed Mycenae and [[s:kingdom-of-tiryns|Tiryns]] and adopted democracy.
argos.e: Allied with [[s:athens|Athens]], [[e:argo|Argos]] was defeated at [[s:mantinea|Mantinea]] in 418 BCE. [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-epirus|Kingdom of Epirus]] died fighting in its streets in 272 BCE. Argos joined the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]] in 229 BCE and passed under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE.

azerbaijan-democratic-republic.t: The first parliamentary republic in the Muslim world, founded in 1918, which granted women the vote before it fell to the Red Army in 1920.
azerbaijan-democratic-republic.o: As the [[s:transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic|Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic]] dissolved, the Azerbaijani National Council declared independence in [[e:tbilisi|Tiflis]] on 28 May 1918. Its government moved to [[s:ganja-khanate|Ganja]] and, with the help of the Ottoman Army of [[e:islam|Islam]], took [[e:baku|Baku]] from the [[s:centrocaspian-dictatorship|Centrocaspian Dictatorship]] in September 1918, making it the capital.
azerbaijan-democratic-republic.r: The republic was led by the [[e:musavat|Musavat]] party under [[e:mammad-amin-rasulzade|Mammad Amin Rasulzade]] and prime ministers such as [[e:fatali-khan-khoyski|Fatali Khan Khoyski]], with a multi-party parliament that included minority representatives. It granted women the vote in 1919, founded [[e:baku|Baku]] State University and adopted the blue, red and green flag. Baku's oil was its economic base, but it faced conflicts with [[s:armenia|Armenia]] over [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]] and [[e:zangezur|Zangezur]].
azerbaijan-democratic-republic.e: In April 1920 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] invaded, and the government ceded power to the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Bolsheviks]], creating the [[s:azerbaijan-ssr|Azerbaijan SSR]]. The independent [[s:azerbaijan|Republic of Azerbaijan]] in 1991 adopted its flag and declared itself its successor.

aduatuci.t: Belgic people said to descend from Cimbri and Teutones, whose entire population was sold into slavery by Caesar in 57 BCE.
aduatuci.o: Caesar says the Aduatuci descended from six thousand [[e:cimbri|Cimbri]] and [[e:teutones|Teutones]] left to guard the baggage of the great migration before 102 BCE, who settled on the middle [[e:meuse|Meuse]]. Their stronghold is usually placed near [[s:county-of-namur|Namur]] or [[e:thuin|Thuin]] in [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]].
aduatuci.r: They imposed tribute on their neighbours, including the [[s:eburones|Eburones]], and fortified a hilltop oppidum.
aduatuci.e: In 57 BCE they surrendered to Caesar but attacked his camp at night with hidden weapons. Caesar stormed the oppidum and sold the inhabitants, fifty-three thousand by his count, into [[e:slavery|slavery]]. Survivors joined [[e:ambiorix|Ambiorix]] in 54 BCE, after which the name disappears.

ahmadnagar-sultanate.t: The Nizam Shahi sultanate of the northern Deccan, remembered for Chand Bibi's defence of Ahmadnagar and Malik Ambar's resistance to the Mughals.
ahmadnagar-sultanate.o: [[e:ahmad-nizam-shah-i|Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah]], son of a Bahmani minister, defeated a Bahmani army in 1490 and declared independence. In 1494 he founded the city of [[e:ahmadnagar|Ahmadnagar]] as his capital, establishing the Nizam Shahi dynasty in the northern [[e:deccan|Deccan]].
ahmadnagar-sultanate.r: The Nizam Shahs annexed the [[s:berar-sultanate|Berar Sultanate]] in 1574 and took part in the victory over the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] at [[e:battle-of-talikota|Talikota]]. [[e:chand-bibi|Chand Bibi]], acting as regent, defended [[e:ahmadnagar|Ahmadnagar]] against Mughal attack in 1595. After the capital fell, the Ethiopian-born minister [[e:malik-ambar|Malik Ambar]] kept the state alive from [[e:aurangabad|Khadki]] (later Aurangabad), pioneering [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] warfare and a land revenue survey later adopted by the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]].
ahmadnagar-sultanate.e: [[e:ahmadnagar|Ahmadnagar]] fell to the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] in 1600, but resistance continued under [[e:malik-ambar|Malik Ambar]] and his son. [[e:shahaji-bhonsle|Shahaji Bhonsle]], a [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] general, propped up a puppet Nizam Shah until [[e:shah-jahan|Shah Jahan]] forced his surrender in 1636 and annexed the remaining territory.

ambiani.t: Belgic people of the Somme valley whose town Samarobriva, modern Amiens, hosted Caesar's council of Gaul in 54 BCE.
ambiani.o: The Ambiani held the lower and middle Somme in [[e:picardy|Picardy]]. Caesar records that they promised ten thousand warriors to the Belgic league of 57 BCE and surrendered after the league broke up.
ambiani.r: Their oppidum of [[e:amiens|Samarobriva]], the bridge on the [[e:somme-river|Samara]] or Somme, controlled a key crossing. They struck abundant gold coins, some of the earliest in northern [[e:gaul|Gaul]].
ambiani.e: Caesar held an assembly of the Gallic peoples at [[e:amiens|Samarobriva]] in 54 BCE and wintered there. The Ambiani sent men to relieve [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]] in 52 BCE and fought again in 51 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] Samarobriva became a major city, later Ambianum, the origin of Amiens.

aedui.t: Leading people of central Gaul and Rome's oldest Gallic ally, whose quarrels with their rivals gave Caesar his pretext to invade Gaul.
aedui.o: The Aedui held the land between the [[e:loire|Loire]] and the [[e:saone|Saône]], in modern [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]], with their great oppidum at [[e:bibracte|Bibracte]] on Mont Beuvray. By the 2nd century BCE they were hailed by the [[s:commune-of-rome|Roman Senate]] as brothers and kinsmen of the Roman people, and they contested leadership of [[e:gaul|Gaul]] with the [[s:arverni|Arverni]] and the [[s:sequani|Sequani]].
aedui.r: Government was oligarchic: a council of nobles and an annual chief magistrate, the vergobret, who could not leave the territory during office. [[e:bibracte|Bibracte]] was a large town of craftsmen, enamellers and traders importing Italian wine. The druid [[e:diviciacus-aedui|Diviciacus]], who had pleaded the Aeduan cause before the [[s:commune-of-rome|Roman Senate]], led the pro-Roman party, while his brother [[e:dumnorix|Dumnorix]] led the anti-Roman party.
aedui.e: Pressed by the [[s:sequani|Sequani]] and [[e:ariovistus|Ariovistus]], the Aedui called on Caesar in 58 BCE, but in 52 BCE they joined [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]], who was chosen supreme leader at [[e:bibracte|Bibracte]]. Pardoned after [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]], they moved to the new city of [[e:autun|Augustodunum]] (Autun), and in 48 CE [[e:claudius|Claudius]] admitted Aeduan nobles to the [[s:commune-of-rome|Roman Senate]].

atrebates.t: Belgic people of Artois whose king Commius served Caesar, then turned against him and founded a dynasty in Britain.
atrebates.o: The [[s:atrebates-britain|Atrebates]] lived in the modern [[s:county-of-artois|Artois]] around [[e:arras|Nemetocenna]] (Arras). They joined the Belgic league in 57 BCE, promising fifteen thousand men, and fought beside the [[s:nervii|Nervii]] at the [[e:battle-of-the-sabis|Sabis]].
atrebates.r: After their defeat Caesar made [[e:commius|Commius]] their king and used him as an envoy to the [[e:britons-celtic-people|Britons]] in 55 BCE, extending his authority over the [[s:morini|Morini]]. Their coins and their links across the [[e:english-channel|Channel]] show close ties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], where a people of the same name lived.
atrebates.e: [[e:commius|Commius]] joined the great revolt of 52 BCE, helped lead the relief army at [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]] and later fled to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], where coins name his successors among the British [[s:atrebates-britain|Atrebates]]. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:arras|Nemetocenna]] became a civitas capital, the origin of Arras, and the name survives in [[s:county-of-artois|Artois]].

acragas.t: Greek city of south-west Sicily, famed for its temples and wealth, home of the philosopher Empedocles, which Pindar called the most beautiful city of mortals.
acragas.o: Colonists from [[s:gela|Gela]], with Rhodians, founded Acragas around 580 BCE on a ridge above the confluence of the Akragas and Hypsas rivers, near [[e:sicily|Sicily's]] south coast. Within a few decades it was one of the largest Greek cities.
acragas.r: The tyrant [[e:phalaris|Phalaris]], notorious for roasting enemies in a bronze bull, ruled around 570–554 BCE. Under [[e:theron-of-acragas|Theron]], who with [[e:gelon|Gelon]] defeated [[e:carthage|Carthage]] at [[s:himera|Himera]] in 480 BCE, Acragas grew rich on grain, olives and trade with Carthage. Prisoners built temples along the southern ridge, today's Valley of the Temples, including the [[e:temple-of-concordia-agrigento|Temple of Concord]] and the colossal [[e:temple-of-olympian-zeus-agrigento|Olympieion]]. The philosopher [[e:empedocles|Empedocles]] helped restore democracy there.
acragas.e: [[e:carthage|Carthage]] sacked Acragas in 406 BCE. Revived by [[e:timoleon|Timoleon]], it was taken by [[e:rome|Rome]] in 262 BCE, retaken by Carthage, and finally captured by Rome in 210 BCE, becoming Agrigentum. The modern city, [[e:agrigento|Agrigento]], overlooks the temples, a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

alawi-sheikhdom.t: One of the smallest states of the Aden Protectorate, a tribal sheikhdom near the Yemeni frontier.
alawi-sheikhdom.o: The Alawi sheikhdom was a small tribal territory in the hills north of [[e:aden|Aden]], near [[s:emirate-of-dhala|Dhala]], with its seat at Al Qasha. Like its neighbours, it gained independence in the 18th century as the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] withdrew from the south. Its early history is barely recorded.
alawi-sheikhdom.r: The sheikhs ruled a few thousand people by tribal custom. The territory entered British protection through treaties in the late 19th century and was part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Western Aden Protectorate]]. In the 1960s it joined the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]], the British-sponsored union of [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] states.
alawi-sheikhdom.e: After the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took power in 1967, the sheikhdom was abolished and absorbed into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

amarnagar-state.t: A minor chiefship of southern Kathiawar, one of the small estates under British supervision.
amarnagar-state.o: Amarnagar, earlier known as Thana Amarnagar, was a small estate in [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a local chiefly family from around 1700. Its founding is poorly documented.
amarnagar-state.r: The ruler held a few villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Standard references record little else of its history.
amarnagar-state.e: Amarnagar merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

adamawa-emirate.t: The largest emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate, stretching from the Benue into what is now Cameroon, and split by Britain and Germany in 1901.
adamawa-emirate.o: [[e:modibbo-adama|Modibbo Adama]], a [[e:fula|Fulani]] scholar, received a flag from [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]], traditionally in 1806 or 1809, to spread the [[e:jihad|jihad]] in Fombina, the southern lands. His followers conquered or absorbed many local chiefdoms on the upper [[e:benue-river|Benue]] and the [[e:cameroon|Cameroon]] highlands, and in 1841 Adama founded [[e:yola|Yola]] as the capital.
adamawa-emirate.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] was a loose federation of dozens of sub-emirates, or lamidates, such as [[s:lamidate-of-ngaoundere|Ngaoundere]], [[e:garoua|Garoua]] and [[e:banyo|Banyo]], each ruled by a [[e:fula|Fulani]] lamido who paid tribute to [[e:yola|Yola]], which in turn paid tribute to [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]]. [[e:slave-raiding|Slave raiding]] against non-Muslim peoples supplied tribute and labour, and the region was among the largest slave-holding societies in [[e:africa|Africa]]. Lawal, [[e:modibbo-adama|Adama]]'s son, ruled from 1847 to 1872.
adamawa-emirate.e: In 1901 British forces took [[e:yola|Yola]] and [[e:emir|Emir]] Zubeiru fled; the Anglo-German border gave most of the [[e:emirate|emirate]] to [[s:kamerun|Kamerun]]. The British part became Adamawa Province in [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Northern Nigeria]], and the Lamido of Adamawa still reigns at Yola.

antemoro-kingdom.t: A south-east Malagasy kingdom of Islamic-influenced clans whose scribes kept the sorabe, Malagasy texts written in Arabic script.
antemoro-kingdom.o: The [[e:antemoro|Antemoro]] formed around the Matitana river near [[e:vohipeno|Vohipeno]] in south-east [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]], where clans claiming descent from Muslim immigrants established a ruling aristocracy around 1500. Their traditions trace the founders to [[e:mecca|Mecca]], though the migrants probably came via the [[e:swahili|Swahili]] coast or the [[e:comoro-islands|Comoros]].
antemoro-kingdom.r: Power lay with the Anteony noble clans, while scribal and priestly clans, the Anakara, guarded the sorabe [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]] on astrology, medicine, history and divination. [[e:antemoro|Antemoro]] diviners (ombiasy) became sought after as advisers at other Malagasy courts, including the [[s:merina-kingdom|Merina Kingdom]]. Society was rigidly stratified, and the kingdom produced distinctive paper made from bark.
antemoro-kingdom.e: Internal revolts in the 17th century weakened the noble clans, and in the 19th century the region fell under the [[s:merina-kingdom|Merina Kingdom]]. French colonial rule followed in 1895–96. The [[e:antemoro|Antemoro]] remain one of [[e:madagascar|Madagascar's]] ethnic groups, still known for their sorabe and Antaimoro paper.
antemoro-kingdom.re: Traditional Malagasy religion with Islamic elements

audumbara.t: A people of the Punjab hills whose coins carry some of the earliest images of a Hindu temple.
audumbara.o: The Audumbaras are mentioned by the grammarian [[e:panini|Panini]] and later texts as a people of the north-west. Coins show that by the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE they formed a state in the region between the [[e:ravi|Ravi]] and the [[e:beas|Beas]], around modern [[e:pathankot|Pathankot]] and the [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] valley.
audumbara.r: Little is known beyond their coinage. Their coins, with legends in Brahmi and Kharoshthi, name rulers such as Dharaghosha, Shivadasa and Rudradasa, and some show a pillared shrine beside a trident, one of the earliest depictions of a temple in [[e:india|India]]. The emphasis on [[e:shiva|Shiva]] and the trident points to a strong [[e:shaivism|Shaiva]] cult, and the name comes from the udumbara fig tree.
audumbara.e: The Audumbaras appear to have lost their independence to the [[s:indo-scythians|Indo-Scythians]] or the [[s:kushan-empire|Kushan Empire]] in the 1st century, after which their coinage ends.

abuja-emirate.t: The refuge state of the Hausa rulers of Zazzau, who kept their independence from the Sokoto Caliphate and whose town gave its name to Nigeria's capital.
abuja-emirate.o: When [[e:fula|Fulani]] jihadists took [[e:zaria|Zaria]] in 1808, the [[e:hausa|Hausa]] ruler of the [[s:kingdom-of-zazzau|Kingdom of Zazzau]], [[e:muhammadu-makau|Muhammadu Makau]], fled south with his followers to Zuba. After his death his brother [[e:abu-ja|Abu Ja]], also called Jatau, founded a new walled town around 1828, which took his name, [[e:suleja|Abuja]], and became the capital of the exiled dynasty.
abuja-emirate.r: [[e:suleja|Abuja]] kept the titles and court ceremonial of old [[s:kingdom-of-zazzau|Zazzau]] and remained outside the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]], repelling attacks from the [[s:zaria-emirate|Zaria Emirate]] and other [[e:fula|Fulani]] forces. Its rulers were Muslims, but they governed a mixed population of [[e:hausa|Hausa]] and Gbagyi farmers. The town became known for crafts such as weaving, pottery and metalwork, and for trade along the routes to the [[e:niger-river|Niger]].
abuja-emirate.e: British forces brought [[e:suleja|Abuja]] under the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]] in 1902, and its emir kept his title. In 1976, when the new federal capital was given the name Abuja, the old town was renamed Suleja.

atabegs-of-yazd.t: A line of local rulers who governed the desert city of Yazd for nearly two centuries under the Seljuks, Khwarazmians and Mongols.
atabegs-of-yazd.o: [[e:yazd|Yazd]] had been held by the last members of the [[s:kakuyid-dynasty|Kakuyid dynasty]] as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]]. Around 1141 the Seljuk sultan appointed [[e:rukn-al-din-sam|Rukn al-Din Sam]], son of a Turkish officer named Langar, as atabeg to the [[e:kakuyids|Kakuyid]] heiresses, and his family took over the city, founding the dynasty sometimes called the [[s:sallarid-dynasty|Langarids]].
atabegs-of-yazd.r: The atabegs ruled a small oasis state around [[e:yazd|Yazd]] and [[e:abarkuh|Abarquh]], living from irrigated farming by [[e:qanat|qanats]], [[e:silk|silk]] weaving and caravan trade across the central desert. They built mosques, [[e:madrasa|madrasas]] and gardens in Yazd and paid tribute to whoever dominated [[e:iran|Iran]], including the [[s:khwarazmian-empire|Khwarazmian Empire]] and, from the 1250s, the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]].
