atabegs-of-yazd.e: In 1319 [[e:mubariz-al-din-muhammad|Mubariz al-Din Muhammad]], founder of the [[s:muzaffarid-dynasty|Muzaffarid dynasty]], defeated the last atabeg, [[e:haji-shah-of-yazd|Haji Shah]], and took [[e:yazd|Yazd]], which became the base of the Muzaffarids.

american-samoa.t: The eastern Samoan islands ceded to the United States from 1900, an unincorporated territory where Samoan custom and communal land endure.
american-samoa.o: The [[e:tripartite-convention-1899|Tripartite Convention of 1899]] ended the [[s:kingdom-of-samoa|Kingdom of Samoa]] and gave the islands east of longitude 171 west to the [[s:united-states|United States]], which prized the harbour of [[e:pago-pago|Pago Pago]] as a coaling station. Chiefs of [[e:tutuila|Tutuila]] and [[e:aunuu|Aunuʻu]] signed a deed of cession in 1900, and the rulers of the [[s:kingdom-of-manu-a|Kingdom of Manuʻa]] ceded their islands in 1904.
american-samoa.r: The [[e:united-states-navy|US Navy]] governed the territory until 1951 through naval commandants, leaving village affairs and land to the matai, the chiefs of extended families. A local [[e:mau-movement|Mau movement]] in the 1920s protested naval rule. Authority passed to the [[e:departement|Department]] of the Interior in 1951, and a constitution adopted in 1960 was revised in 1967. Tuna canning became the main industry.
american-samoa.e: American Samoans elected their first governor, [[e:peter-tali-coleman|Peter Tali Coleman]], in 1977. The territory remains unincorporated and unorganised; its people are US nationals rather than citizens, an arrangement many defend as protecting communal land and the faʻa [[e:samoan-islands|Samoa]] way of life.
american-samoa.re: Protestantism, Roman Catholicism, Latter-day Saint movement

abhira-dynasty.t: A Deccan dynasty that took over the Nashik region from the Satavahanas and founded the era later used by the Kalachuris.
abhira-dynasty.o: The [[e:abhira-people|Abhiras]] were a pastoral people of western [[e:india|India]], first serving as generals under the [[s:western-satraps|Western Satraps]]. As the [[s:satavahana-dynasty|Satavahana dynasty]] weakened in the early 3rd century, an Abhira chief, [[e:ishvarasena|Ishvarasena]], established a kingdom around [[e:nashik|Nashik]] in [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]]. An era beginning in 248 or 249, perhaps founded by him, was later known as the [[e:kalachuri-chedi-era|Kalachuri-Chedi era]].
abhira-dynasty.r: The dynasty is known mainly from a [[e:prakrit|Prakrit]] inscription of [[e:ishvarasena|Ishvarasena]] at the Buddhist caves of [[e:nashik|Nashik]], recording an endowment by a laywoman, and from coins. The [[e:puranas|Puranas]] say ten [[e:abhira-people|Abhira]] kings ruled. They seem to have controlled northern [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]] and parts of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and Konkan.
abhira-dynasty.e: The [[e:abhira-people|Abhira]] kingdom declined in the 4th century; the [[e:prayagraj|Allahabad]] pillar inscription lists the Abhiras among peoples who submitted to [[e:samudragupta|Samudragupta]] of the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]]. Their lands passed to the [[e:traikutaka-dynasty|Traikutakas]] and later to the [[s:kalachuris-of-mahishmati|Kalachuris of Mahishmati]].

ashanti-colony.t: The British colony created from the conquered Ashanti Empire after the War of the Golden Stool, which joined independent Ghana in 1957.
ashanti-colony.o: British forces occupied [[e:kumasi|Kumasi]] in 1896 and exiled the [[e:asantehene|Asantehene]] [[e:prempeh-i|Prempeh I]], eventually to the [[s:british-seychelles|Seychelles]]. In 1900 the governor's demand for the [[e:golden-stool|Golden Stool]], the sacred symbol of the [[e:ashanti-empire|Asante]] nation, provoked a rising led by [[e:yaa-asantewaa|Yaa Asantewaa]], queen mother of [[e:ejisu|Ejisu]]. After its suppression [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed Ashanti as a crown colony on 1 January 1902.
ashanti-colony.r: A chief commissioner at [[e:kumasi|Kumasi]] governed through [[e:ashanti-empire|Asante]] chiefs. The colony became the heart of [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast]] cocoa production, and Kumasi grew into a major commercial centre linked by rail to the coast. [[e:prempeh-i|Prempeh I]] was allowed to return in 1924, and in 1935 the British restored the Asante [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederacy]] under his successor [[e:prempeh-ii|Prempeh II]].
ashanti-colony.e: In the 1950s the [[e:national-liberation-movement-ghana|National Liberation Movement]], based in [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]], demanded a federal constitution, but on 6 March 1957 Ashanti became part of a unitary [[e:ghana|Ghana]]. The [[e:asantehene|Asantehene]] remains the most influential traditional ruler in the country.

agathyrsi.t: Gold-rich people of Transylvania described by Herodotus, known for tattoos, luxury and refusing to join the Scythians against Persia.
agathyrsi.o: [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] places the Agathyrsi along the [[e:mari|Maris]] ([[e:mures-river|Mureș]]) in [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] in the 6th century BCE. Their origins are debated: they may have been a Scythian-influenced elite over a Thracian population, and Greek myth made their founder Agathyrsus a son of [[e:heracles|Heracles]].
agathyrsi.r: [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] describes them as wearing much gold, tattooing themselves and holding wives in common so that all would be kin. Their king [[e:spargapeithes|Spargapeithes]] killed the Scythian king [[e:ariapeithes|Ariapeithes]]. When [[e:darius-i|Darius I]] invaded [[s:scythia|Scythia]] around 513 BCE, they refused Scythian refugees entry to their land. Scythian-style graves in [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] are often linked to them.
agathyrsi.e: After the 5th century BCE they vanish from the record; their lands later appear as part of the territory of the [[s:getae|Getae]] and [[e:dacians|Dacians]], into whom they were probably absorbed.

ava-kingdom.t: The dominant kingdom of Upper Burma for nearly two centuries, which fought the Mon of Hanthawaddy for forty years and shaped classical Burmese literature.
ava-kingdom.o: After Shan raiders sacked [[s:pinya-kingdom|Pinya]] and [[s:sagaing-kingdom|Sagaing]] in 1364, [[e:thado-minbya|Thado Minbya]] united the two courts and in 1365 founded a new capital at Ava, Inwa, at the confluence of the [[e:irrawaddy-river|Irrawaddy]] and [[e:myitnge-river|Myitnge]] rivers. He presented his kingdom as the successor of the [[s:pagan-kingdom|Pagan Kingdom]].
ava-kingdom.r: Ava controlled the [[e:kyaukse|Kyaukse]] and [[e:minbu|Minbu]] [[e:rice|rice]] lands and claimed authority over [[s:prome-kingdom|Prome]], Toungoo and the Shan borders. [[e:swa-saw-ke|Swa Saw Ke]] and his son [[e:minkhaung-i|Minkhaung I]] fought the [[e:forty-years-war|Forty Years' War]] against [[e:razadarit|Razadarit]] of the [[s:hanthawaddy-kingdom|Hanthawaddy Kingdom]] from 1385 to 1424. Monks and court poets such as [[e:shin-maha-thilawuntha|Shin Maha Thilawuntha]] and [[e:shin-maha-rahtathara|Shin Maha Rahtathara]] made Ava the golden age of Burmese classical literature.
ava-kingdom.e: Ava weakened as [[e:vassal|vassals]] broke away, including [[s:prome-kingdom|Prome]] and Toungoo. In 1527 a confederation of Shan states led by [[s:mohnyin|Mohnyin]] captured Ava, ruling it as the [[s:confederation-of-shan-states|Confederation of Shan States]]. In 1555 [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]] of the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] conquered it, and Ava later became the capital of the [[s:restored-toungoo-kingdom|Restored Toungoo Kingdom]].

akalkot-state.t: A Bhonsle Maratha state of the Deccan, founded by the adopted son of Chhatrapati Shahu, and home of the saint Swami Samarth.
akalkot-state.o: Akkalkot was granted in 1708 to [[e:fatehsinh-bhonsle|Fatehsinh Bhonsle]], born into the Lokhande family and adopted as a boy by the [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] king [[e:shahu-i|Shahu]]. His descendants ruled as Rajas under the [[e:satara|Satara]] [[e:chhatrapati|Chhatrapatis]].
akalkot-state.r: The Rajas governed a dry [[e:deccan|Deccan]] territory of [[e:millet|millet]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] near [[e:solapur|Solapur]]. After 1818 the state came under British protection, later the [[e:deccan-states-agency|Deccan States Agency]]. In the 19th century Akkalkot became famous as the home of the saint [[e:swami-samarth|Swami Samarth]], whose shrine draws pilgrims.
akalkot-state.e: Akkalkot merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]] in 1960, in [[e:solapur|Solapur]] district.

ayyubid-emirate-of-damascus.t: The Ayyubid principality of Damascus after Saladin, a prize fought over by his brothers, sons and grandsons until the Mongols arrived in 1260.
ayyubid-emirate-of-damascus.o: When [[e:saladin|Saladin]] died in [[e:damascus|Damascus]] in 1193, his empire was divided among his sons, and Damascus went to the eldest, [[e:al-afdal|al-Afdal]] Ali. In 1196 his uncle [[e:al-adil|al-Adil]] and brother [[e:al-aziz|al-Aziz]] drove him out, and Damascus passed to al-Adil's line.
ayyubid-emirate-of-damascus.r: [[e:damascus|Damascus]] was the richest prize in [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and the seat of a scholarly and religious elite. [[e:al-muazzam-isa|Al-Mu'azzam Isa]] (1218-1227), a [[e:hanafi-school|Hanafi]] jurist, built schools and dismantled the walls of [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in 1219 to keep them from the [[e:crusader-states|Crusaders]]. Later princes, [[e:al-nasir-dawud|al-Nasir Dawud]], al-[[e:al-ashraf-musa-sultan-of-damascus|Ashraf Musa]] and [[e:as-salih-ismail|al-Salih Ismail]], fought the sultans in [[e:egypt|Egypt]]; al-[[s:salihids|Salih]] Ismail even ceded castles to the [[s:franks|Franks]]. [[e:as-salih-ayyub|Al-Salih Ayyub]] took the city in 1245.
ayyubid-emirate-of-damascus.e: [[e:al-nasir-yusuf|Al-Nasir Yusuf]] of the [[s:ayyubid-emirate-of-aleppo|Ayyubid Emirate of Aleppo]] seized [[e:damascus|Damascus]] in 1250. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] occupied it in March 1260, and after their defeat at [[e:battle-of-ain-jalut|Ain Jalut]] it passed to the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]].

arretium.t: Northern Etruscan city, home of the bronze Chimera of Arezzo, which grew rich on farming and metalworking and became an early Roman ally.
arretium.o: Arretium, Etruscan Aritim, modern [[s:commune-of-arezzo|Arezzo]], lay where the [[e:val-di-chiana|Val di Chiana]] meets the upper [[e:arno|Arno]], controlling routes between [[e:etruria|Etruria]], [[e:umbria|Umbria]] and the Po valley. It developed into a city from the 6th century BCE, later than most Etruscan centres, and grew powerful in the 4th century BCE.
arretium.r: Arretium was known for agriculture and metalwork. The bronze [[e:chimera-of-arezzo|Chimera of Arezzo]], cast around 400 BCE and found in 1553, is a masterpiece of Etruscan art. The city was dominated by great families, among them the Cilnii, whom [[e:livy|Livy]] reports being driven out by a popular revolt in 302 BCE and restored with Roman help; the Augustan minister [[e:gaius-maecenas|Maecenas]] was descended from them.
arretium.e: Arretium made truces with [[e:rome|Rome]] in 310 and 294 BCE and became a loyal ally, supplying weapons and grain to [[e:scipio-africanus|Scipio]] in 205 BCE. Under Rome it became famous for Arretine ware, a red-glazed tableware exported across the empire. The town continued as [[s:commune-of-arezzo|Arezzo]], birthplace of [[e:petrarch|Petrarch]].

afrighid-khwarazm.t: The native dynasty of Khwarazm for nearly seven centuries, whose shahs kept the region's Iranian culture alive through Arab conquest and Samanid overlordship.
afrighid-khwarazm.o: According to the Khwarazmian scholar al-Biruni, the Afrighid dynasty was founded by Afrig in 305 CE, succeeding the older royal house of the [[s:kingdom-of-khwarazm|Kingdom of Khwarazm]]. Afrig built a fortress at Kath on the [[e:oxus|Amu Darya]], which became the capital.
afrighid-khwarazm.r: The shahs ruled an irrigated land of canals, towns and fortified manors that traded north with the steppe and the [[e:volga|Volga]]. [[e:zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]] and the Khwarazmian language and calendar persisted. After the Arab general [[e:qutayba-ibn-muslim|Qutayba ibn Muslim]] conquered [[e:khwarazm|Khwarazm]] in 712, the shahs remained as [[e:vassal|vassals]], converted to [[e:islam|Islam]] and ruled under Caliphal and later [[e:samanid-empire|Samanid]] authority, while a rival centre grew at [[e:gurganj|Gurganj]].
afrighid-khwarazm.e: In 995 the emir of [[e:gurganj|Gurganj]], [[e:mamun-ibn-muhammad|Ma'mun ibn Muhammad]], overthrew and killed the last Afrighid shah, [[e:abu-abdallah-muhammad-afrighid|Abu Abdallah Muhammad]], and founded [[s:mamunid-khwarazm|Ma'munid Khwarazm]]. [[e:al-biruni|Al-Biruni]], born near Kath, preserved much of what is known of the dynasty.

cr.a: Edited by HistoryofIran, originally work by Gabagool

aegina.t: Island state in the Saronic Gulf that minted some of the first Greek coins and was the great commercial rival of Athens until 431 BCE.
aegina.o: Aegina, an island between [[e:attica|Attica]] and the [[e:argolid|Argolid]], was settled from the [[e:neolithic|Neolithic]] and had a strong [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]] town at Kolonna. In the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] it was resettled by [[e:dorians|Dorians]] from [[s:epidaurus|Epidaurus]], and by the 7th century BCE it had become one of the busiest trading states of the Greek world.
aegina.r: Aegina struck [[e:silver|silver]] 'turtle' coins from c. 550 BCE, and its weight standard spread across much of [[e:greece|Greece]]. Its merchants traded at [[e:naucratis|Naucratis]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]], and its oligarchic elite built the temple of [[e:temple-of-aphaia|Aphaia]], whose pediment sculptures are now in [[e:munich|Munich]]. Aegina gave earth and water to [[e:persia|Persia]] in 491 BCE, but its ships won the prize for valour at [[e:battle-of-salamis|Salamis]] in 480 BCE.
aegina.e: Long wars with [[s:athens|Athens]] ended in 457 BCE, when Aegina was forced into the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. In 431 BCE [[e:athens|Athens]] expelled the Aeginetans and settled colonists; [[s:sparta|Sparta]] gave the exiles land at Thyrea. [[e:lysander|Lysander]] restored survivors in 405 BCE, but the island never regained its former power.

akwamu.t: Akan kingdom that dominated the eastern Gold Coast in the late 17th century, conquering the Ga and seizing a Danish castle.
akwamu.o: Akwamu was founded by [[e:akan|Akan]] migrants in the hills north of [[e:accra|Accra]], with its capital at Nyanaoase. By the mid-17th century it controlled trade routes from the forest to the coast, and under [[e:ansa-sasraku|Ansa Sasraku]] it conquered the [[s:ga-kingdom|Ga kingdom]] between 1677 and 1681, gaining access to the European forts at Accra.
akwamu.r: Akwamu's kings ruled a military empire stretching from [[e:accra|Accra]] to the [[e:volta-river|Volta]] and beyond, extracting tribute and slaves from conquered peoples. In 1693 an Akwamu trader, [[e:asameni|Asameni]], seized the Danish castle of [[e:osu-castle|Christiansborg]] and held it for a year. Akonno, king in the early 18th century, extended Akwamu power east across the Volta.
akwamu.e: In 1730 [[s:akyem-abuakwa|Akyem Abuakwa]], [[s:kingdom-of-akyem-kotoku|Akyem Kotoku]] and the Ga defeated Akwamu, which moved east across the [[e:volta-river|Volta]] to Akwamufie. It survived there as a smaller state under the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] and later the British.

abrincatui.t: Small Gallic people of the bay of Mont Saint-Michel, whose name survives in the town of Avranches.
abrincatui.o: Known only from [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny]], Ptolemy and later Roman records, the Abrincatui held the southern end of the Cotentin coast on the border of [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] and [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]]. They were neighbours of the [[s:unelli|Unelli]] and [[s:redones|Redones]] and were probably dependents of a larger Armorican people.
abrincatui.r: Nothing is recorded of their institutions. Ptolemy names their town Ingena, generally placed at [[e:avranches|Avranches]].
abrincatui.e: They were drawn into the Roman conquest of [[e:armorica|Armorica]] in 57 and 56 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] they formed a small civitas in [[e:gallia-lugdunensis|Gallia Lugdunensis]] whose chief town took the people's name as Abrincatae, the origin of [[e:avranches|Avranches]], later a bishopric.

abadzekhs.t: A self-governing Circassian people of the forested foothills of the western Caucasus, among the most determined opponents of the Russian conquest.
abadzekhs.o: The Abadzekhs inhabited the forested valleys of the upper [[e:belaya-river-kuban|Belaya]], [[e:pshish|Pshish]] and [[e:psekups|Psekups]] rivers, behind the coastal [[s:shapsugs|Shapsugs]]. They emerged as a distinct and numerous [[e:circassians|Adyghe]] community of [[s:circassia|Circassia]] by the 17th century; earlier history is not separately recorded. Their villages lay scattered in clearings across the forest.
abadzekhs.r: Like the [[s:shapsugs|Shapsugs]] and [[s:natukhaj|Natukhaj]], they shed the authority of princes in the late 18th century and governed through assemblies and customary law, with sworn associations of households. They lived by farming, herding and forest crafts. From 1848 [[e:muhammad-amin-naib-of-shamil|Muhammad Amin]], [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]]'s envoy, organised them into a more centralised Islamic administration with courts and taxes.
abadzekhs.e: The Abadzekhs submitted to [[e:russia|Russia]] in 1859 but soon resumed resistance. The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] completed the conquest in 1864, and the great majority were expelled to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]]. A few villages remained near [[e:maykop|Maykop]], in what is now [[e:adygea|Adygea]].

ashkelon.t: Ashkelon, the Philistine seaport of the southern Levant, whose Iron Age cemetery has revealed the Aegean origins of its settlers.
ashkelon.o: Ashkelon had been a large Canaanite harbour town since the [[e:middle-bronze-age|Middle Bronze Age]], and its kings wrote to [[e:egypt|Egypt]] in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]]. In the 12th century BCE [[s:philistine-pentapolis|Philistines]] settled there, and it became one of the cities of the Philistine Pentapolis.
ashkelon.r: Its kings ruled a busy port trading wine and oil, with a market in the city centre. Excavations led by [[e:lawrence-stager|Lawrence Stager]] uncovered a Philistine cemetery, and a 2019 DNA study found that its early inhabitants included newcomers of southern European ancestry. King [[e:sidqa|Sidqa]] rebelled against [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib]] in 701 BCE and was deported.
ashkelon.e: Ashkelon remained an Assyrian [[e:vassal|vassal]] until [[e:nebuchadnezzar-ii|Nebuchadnezzar II]] of the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]] destroyed it in 604 BCE and deported its king Aga to [[e:babylon|Babylon]]. The city later revived as a Phoenician and Greek port.

armenia.t: The independent Republic of Armenia, a landlocked state in the South Caucasus with a global diaspora and the world's oldest national church.
armenia.o: Following the [[e:karabakh-movement|Karabakh movement]] and the 1988 [[e:1988-armenian-earthquake|Spitak earthquake]], the [[s:armenian-ssr|Armenian SSR]] voted for independence in a referendum on 21 September 1991 and became sovereign when the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] dissolved. It took the flag and anthem of the [[s:first-republic-of-armenia|First Republic of Armenia]], and [[e:levon-ter-petrosyan|Levon Ter-Petrosyan]] became its first president.
armenia.r: Armenia emerged from the [[e:first-nagorno-karabakh-war|First Karabakh War]] in 1994 with Armenian forces controlling [[e:nagorno-karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh]], but under [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]] by [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] and [[e:turkey|Turkey]] and in an energy crisis. Presidents [[e:robert-kocharyan|Robert Kocharyan]] and [[e:serzh-sargsyan|Serzh Sargsyan]] led a system closely tied to [[e:russia|Russia]]. In 2018, as a new constitution made Armenia a parliamentary republic, peaceful protests, the [[e:2018-armenian-revolution|Velvet Revolution]], brought [[e:nikol-pashinyan|Nikol Pashinyan]] to power.
armenia.e: Defeat in the 2020 war and [[e:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan's]] 2023 takeover of [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]] brought over 100,000 refugees and a cooling of relations with [[e:russia|Russia]]. Armenia has since pursued a peace settlement with [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] and closer ties with the West.

armenian-principality-of-cilicia.t: A mountain principality founded by Armenian refugees and nobles in the Taurus, which grew into the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia and allied with the Crusaders.
armenian-principality-of-cilicia.o: After the Byzantine defeat at [[e:battle-of-manzikert|Manzikert]] in 1071 and the loss of Armenian lands to the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]], Armenian lords established themselves in the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] mountains of [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]]. Around 1080 [[e:ruben-i-prince-of-armenia|Ruben]], a follower of the last [[e:bagratuni-dynasty|Bagratid]] king, created a lordship that became the base of the [[e:rubenid-dynasty|Rubenid dynasty]].
armenian-principality-of-cilicia.r: Lords ruled from fortresses such as [[e:vahka|Vahka]] and later the plain cities of [[e:sis-cilicia|Sis]] and [[e:anazarbus|Anazarbus]]. [[e:thoros-i-prince-of-armenia|Thoros I]] took the Cilician plain from [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], and the [[e:rubenid-dynasty|Rubenids]] cooperated with the [[e:crusader-states|Crusader states]] of [[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]] and [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]]. Its ports gave it a role in [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] trade, while monasteries such as Drazark preserved Armenian learning.
armenian-principality-of-cilicia.e: [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] temporarily regained [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]] and imprisoned Leo I in 1137, but [[e:thoros-ii-prince-of-armenia|Thoros II]] restored the principality. In 1198 [[e:leo-i-king-of-armenia|Leo II]] was crowned king with the blessing of the [[e:holy-roman-emperor|Holy Roman Emperor]] and the pope, transforming it into a kingdom.

arverni.t: Leading people of central Gaul, rulers of the Auvergne, whose noble Vercingetorix united Gaul against Caesar in 52 BCE.
arverni.o: The Arverni held the volcanic uplands and the fertile [[e:limagne|Limagne]] plain of the [[s:county-of-auvergne|Auvergne]]. By the 2nd century BCE they dominated much of southern and central [[e:gaul|Gaul]]. Their king [[e:luernios|Luernios]] was remembered by Greek writers for scattering gold and [[e:silver|silver]] to his followers, and his son [[e:bituitus|Bituitus]] led a vast army against [[e:rome|Rome]].
arverni.r: Their power rested on a network of client peoples, such as the [[s:gabali|Gabali]], [[s:vellavi|Vellavi]] and [[s:cadurci|Cadurci]], and on great oppida like [[e:corent|Corent]] and [[e:gergovia|Gergovia]], which imported Italian wine on a huge scale. After the defeat of [[e:bituitus|Bituitus]] kingship was abolished, and [[e:celtillus|Celtillus]], father of [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]], was put to death for seeking to restore it.
arverni.e: [[e:bituitus|Bituitus]] was defeated by the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]] in 121 BCE. In 52 BCE [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]] raised [[e:gaul|Gaul]] in revolt and repulsed Caesar at [[e:gergovia|Gergovia]], but surrendered at [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]] and was later executed in [[e:rome|Rome]]. The Arverni were treated leniently, and their Roman capital [[e:clermont-ferrand|Augustonemetum]] grew into Clermont-Ferrand.

ayyubid-emirate-of-kerak.t: An Ayyubid principality based on the Crusader castle of Kerak, which held out until 1263, after most of Ayyubid Syria had fallen.
ayyubid-emirate-of-kerak.o: [[e:al-nasir-dawud|Al-Nasir Dawud]], son of [[e:al-muazzam-isa|al-Mu'azzam Isa]] of [[e:damascus|Damascus]], lost Damascus to his uncles in 1229 but kept [[e:al-karak|Kerak]] and the lands east of the [[e:dead-sea|Dead Sea]], which became a separate principality.
ayyubid-emirate-of-kerak.r: [[e:al-nasir-dawud|Al-Nasir Dawud]] was a poet and scholar who used [[e:al-karak|Kerak]] as a base for intrigue, briefly occupying [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in 1239 and holding, then releasing and backing, the future sultan [[e:as-salih-ayyub|al-Salih Ayyub]]. The principality controlled the routes from [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] to [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and the [[e:hejaz|Hijaz]], and the near-impregnable castle made it a refuge. From 1250 [[e:al-mughith-umar|al-Mughith Umar]] ruled Kerak, harbouring [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] dissidents and challenging the new regime in Egypt.
ayyubid-emirate-of-kerak.e: In 1263 the [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] sultan [[e:baybars|Baybars]] lured [[e:al-mughith-umar|al-Mughith Umar]] out of [[e:al-karak|Kerak]], arrested and executed him, and annexed the principality.

ambracia.t: Corinthian colony in north-west Greece that became the capital of King Pyrrhus and was besieged and plundered by Rome in 189 BCE.
ambracia.o: Ambracia was founded c. 625 BCE by Corinthians under Gorgus, a son of the tyrant [[e:cypselus|Cypselus]], on the [[e:arachthos|Arachthos]] river north of the [[e:ambracian-gulf|Ambracian Gulf]]. It controlled fertile land and routes into [[e:epirus|Epirus]], and Cypselid relatives ruled it as tyrants until the early 6th century BCE.
ambracia.r: Ambracia was a loyal ally of [[s:corinth|Corinth]] and [[s:sparta|Sparta]]. In the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]] it fought the [[e:acarnania|Acarnanians]] and [[e:amphilochian-argos|Amphilochian Argos]], and in 426 BCE the Athenian general [[e:demosthenes-general|Demosthenes]] destroyed its army at [[e:battle-of-idomene|Idomene]]. It traded [[e:timber|timber]] and goods with [[e:epirus|Epirus]]. [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-epirus|Kingdom of Epirus]] made it his capital and adorned it with palaces and statues.
ambracia.e: After joining the [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]], Ambracia was besieged by [[e:marcus-fulvius-nobilior|Marcus Fulvius Nobilior]] in 189 BCE, who carried its works of art to [[e:rome|Rome]]. It declined, and Augustus moved its people to [[e:nicopolis-epirus|Nicopolis]]. Modern [[e:arta-greece|Arta]] stands on the site.

aden-settlement.t: Aden as a dependency of British India, seized in 1839 to serve as a coaling station on the steamship route to Bombay.
aden-settlement.o: In January 1839 forces of the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]] under Captain [[e:stafford-bettesworth-haines|Stafford Haines]] captured [[e:aden|Aden]] from the [[s:sultanate-of-lahej|Sultanate of Lahej]] after a dispute over a plundered ship. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] wanted a coaling station for steamships between Suez and [[e:mumbai|Bombay]], and Aden was governed from the [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Presidency]].
aden-settlement.r: [[e:stafford-bettesworth-haines|Haines]] served as political agent and built up the port, which had shrunk to a village. [[e:aden|Aden]] was declared a free port in 1850, and after the [[e:suez-canal|Suez Canal]] opened in 1869 it became one of the world's busiest bunkering stations, with Indian, [[e:somalis|Somali]], Jewish and Yemeni communities. From the 1870s [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] signed protection treaties with the hinterland rulers, creating the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. Its administration passed to [[s:british-raj|British India]] and then the [[e:british-raj|British Raj]].
aden-settlement.e: Under the [[e:government-of-india|Government of India]] Act of 1935, [[e:aden|Aden]] was separated from [[e:india|India]] and became a [[e:crown-colony|Crown colony]] on 1 April 1937, as the [[s:colony-of-aden|Colony of Aden]].
aden-settlement.re: Islam, with Hindu, Jewish and Christian minorities

aram-maacah.t: Aram-Maacah, a small Aramaean kingdom near Mount Hermon, known only from the Hebrew Bible.
aram-maacah.o: Maacah lay in the northern [[e:golan-heights|Golan]] and the slopes of [[e:mount-hermon|Mount Hermon]], north of [[s:geshur|Geshur]]. It is known only from the [[e:hebrew-bible|Hebrew Bible]], which lists it among the Aramaean kingdoms of the 10th century BCE.
aram-maacah.r: Nothing is known of its government. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] relates that its king sent a thousand men to support [[s:ammon|Ammon]] against [[e:david|David]] of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]].
aram-maacah.e: Maacah was absorbed by [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]] or the [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Kingdom of Israel]] in the 9th century BCE; the town of [[e:abel-beth-maacah|Abel-beth-maacah]] preserves its name.

arwad.t: Arwad, a tiny Phoenician island city off the Syrian coast whose sailors made it a naval power for more than a thousand years.
arwad.o: Arwad occupies a small island off [[e:tartus|Tartus]], giving it a sheltered harbour and natural defences. A Canaanite town by the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]], it appears in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]], and after 1200 BCE it became the northernmost of the great Phoenician cities, controlling the facing coast.
arwad.r: Kings ruled with a council of elders over a city of tall houses and a fleet of merchant ships. Arwad supplied ships to [[e:tiglath-pileser-i|Tiglath-Pileser I]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], and its king Mattan-[[e:baal|Baal]] sent troops to the coalition against [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] at [[e:battle-of-qarqar|Qarqar]] in 853 BCE. It later contributed ships to the Persian fleet.
arwad.e: Arwad submitted to Alexander of the [[s:macedonian-empire|Macedonian Empire]] in 332 BCE, kept wide autonomy under the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]], and counted its own era from 259 BCE. It lost independence when [[e:pompey|Pompey]] annexed [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] in 64 BCE.

ahom-kingdom.t: The Tai kingdom of the Brahmaputra valley that ruled Assam for six centuries and repeatedly defeated the Mughal Empire.
ahom-kingdom.o: [[e:sukaphaa|Sukaphaa]], a Tai prince from the Shan region of upper [[s:myanmar|Burma]], crossed the Patkai hills with his followers and settled in the upper [[e:brahmaputra|Brahmaputra]] valley in 1228. He founded his capital at [[e:charaideo|Charaideo]] and gradually absorbed local [[e:moran-people|Moran]] and Borahi peoples, laying the foundations of a state that expanded westwards for three centuries.
ahom-kingdom.r: The [[e:ahom-people|Ahoms]] ran a distinctive paik system in which every adult man owed labour or military service to the state, allowing large irrigation, road and embankment works. Court chronicles called buranjis record their history. [[e:suhungmung|Suhungmung]] annexed the [[s:chutia-kingdom|Chutia kingdom]], and the general [[e:lachit-borphukan|Lachit Borphukan]] defeated a Mughal army at the [[e:battle-of-saraighat|Battle of Saraighat]] in 1671. Kings gradually adopted [[e:hinduism|Hinduism]] and Assamese.
ahom-kingdom.e: The Moamoria rebellion of the late 18th century and Burmese invasions from 1817 devastated the kingdom. After the [[e:first-anglo-burmese-war|First Anglo-Burmese War]], the [[e:treaty-of-yandabo|Treaty of Yandabo]] in 1826 gave [[e:assam|Assam]] to the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]], which annexed it to its Indian territories. The Ahom legacy shaped modern Assamese identity.

azad-hind.t: A provisional government of free India led by Subhas Chandra Bose and backed by Japan during the Second World War.
azad-hind.o: [[e:subhas-chandra-bose|Subhas Chandra Bose]], a former president of the [[e:indian-national-congress|Indian National Congress]], escaped [[s:british-raj|British India]] in 1941 and reached Japanese-held [[s:singapore|Singapore]] in 1943. There he took command of the [[e:indian-national-army|Indian National Army]], made up largely of Indian prisoners of war, and in October 1943 proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free [[e:india|India]].
azad-hind.r: The government was recognised by [[e:japan|Japan]], [[e:germany|Germany]] and their allies and declared war on [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and the [[s:united-states|United States]]. Japan handed it nominal authority over the [[e:andaman-and-nicobar-islands|Andaman and Nicobar Islands]], but real control stayed with the Japanese navy. It ran its own currency, courts and a women's unit, the [[e:rani-of-jhansi-regiment|Rani of Jhansi Regiment]], and recruited among Indians in South-[[e:east-asia|East Asia]].
azad-hind.e: The [[e:indian-national-army|Indian National Army]] joined the failed Japanese offensive on [[e:battle-of-imphal|Imphal]] and [[e:battle-of-kohima|Kohima]] in 1944. With [[e:japan|Japan's]] surrender in 1945 the government collapsed, and [[e:subhas-chandra-bose|Bose]] died after a plane crash in [[s:republic-of-china|Taiwan]]. The trials of its officers at the [[e:red-fort|Red Fort]] stirred nationalist feeling in [[e:india|India]].

arab-byzantine-condominium-of-cyprus.t: Nearly three centuries in which Cyprus was neutral ground shared between the Byzantine Empire and the Caliphate, which split its taxes.
arab-byzantine-condominium-of-cyprus.o: Arab fleets raided [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] from 649. In 688 the Byzantine emperor [[e:justinian-ii|Justinian II]] and the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:abd-al-malik-ibn-marwan|Abd al-Malik]] agreed a treaty under which the revenues of Cyprus, along with those of [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and [[e:iberia|Iberia]], were divided equally between them. The island was to be demilitarised and neutral, though the arrangement was repeatedly interrupted.
arab-byzantine-condominium-of-cyprus.r: [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] kept its Greek-speaking Christian population, its [[e:bishop|bishops]] and local officials, while paying tribute to both powers. [[e:justinian-ii|Justinian II]] moved many islanders to [[s:cyzicus|Cyzicus]] around 691, and they returned about 698. Both sides violated the neutrality: Byzantine and Abbasid fleets raided the island, and [[e:harun-al-rashid|Harun al-Rashid's]] forces deported Cypriots. Historians debate how formal the condominium really was.
arab-byzantine-condominium-of-cyprus.e: As Byzantine power revived in the 10th century, [[e:nikephoros-ii-phokas|Nikephoros II Phokas]] sent the patrician [[e:niketas-chalkoutzes|Niketas Chalkoutzes]] to retake [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] in 965. It became a Byzantine province until [[e:isaac-komnenos-of-cyprus|Isaac Komnenos]] seized it in 1184.

aegium.t: Achaean city on the Gulf of Corinth where the assembly of the Achaean League met at the sanctuary of Zeus Homarios.
aegium.o: Aegium lay on the southern shore of the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]], one of the twelve Achaean cities of the northern [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]]. It grew in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] on a terrace above a harbour; myth said [[e:agamemnon|Agamemnon]] gathered the Greek chiefs there before [[e:troy|Troy]].
aegium.r: The sanctuary of [[e:zeus|Zeus]] Homarios near Aegium was the religious centre of the [[e:achaeans-achaea|Achaeans]]. After the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]] was refounded in 280 BCE, Aegium expelled its Macedonian garrison in 275 BCE and joined; the league's regular assemblies met there. The town lived from farming and the coastal trade of the gulf.
aegium.e: [[e:philopoemen|Philopoemen]] moved the meetings in rotation among member cities in the 180s BCE, reducing Aegium's role. It passed under Roman control in 146 BCE and continues as the modern town of [[s:barony-of-vostitsa|Aigio]].
aegium.re: Greek religion; cult of Zeus Homarios

avar-khanate.t: The leading Avar state of mountainous Dagestan for six centuries, centred on Khunzakh, whose khans were courted by Persia, the Ottomans and Russia.
avar-khanate.o: After the decline of Christian [[s:sarir|Sarir]], a ruling house of [[e:avars|Avar]] nutsals emerged at [[e:khunzakh|Khunzakh]] around the 12th and 13th centuries. [[e:islam|Islam]] spread into the region during the 13th to 15th centuries, and the nutsals came to rule as Muslim khans over the Avar communities of the highlands.
avar-khanate.r: The khans held direct power over [[e:khunzakh|Khunzakh]] and nearby villages but relied on alliances with the self-governing [[e:avars|Avar]] free communities, which had their own assemblies and customary law. Wealth came from herding, terraced farming and raiding. [[e:umma-khan-v|Umma Khan]], who ruled from 1774, led raids deep into [[s:georgia|Georgia]] and [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvan]], and the khanate received [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] from the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]] and later [[e:russia|Russia]].
avar-khanate.e: In 1834 [[e:hamzat-bek|Hamzat Bek]], [[e:imam|imam]] of the [[s:caucasian-imamate|Caucasian Imamate]], massacred the khan's family at [[e:khunzakh|Khunzakh]]. The khanate then passed to rulers installed by [[e:russia|Russia]], was held by [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]]'s forces from 1843 to 1859, and was abolished by the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] in 1864 and turned into the [[e:avars|Avar]] district.

austrasia.t: Eastern kingdom of the Merovingian Franks, centred on Metz and Reims, and the homeland of the Carolingian dynasty.
austrasia.o: Austrasia, the eastern land, arose from the share of [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]]' eldest son [[e:theuderic-i|Theuderic I]] in 511, ruled from [[e:reims|Reims]] and later [[e:metz|Metz]]. It covered north-eastern [[e:france|France]], the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]], [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]], and was extended over [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]], [[s:duchy-of-alamannia|Alemannia]] and [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]].
austrasia.r: Its population was more Germanic than that of [[s:neustria|Neustria]], and its aristocracy was powerful. [[e:sigebert-i|Sigebert I]] and his Visigothic queen [[e:brunhilda-of-austrasia|Brunhild]] fought a long feud with Neustria. From the 7th century the mayors of the palace, above all the [[e:pippinids|Pippinid]] family, held real power while kings reigned as figureheads.
austrasia.e: [[e:pippin-of-herstal|Pippin of Herstal]] defeated [[s:neustria|Neustria]] at [[e:battle-of-tertry|Tertry]] in 687 and became master of the whole [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]]. His son [[e:charles-martel|Charles Martel]] and grandson [[e:pepin-the-short|Pippin the Short]] followed, and in 751 Pippin made himself king, ending Austrasia as a separate kingdom.

antanosy-kingdom.t: The kingdom of the Anosy region in south-east Madagascar, the first Malagasy state to confront a French colony on the island.
antanosy-kingdom.o: The [[e:antanosy|Antanosy]] kingdom took shape around 1500 in the fertile Anosy region near modern [[e:taolagnaro|Taolagnaro]], under the [[e:zafiraminia|Zafiraminia]], a ruling clan claiming descent from Muslim immigrants. They kept Arabic-script writing and certain Islamic customs while ruling a largely Malagasy population.
antanosy-kingdom.r: [[e:zafiraminia|Zafiraminia]] nobles held ritual privileges, including the exclusive right to slaughter [[e:cattle|cattle]], and ruled over clans of commoners and slaves. The French governor [[e:etienne-de-flacourt|Etienne de Flacourt]] described [[e:antanosy|Antanosy]] society in detail in his [[e:history-of-the-great-island-of-madagascar|History of the Great Island of Madagascar]] of 1658. Relations with the [[s:fort-dauphin-colony|Fort-Dauphin Colony]] swung between trade and war, with the French seizing cattle and [[e:rice|rice]].
antanosy-kingdom.e: The French abandoned [[s:fort-dauphin-colony|Fort-Dauphin]] in 1674 after an [[e:antanosy|Antanosy]] uprising. The region remained divided among rival lords until the [[s:merina-kingdom|Merina Kingdom]] conquered it in 1825. The Antanosy remain a distinct people of south-east [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]].
antanosy-kingdom.re: Traditional Malagasy religion with Islamic elements

aulikara-dynasty.t: A Malwa dynasty of Dashapura whose king Yashodharman claimed victory over the Huns and boasted of ruling from the Himalaya to the ocean.
aulikara-dynasty.o: The Aulikaras ruled [[e:mandsaur|Dashapura]], modern Mandsaur in western [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]], from around 400, at first as allies or feudatories of the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]]. Their early kings, such as Naravarman and Bandhuvarman, are known from inscriptions dated in the Malava era.
aulikara-dynasty.r: The [[e:mandsaur|Mandsaur]] [[e:silk|silk]] weavers' inscription records how a [[e:guild|guild]] of weavers migrated from [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] to Dashapura and built a Sun temple in 436, restoring it in 473, a vivid picture of guild life in a prosperous city. Around 528 [[e:yasodharman|Yashodharman]] set up victory pillars at Sondani near Mandsaur, claiming to have defeated the Hun ruler [[e:mihirakula|Mihirakula]] and to rule lands never held by the [[e:gupta-empire|Guptas]].
aulikara-dynasty.e: [[e:yasodharman|Yashodharman's]] dominion seems to have collapsed after his death, and the dynasty disappears from the record by the mid-6th century. [[e:malwa|Malwa]] passed to the [[s:kalachuris-of-mahishmati|Kalachuris of Mahishmati]] and other powers.

ayyubid-emirate-of-baalbek.t: An Ayyubid principality in the Beqaa Valley, held for half a century by the poet-prince al-Amjad Bahramshah.
ayyubid-emirate-of-baalbek.o: [[e:saladin|Saladin]] took [[e:baalbek|Baalbek]] in 1174 and granted it in 1179 to his nephew [[e:farrukh-shah|Farrukh Shah]]. On Farrukh Shah's death in 1182 the town passed to his son [[e:al-amjad-bahramshah|al-Amjad Bahramshah]].
ayyubid-emirate-of-baalbek.r: [[e:baalbek|Baalbek's]] rulers lived within the great Roman temple complex, which had been turned into a citadel. [[e:al-amjad-bahramshah|Bahramshah]] ruled for nearly fifty years as a minor member of the Ayyubid family, depending on the stronger princes of [[e:damascus|Damascus]], and was known as a poet. The district produced grain and fruit in the [[e:beqaa-valley|Beqaa]] and controlled the road from Damascus to [[e:homs|Homs]].
ayyubid-emirate-of-baalbek.e: [[e:al-ashraf-musa-sultan-of-damascus|Al-Ashraf Musa]] took [[e:baalbek|Baalbek]] from [[e:al-amjad-bahramshah|Bahramshah]] in 1230, and it passed to [[e:as-salih-ismail|al-Salih Ismail]]. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] occupied the town in 1260 and damaged the citadel, and after [[e:battle-of-ain-jalut|Ain Jalut]] it came under the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]].

ashikaga-shogunate.t: The second warrior government of Japan, based in Kyoto's Muromachi district, whose age produced Noh theatre, Zen gardens and the tea ceremony.
ashikaga-shogunate.o: [[e:ashikaga-takauji|Ashikaga Takauji]] turned against [[e:emperor-go-daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo's]] [[s:kenmu-restoration|Kenmu Restoration]], took [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] in 1336, issued the Kenmu shikimoku as a statement of policy and installed an emperor of the [[s:northern-court|Northern Court]], who named him [[e:shogun|shogun]] in 1338.
ashikaga-shogunate.r: The [[e:shogun|shoguns]] ruled through great [[e:vassal|vassal]] families serving as provincial military governors (shugo) and deputies (kanrei). [[e:ashikaga-yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]] ended the split between the Northern and Southern Courts in 1392, built the [[e:kinkaku-ji|Golden Pavilion]] and opened tally trade with [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]]. Culture flourished under shogunal patronage: [[e:zeami-motokiyo|Zeami]]'s Noh, [[e:sesshu-toyo|Sesshu]]'s ink painting, Zen temples and the [[e:ginkaku-ji|Silver Pavilion]] of Yoshimasa.
ashikaga-shogunate.e: The [[e:onin-war|Onin War]] of 1467 to 1477 shattered shogunal authority and began the [[e:sengoku-period|Sengoku]] era of warring lords. [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]] drove out the last [[e:shogun|shogun]], [[e:ashikaga-yoshiaki|Ashikaga Yoshiaki]], in 1573.

ausci.t: Aquitanian people of Gascony whose chief town Elimberris became Auch, later the religious capital of the region.
ausci.o: The Ausci lived in the hills of central [[e:gascony|Gascony]], in the modern [[e:gers|Gers]]. They were among the [[e:aquitani|Aquitani]], whose language was related to Basque; the name of their town, [[e:auch|Elimberris]], is usually read as Basque-like 'new town', comparable with Iliberris in [[e:iberia|Iberia]].
ausci.r: [[e:pomponius-mela|Pomponius Mela]] calls them the most distinguished of the Aquitanian peoples. Nothing is recorded of their rulers before the conquest.
ausci.e: The Ausci gave hostages to [[e:publius-licinius-crassus|Publius Crassus]] in 56 BCE without fighting. Their town was refounded as [[e:auch|Augusta Auscorum]], and in the early [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]] it replaced [[e:eauze|Eauze]] as the metropolitan see of [[e:novempopulania|Novempopulana]]. Auch remained the seat of an archbishop for all of [[e:gascony|Gascony]].

aorsi.t: A powerful Sarmatian people between the Don and the Caspian, whose control of caravan routes made them rich in gold and allies of Rome.
aorsi.o: The Aorsi emerge in Greek sources in the 2nd century BCE as one of the leading Sarmatian groups, descended from the earlier steppe populations of the [[s:sarmatians|Sauromatae]]. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] divides them into a western group on the lower [[e:don-river|Don]] and the 'Upper Aorsi' further east, who ruled most of the Caspian shore.
aorsi.r: [[e:strabo|Strabo]] reports that the Aorsi could field 200,000 horsemen and that the Upper Aorsi wore gold because they carried Indian and Babylonian goods on [[e:camel|camels]] from [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and Media. They were pastoral nomads organised under kings, and they appear in the politics of the [[s:bosporan-kingdom|Bosporan Kingdom]], fighting with [[e:rome|Rome]] against the [[e:siraces|Siraces]] in 49 CE under their king [[e:eunones|Eunones]].
aorsi.e: From the late 1st century CE the Aorsi fade from the record as the [[s:alans|Alans]] rose to dominate the same steppes. Most historians think they were absorbed into the Alan confederation, which the [[e:huns|Huns]] overran in the 370s.

armenian-ssr.t: Soviet Armenia, a republic of the USSR from 1920 to 1991, which saw rapid industrialisation, mass immigration and the devastating 1988 earthquake.
armenian-ssr.o: In December 1920, with Turkish forces in the west and the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] in the east, the government of the [[s:first-republic-of-armenia|First Republic of Armenia]] ceded power to the Bolsheviks. After a brief anti-Bolshevik revolt in 1921, the Armenian SSR was established, joined the [[s:transcaucasian-sfsr|Transcaucasian SFSR]] in 1922 and became a full union republic in 1936.
armenian-ssr.r: Soviet rule brought industry, hydroelectric power at [[e:lake-sevan|Lake Sevan]], universities and the growth of [[e:yerevan|Yerevan]] to a planned capital designed by [[e:alexander-tamanian|Alexander Tamanian]]. Tens of thousands of diaspora [[e:armenians|Armenians]] resettled there after 1946. The church was repressed, and [[e:joseph-stalin|Stalin]]'s purges struck the intelligentsia. In 1965 mass demonstrations marked the 50th anniversary of the [[e:genocide|genocide]].
armenian-ssr.e: From 1988 the [[e:karabakh-movement|Karabakh movement]] mobilised [[e:armenians|Armenians]] to demand [[e:nagorno-karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh]], while the [[e:1988-armenian-earthquake|Spitak earthquake]] killed about 25,000 people. [[s:armenia|Armenia]] voted for independence in September 1991, becoming the [[s:first-republic-of-armenia|Republic of Armenia]].

alans.t: Iranian-speaking horse nomads of the North Caucasus steppe who raided Rome and Persia, followed the Vandals to Africa, and gave rise to the Ossetians.
alans.o: The Alans emerged in the 1st century CE among the [[s:sarmatians|Sarmatians]] on the steppes north of the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]]. Roman writers record their raids through the Caucasus passes into [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and Media in the 70s CE, and in the 130s the governor [[e:arrian|Arrian]] wrote a battle plan against them.
alans.r: They lived as mounted herders in clans under chiefs, moving with wagons and fighting as [[e:heavy-cavalry|heavy cavalry]] with lances, a style that influenced Roman cavalry. [[e:ammianus-marcellinus|Ammianus Marcellinus]] described their worship of a naked sword. They traded and fought with the [[s:roman-empire|Roman Empire]], the [[s:parthian-empire|Parthian Empire]] and the peoples of the steppe.
alans.e: The [[s:hunnic-empire|Hunnic Empire]] shattered them around 370. Some Alans moved west with the [[e:vandals|Vandals]] into [[e:gaul|Gaul]], [[e:spain|Spain]] and [[e:north-africa|North Africa]], while others stayed in the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]] foothills, became tributary to the [[s:khazar-khaganate|Khazar Khaganate]] and formed the [[s:kingdom-of-alania|Kingdom of Alania]]. The [[e:ossetians|Ossetians]] descend from them.

ah-canul.t: A Maya province of north-western Campeche governed by the Canul lineage, whose history survives in the Codex of Calkiní.
ah-canul.o: The Canul lineage traced its origins to warriors from the [[e:gulf-coast-of-mexico|Gulf Coast]] who served the rulers of [[s:league-of-mayapan|Mayapan]]. After the fall of the League of Mayapan around 1441, they settled in northern [[e:campeche|Campeche]] and established a province with [[e:calkini|Calkiní]] as its leading town.
ah-canul.r: Ah Canul was governed by a council of lords of the Canul lineage rather than a single supreme ruler, each heading a group of towns. Its people farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] and traded with the coast. The [[e:codex-of-calkini|Codex of Calkiní]], written in Maya in the colonial period, records its lineages and the coming of the Spanish.
ah-canul.e: In 1541 the Canul lords submitted peacefully to [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-younger|Francisco de Montejo the Younger]], and the province was absorbed into the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]]. [[e:calkini|Calkiní]] is now a town in [[e:campeche|Campeche]].

ajaigarh-state.t: A Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand named after the hill fortress of Ajaigarh, a former Chandela stronghold.
ajaigarh-state.o: [[e:ajaigarh|Ajaigarh's]] rulers descended from [[e:chhatrasal|Chhatrasal]] through the [[s:panna-state|Panna]] line. Around 1765 [[e:guman-singh|Guman Singh]] received a share of the family lands with his seat at [[s:kingdom-of-banda|Banda]]. After the British took Banda, his successor [[e:bakht-singh-of-ajaigarh|Bakht Singh]] was granted the hill fort of Ajaigarh and its lands by sanad in the early 19th century.
ajaigarh-state.r: [[e:ajaigarh|Ajaigarh]] was an 11-gun salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]], ruled by a Raja, later [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]], over hilly country between the Ken river and the [[e:vindhya-range|Vindhya]] scarp. The fort, with its medieval Chandela temples and gates, was the state's chief monument.
ajaigarh-state.e: After independence [[e:ajaigarh|Ajaigarh]] was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] in 1948 and joined [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956; it lies in [[s:panna-state|Panna]] district.

airenosi.t: A Pyrenean people known only from Polybius' list of those Hannibal conquered in 218 BCE, possibly of the Val d'Aran.
airenosi.o: The Airenosi appear in [[e:polybius|Polybius]] among the peoples between the [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] and the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] subdued by [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] in 218 BCE. Their location is uncertain; they are often placed in the central Pyrenees, perhaps in the [[e:val-daran|Val d'Aran]], on the basis of their name.
airenosi.r: Nothing is known of their society or government.
airenosi.e: After [[e:hannibal|Hannibal's]] conquest the region was held for [[e:carthage|Carthage]] by Hanno until the Roman advance. It came under [[e:rome|Rome]] in the early 2nd century BCE, and the Airenosi disappear from the record.

ashnakkum.t: Ashnakkum, a kingdom of the upper Khabur region in the age of Mari, one of the shifting players in the politics of northern Mesopotamia.
ashnakkum.o: Ashnakkum was a city of the [[e:ida-maras|Ida-Maras]] district in north-eastern [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], often identified with Chagar Bazar, though this is debated. Chagar Bazar, excavated by [[e:max-mallowan|Max Mallowan]] in the 1930s, served as a provincial centre under [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]]'s [[s:kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia|Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia]] in the early 18th century BCE.
ashnakkum.r: After [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]]'s death Ashnakkum became an independent kingdom that appears often in the [[s:mari|Mari]] letters, alternately allied with and opposed to [[e:zimri-lim|Zimri-Lim]]. Tablets from Chagar Bazar record rations and administration of farmland, livestock and workers.
ashnakkum.e: Ashnakkum fell under the shadow of [[e:babylon|Babylon]] after the destruction of [[s:mari|Mari]] c. 1760 BCE and lost its independence. The region later formed part of the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]].

artuqids-of-hasankeyf.t: A Turkmen dynasty on the Tigris that ruled Hasankeyf and Amid and employed the engineer al-Jazari, author of a celebrated book of machines.
artuqids-of-hasankeyf.o: The [[s:artuqids-of-mardin|Artuqids]] descended from [[e:artuq-ibn-ekseb|Artuq]], a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] commander of the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]]. His son [[e:sokmen-ibn-artuq|Sokmen]], who lost [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] to the [[e:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimids]] in 1098, took [[e:hasankeyf|Hisn Kayfa]] (Hasankeyf) on the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] in 1102 and helped defeat the [[e:crusader-states|Crusaders]] at [[e:harran|Harran]] in 1104.
artuqids-of-hasankeyf.r: The [[e:hasankeyf|Hasankeyf]] line ruled the upper [[e:tigris|Tigris]] valley and from 1183, when [[e:saladin|Saladin]] gave them Amid, the city of [[e:diyarbakir|Diyarbakir]]. They built the great bridge at Hasankeyf and repaired the walls of Amid. At their court [[e:ismail-al-jazari|Ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari]] completed around 1206 his [[e:book-of-knowledge-of-ingenious-mechanical-devices|Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices]], describing water clocks, automata and pumps. Their coins often carried figurative images borrowed from Byzantine and classical models.
artuqids-of-hasankeyf.e: Caught between the [[e:ayyubid-empire|Ayyubids]] and the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]], the dynasty lost [[e:hasankeyf|Hasankeyf]] and Amid to the Ayyubid [[e:al-kamil|al-Kamil]] in 1232, and the [[s:ayyubids-of-hisn-kayfa|Ayyubids of Hisn Kayfa]] took over.

azai-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Azai of northern Omi, whose lord Azai Nagamasa betrayed his brother-in-law Oda Nobunaga and was destroyed in 1573.
azai-clan-domain.o: The Azai were retainers of the [[e:kyogoku-clan|Kyogoku]] governors of northern [[e:omi-province|Omi]]. In the 1520s [[e:azai-sukemasa|Azai Sukemasa]] took power from his masters in a period of internal strife and built the mountain fortress of Odani, overlooking [[e:lake-biwa|Lake Biwa's]] northern shore.
azai-clan-domain.r: The domain lay on the main roads between the capital and eastern [[e:japan|Japan]]. [[e:azai-sukemasa|Sukemasa]]'s son [[e:azai-hisamasa|Hisamasa]] was overshadowed by the [[e:rokkaku-clan|Rokkaku]] of southern [[e:omi-province|Omi]], but [[e:azai-nagamasa|Nagamasa]] defeated them in 1560 and married [[e:oichi|Oichi]], sister of [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]], around 1567, an alliance that secured Nobunaga's route to [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]].
azai-clan-domain.e: In 1570 [[e:azai-nagamasa|Nagamasa]] honoured an older alliance with the Asakura and attacked [[e:oda-nobunaga|Nobunaga]]. Defeated at [[e:battle-of-anegawa|Anegawa]] that year, he held out until 1573, when Odani fell and he killed himself. His daughters, [[e:yodo-dono|Chacha]], [[e:ohatsu|Hatsu]] and Go, later shaped [[e:toyotomi-clan|Toyotomi]] and Tokugawa politics.

angrivarii.t: A Germanic people of the middle Weser whose earthen boundary wall became the site of a major battle between Germanicus and Arminius in 16 CE.
angrivarii.o: The Angrivarii lived on both banks of the middle [[e:weser|Weser]], north of the [[s:cherusci|Cherusci]], in what is now [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]] and eastern [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]]. They appear in Roman sources around the time of [[e:nero-claudius-drusus|Drusus]]' campaigns, and were at times allies, at times enemies of [[e:rome|Rome]].
angrivarii.r: Little is known of their government. [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] mentions a broad earthwork they had built to mark their boundary with the [[s:cherusci|Cherusci]]; in 16 CE [[e:germanicus|Germanicus]] fought the [[e:battle-of-the-angrivarian-wall|Battle of the Angrivarian Wall]] there after his victory at [[e:battle-of-idistaviso|Idistaviso]]. After a revolt against [[e:rome|Rome]] they submitted and returned Roman captives bought from other tribes.
angrivarii.e: Around 98 [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] reports that the Angrivarii and [[e:chamavi|Chamavi]] had moved into the lands of the defeated [[s:bructeri|Bructeri]]. They were later absorbed into the [[s:saxons|Saxons]]; their name survives in [[e:angria|Engern]] (Angria), one of the three provinces of Old [[e:saxony|Saxony]], alongside [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] and [[e:eastphalia|Eastphalia]].

aden-protectorate.t: Britain's patchwork of some two dozen protected sultanates, emirates and sheikhdoms in the hinterland of Aden, the core of later South Yemen.
aden-protectorate.o: To secure the [[s:aden-settlement|Aden Settlement]] and keep the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] away from it, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] signed treaties with the tribal rulers around [[e:aden|Aden]] from the 1870s, beginning with the [[s:sultanate-of-lahej|Sultanate of Lahej]] and its neighbours, and later with the Hadrami states. Each ruler gave [[e:britain|Britain]] control of his foreign relations in return for protection and stipends.
aden-protectorate.r: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] at first intervened little in internal affairs. From 1937 the territory was divided into a Western and an Eastern Aden Protectorate, with political officers and local forces such as the [[e:aden|Aden]] [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]] Levies. In [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Hadramawt]] the agent [[e:harold-ingrams|Harold Ingrams]] negotiated a truce among hundreds of feuding tribes in 1937, known as Ingrams' Peace. An Anglo-Ottoman line of 1904-1914 marked the border with [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]].
aden-protectorate.e: In 1959 six western states formed the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]], later the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]], which most of the others joined; the eastern states, including the [[s:quaiti-sultanate|Qu'aiti Sultanate]], remained outside. All were swept away by the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] in 1967 and absorbed into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

aro-confederacy.t: A trading network of the Aro people centred on Arochukwu and its oracle, which dominated commerce, including the slave trade, across much of Igboland.
aro-confederacy.o: The Aro emerged at Arochukwu in the late 17th century from wars and alliances among [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]], [[e:ibibio-people|Ibibio]] and Akpa groups, traditionally under leaders remembered as Nnachi and Akuma Nnubi. The new community controlled the shrine of [[e:ibini-ukpabi|Ibini Ukpabi]], an oracle that Europeans called the Long Juju, whose authority was respected far beyond Arochukwu.
aro-confederacy.r: It was not a territorial state but a confederation of Aro lineages and settlements, ruled at home by the Eze Aro and councils of elders. Aro traders founded colonies along trade routes throughout [[e:igboland|Igboland]] and beyond, and used the oracle, alliances with [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] groups such as the [[e:abam|Abam]], and markets to move slaves to the ports of the [[s:bonny-kingdom|Bonny Kingdom]] and [[s:old-calabar|Old Calabar]], later dealing in [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]].
aro-confederacy.e: The British saw the Aro and their oracle as obstacles to trade and colonial control. In the [[e:anglo-aro-war|Anglo-Aro War]] of 1901-1902 British forces took Arochukwu and destroyed the shrine, and the Aro lands became part of the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]].

afrasiyab-dynasty-of-basra.t: A family of hereditary pashas who made Basra a nearly independent port state under nominal Ottoman rule for seventy years.
afrasiyab-dynasty-of-basra.o: In 1596 [[e:afrasiyab-of-basra|Afrasiyab]], a local official of uncertain origin, bought the governorship of [[e:basra|Basra]] from the Ottoman governor, who could no longer hold the remote province. [[e:afrasiab|Afrasiyab]] and his descendants ruled as hereditary pashas, sending token tribute to [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]].
afrasiyab-dynasty-of-basra.r: [[e:basra|Basra]] flourished as a free-trading port between the Gulf, [[e:india|India]] and the Ottoman lands. Ali Pasha (c. 1624 to 1650) welcomed Portuguese, English and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] merchants, patronised poets and scholars and resisted Safavid attacks. The pashas relied on Arab tribal allies and paid little attention to [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]]. Their rule saw Basra become a major centre for the trade in horses, dates and Indian textiles.
afrasiyab-dynasty-of-basra.e: Husayn Pasha's harsh rule provoked revolts and Ottoman intervention. In 1668 an Ottoman expedition took [[e:basra|Basra]], and Husayn fled to [[e:india|India]], ending the dynasty.

austuriani.t: A Libyan desert people whose raids on Tripolitania and Cyrenaica in the late 4th and 5th centuries exposed Roman weakness.
austuriani.o: The Austuriani (Austoriani) are known only from Roman writers. They lived in the desert hinterland of the [[e:gulf-of-sirte|Gulf of Sirte]] and first appear in the 360s, when they raided the territory of [[s:leptis-magna|Leptis Magna]] after one of their men, Stachao, was burned alive by the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]].
austuriani.r: They were [[e:camel|camel]]-using pastoral tribes without a known central government. [[e:ammianus-marcellinus|Ammianus Marcellinus]] describes their raids of 363 to 365, which devastated the farms around [[e:leptis-magna|Leptis]] and [[e:tripoli|Oea]], and the failure of the military count [[e:romanus-comes-africae|Romanus]], who demanded supplies and camels before acting. In the early 5th century they raided [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] repeatedly, as [[e:synesius|Bishop Synesius of Ptolemais]] reports in his letters.
austuriani.e: After the mid-5th century the name disappears. They were probably absorbed into, or renamed as, the larger [[s:laguatan|Laguatan]] confederation, which continued to press on [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] and [[s:praetorian-prefecture-of-africa|Byzantine Africa]].

abkhaz-ssr.t: A Soviet republic of Abkhazia that existed from 1921 to 1931 in a treaty union with Georgia, a status later invoked by Abkhaz separatists.
abkhaz-ssr.o: After the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] overthrew the [[s:democratic-republic-of-georgia|Democratic Republic of Georgia]] in early 1921, Bolsheviks at Sukhumi proclaimed the Soviet Socialist Republic of [[s:principality-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]] on 31 March 1921. In December 1921 it signed a special union treaty with the [[s:georgian-ssr|Georgian SSR]], and through it joined the [[s:transcaucasian-sfsr|Transcaucasian SFSR]] in 1922.
abkhaz-ssr.r: The republic was led by the popular [[e:abkhaz-people|Abkhaz]] Bolshevik [[e:nestor-lakoba|Nestor Lakoba]], who slowed collectivisation and protected local landowners and traditions. It had its own constitution from 1925 and promoted the Abkhaz language and culture, while its economy rested on tobacco, citrus fruit and [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] resorts.
abkhaz-ssr.e: In 1931, under [[e:joseph-stalin|Stalin]], its status was reduced to that of the [[e:abkhaz-people|Abkhaz]] Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic within the [[s:georgian-ssr|Georgian SSR]]. [[e:nestor-lakoba|Lakoba]] died in 1936, probably poisoned by [[e:lavrentiy-beria|Beria]]. Abkhaz leaders cited the 1921-1931 republic when breaking away from [[s:georgia|Georgia]] in the 1990s.
abkhaz-ssr.re: Christianity and Sunni Islam (officially atheist state)

amago-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Amago of Izumo, who rose from deputies to masters of much of western Honshu before falling to the Mori in 1566.
amago-clan-domain.o: The Amago were deputy governors of [[e:izumo-province|Izumo]] for the [[e:kyogoku-clan|Kyogoku]] family. [[e:amago-tsunehisa|Amago Tsunehisa]] was expelled from his post but, according to tradition, retook [[e:gassantoda-castle|Gassan-Toda]] castle by a ruse in 1486, and went on to make himself independent ruler of Izumo.
amago-clan-domain.r: [[e:amago-tsunehisa|Tsunehisa]] and his grandson [[e:amago-haruhisa|Haruhisa]] extended their power over the [[e:sanin-region|San'in]] and [[e:sanyo-region|San'yo]] regions, at their height claiming influence over eleven provinces. They contested the Iwami [[e:silver|silver]] mine with the [[e:ouchi-clan|Ouchi]] and withstood an Ouchi siege of [[e:gassantoda-castle|Gassan-Toda]] in 1542 and 1543. The mountain fortress was the heart of a network of allied local lords.
amago-clan-domain.e: After [[e:amago-haruhisa|Haruhisa]]'s death, [[e:mori-motonari|Mori Motonari]] invaded [[e:izumo-province|Izumo]] and besieged [[e:gassantoda-castle|Gassan-Toda]], and [[e:amago-yoshihisa|Amago Yoshihisa]] surrendered in 1566. The retainer [[e:yamanaka-yukimori|Yamanaka Yukimori]] fought to restore the clan until his death in 1578.

arzawa.t: Arzawa, the main kingdom of western Anatolia in the Late Bronze Age, a rival of the Hittites courted by Egypt.
arzawa.o: Arzawa emerged by the 16th century BCE in western [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], with its capital at [[e:apasa|Apasa]], later [[s:ephesus|Ephesus]]. Its Luwian-speaking rulers dominated the river valleys of the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] hinterland and exploited every period of Hittite weakness to expand eastward.
arzawa.r: In the 14th century BCE Arzawa was strong enough for [[e:amenhotep-iii|Amenhotep III]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] to negotiate a marriage with the daughter of King [[e:tarhundaradu|Tarhundaradu]]; the two [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]] involved are written in Hittite. The kingdom had links with the Mycenaean [[s:ahhiyawa|Ahhiyawa]] across the [[e:aegean|Aegean]].
arzawa.e: [[e:mursili-ii|Mursili II]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] defeated King [[e:uhha-ziti|Uhha-ziti]] c. 1320 BCE and took [[e:apasa|Apasa]]; Uhha-ziti fled across the sea to the islands. The [[e:hittite-empire|Hittites]] divided Arzawa into [[e:vassal|vassal]] states, including [[s:mira|Mira]], the [[s:seha-river-land|Seha River Land]] and [[s:hapalla|Hapalla]].

ashdod.t: Ashdod, a Philistine city of the coastal plain, famed in the Bible for its temple of Dagon and later for revolt against Assyria.
ashdod.o: Ashdod had been a Canaanite town before Philistine newcomers settled there in the 12th century BCE, making it one of the cities of the [[s:philistine-pentapolis|Philistine Pentapolis]]. Excavations at Tel Ashdod uncovered Aegean-style pottery and figurines from this period.
ashdod.r: Its kings ruled the city and a harbour on the coast. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] tells of the [[e:ark-of-the-covenant|Ark of the Covenant]] placed in its temple of [[e:dagan|Dagon]]. In 712 BCE King [[e:yamani|Yamani]] led a revolt against the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], and [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] crushed it, setting up a victory stele in the city.
ashdod.e: Ashdod remained an Assyrian [[e:vassal|vassal]], survived a long Egyptian siege under [[e:psamtik-i|Psamtik I]], and lost its kings to [[e:nebuchadnezzar-ii|Nebuchadnezzar II]] of the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]], who deported them to [[e:babylon|Babylon]] c. 604 BCE.

austrian-empire.t: The Habsburg monarchy as a hereditary empire, the conservative pillar of Metternich's Europe from Napoleon to the Compromise with Hungary.
austrian-empire.o: Facing [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] proclamation as Emperor of the French, [[e:francis-ii|Francis II]] proclaimed the Austrian Empire in August 1804, uniting the [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] hereditary lands, [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[e:hungary|Hungary]] under one imperial title. When he dissolved the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] in 1806, he continued as Francis I of [[e:austria|Austria]].
austrian-empire.r: Under [[e:klemens-von-metternich|Metternich]], foreign minister from 1809 and chancellor from 1821, [[e:austria|Austria]] led the Congress of Vienna and presided over the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]], suppressing liberal and national movements through censorship and police. The empire was multinational, with Germans, Hungarians, [[e:czechs|Czechs]], [[e:poles|Poles]], Italians and others, and Catholic in its institutions. The revolutions of 1848 were crushed with Russian help, and the young [[e:franz-joseph-i|Franz Joseph]] ruled through centralised neo-absolutism in the 1850s.
austrian-empire.e: Defeats at [[e:battle-of-solferino|Solferino]] in 1859 and [[e:battle-of-koniggratz|Königgrätz]] in 1866 cost [[e:austria|Austria]] [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]], [[e:venetia|Venetia]] and its leadership in [[e:germany|Germany]]. The [[e:austro-hungarian-compromise-of-1867|Compromise of 1867]] with [[e:hungary|Hungary]] transformed the empire into the dual monarchy of [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]].

aulerci-diablintes.t: Branch of the Aulerci in the western Mayenne whose Roman town at Jublains preserves one of the best surviving Roman forts in France.
aulerci-diablintes.o: The [[e:aulerci|Aulerci]] were a group of related peoples in north-western [[e:gaul|Gaul]]; the Diablintes held the area around [[e:jublains|Jublains]] in [[e:mayenne|Mayenne]], between the [[s:aulerci-cenomani|Cenomani]] and the [[s:redones|Redones]]. Caesar names them among the allies of the [[s:veneti|Veneti]], and Ptolemy gives their town as Noviodunum.
aulerci-diablintes.r: Very little is known of their society before the conquest. They shared in the Atlantic and Armorican trade networks and struck coins of Armorican type.
aulerci-diablintes.e: After joining the [[s:veneti|Veneti]] in 56 BCE they were defeated and absorbed into [[e:gallia-lugdunensis|Gallia Lugdunensis]]. Their Roman town of [[e:jublains|Noviodunum Diablintum]] at Jublains, with its temple, baths, [[e:theatre|theatre]] and fortified store-building, declined in late antiquity when the civitas merged with that of the [[s:aulerci-cenomani|Cenomani]].

cr.a: Diablintes (peuple celtique de Gaule). Autorité émettrice de monnaie

alaouite-sultanate.t: The sharifian dynasty from Tafilalt that reunited Morocco in the 1660s and has reigned ever since, keeping the country outside Ottoman rule.
alaouite-sultanate.o: The [[e:alaouite-dynasty|Alaouites]] were a sharifian family settled in the [[e:tafilalt|Tafilalt]] oasis. Amid the collapse of the [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]], [[e:moulay-ali-al-sharif|Moulay Ali al-Sharif]] was proclaimed leader there around 1631. His son [[e:al-rashid-of-morocco|Moulay al-Rashid]] took [[e:fez|Fez]] in 1666, crushed the [[s:dilaiyya|Dila'iyya]] in 1668 and took [[e:marrakesh|Marrakesh]] in 1669, reuniting [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]].
alaouite-sultanate.r: [[e:moulay-ismail|Moulay Ismail]], ruling from 1672 to 1727, made [[e:meknes|Meknes]] a vast imperial city and built the [[e:black-guard-morocco|Abid al-Bukhari]], an army of enslaved black soldiers. He recovered [[e:tangier|Tangier]], [[e:mehdya|La Mamora]] and [[e:larache|Larache]] from Europeans. [[e:mohammed-iii-of-morocco|Sidi Mohammed ibn Abdallah]] founded [[e:essaouira|Essaouira]] as a trading port and in 1777 was among the first rulers to recognise the [[s:united-states|United States]]. The sultan ruled through the makhzen, with tribes alternately obedient or dissident.
alaouite-sultanate.e: Defeats by [[e:france|France]] at [[e:battle-of-isly|Isly]] in 1844 and by [[e:spain|Spain]] in 1860 opened [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] to European pressure, and the [[e:treaty-of-fez|Treaty of Fez]] of 1912 created the [[s:french-protectorate-in-morocco|French protectorate in Morocco]]; a Franco-Spanish treaty later that year set up the [[s:spanish-protectorate-in-morocco|Spanish protectorate in Morocco]] in the north. The dynasty survived, and after independence in 1956 [[e:mohammed-v-of-morocco|Mohammed V]] took the title of king, forming the Kingdom of [[e:morocco|Morocco]].

ayudha-dynasty.t: A short-lived dynasty of Kannauj whose kings became pawns in the struggle between the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.
ayudha-dynasty.o: The Ayudhas held [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] in the late 8th century after the decline of the [[s:varman-dynasty-of-kannauj|Varman dynasty of Kannauj]]. The dynasty is known only from references in the inscriptions of neighbouring powers and in Jain literature, and its first known king is [[e:indrayudha|Indrayudha]].
ayudha-dynasty.r: [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] was the symbolic capital of northern [[e:india|India]], and control of it was the prize in the tripartite struggle. [[e:dharmapala-pala-emperor|Dharmapala]] of the [[s:pala-empire|Pala Empire]] deposed [[e:indrayudha|Indrayudha]] and placed [[e:chakrayudha|Chakrayudha]] on the throne, holding a great court where northern kings acknowledged the new ruler. Chakrayudha was effectively a Pala client.
ayudha-dynasty.e: Around 816 [[e:nagabhata-ii|Nagabhata II]] of the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]] defeated [[e:chakrayudha|Chakrayudha]] and took [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]], which became the Pratihara capital. Nothing is known of the Ayudhas afterwards.

austrian-netherlands.t: The southern Low Countries under Austrian Habsburg rule, a prosperous but contested land whose resistance to Joseph II's reforms foreshadowed Belgium.
austrian-netherlands.o: After the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]], the [[e:treaty-of-utrecht|Treaties of Utrecht]] and [[e:treaty-of-rastatt|Rastatt]] in 1713–1714 transferred the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]] to [[e:charles-vi-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Charles VI]]. The [[e:barrier-treaty-1715|Barrier Treaty]] of 1715 allowed [[e:dutch|Dutch]] garrisons in a line of fortresses against [[e:france|France]].
austrian-netherlands.r: Governors ruled from [[e:brussels|Brussels]], the most popular being [[e:charles-duke-of-lower-lorraine|Charles of Lorraine]] (1744–1780). The [[e:ostend-company|Ostend Company]], founded in 1722 to trade with Asia, was suppressed in 1731 under [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and British pressure. [[e:france|France]] occupied the country after [[e:battle-of-fontenoy|Fontenoy]] in 1745–1748. Agriculture, roads and industry developed under [[e:maria-theresa|Maria Theresa]], and Brussels gained neoclassical squares.
austrian-netherlands.e: [[e:joseph-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Joseph II]]'s centralising and church reforms sparked the [[e:brabant-revolution|Brabant Revolution]] of 1789 and the short-lived [[s:united-belgian-states|United Belgian States]]. [[e:austria|Austria]] restored control in 1790, but French victory at [[e:battle-of-fleurus-1794|Fleurus]] in 1794 led to annexation in 1795, confirmed by the [[e:treaty-of-campo-formio|Treaty of Campo Formio]] in 1797.

cr.a: self made from a low resolution raster version probably by Auseklis or Stijn_Calle, with some elements by Sodacan

abdallab-sheikhdom.t: The Arab sheikhdom of Qerri, partner of the Funj sultans, which governed the northern Sudanese Nile as their chief vassal for three centuries.
abdallab-sheikhdom.o: The Abdallab descended from [[e:abdallah-jamma|Abdallah Jamma]], leader of the Qawasma [[e:arabs|Arabs]], who allied with the [[e:funj-sultanate-of-sennar|Funj]] leader [[e:amara-dunqas|Amara Dunqas]] to destroy [[s:alodia|Alodia]] around 1504. Abdallah established his seat at [[e:qerri|Qerri]], north of the confluence of the Blue and [[e:white-nile|White Niles]], controlling the routes north toward [[e:egypt|Egypt]].
abdallab-sheikhdom.r: The Abdallab chiefs, titled manjil, ruled the Arab tribes and the northern provinces as [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]] of the [[s:funj-sultanate|Funj Sultanate]], collecting tribute and controlling trade with [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. [[e:ajib-al-kafuta|Ajib al-Kafuta]], the most famous chief, sought greater independence and was killed by the [[e:funj-sultanate-of-sennar|Funj]] around 1611; afterwards the sheikhs remained subordinate but influential.
abdallab-sheikhdom.e: The Abdallab lost much of their power in the 18th century as the [[e:hamaj|Hamaj]] regents dominated [[e:funj-sultanate-of-sennar|Sennar]]. In 1821 they submitted to the invading army of [[s:egypt-under-muhammad-ali|Egypt under Muhammad Ali]], and the [[s:turco-egyptian-sudan|Turco-Egyptian Sudan]] absorbed their lands.

aptera.t: Hilltop city above Souda Bay in western Crete, whose name myth linked to Sirens who lost their wings in a contest with the Muses.
aptera.o: Aptera stood on a plateau overlooking [[e:souda-bay|Souda Bay]] in western [[e:crete|Crete]]. A place called a-pa-ta-wa in [[e:linear-b|Linear B]] tablets from [[s:knossos|Knossos]] may be its forerunner. The city grew in the Archaic period; its name, meaning wingless, was explained by a legend that the [[e:sirens|Sirens]] lost their feathers after losing a singing contest to the [[e:muses|Muses]].
aptera.r: Aptera had a port at [[e:kissamos|Kisamos]] on [[e:souda-bay|Souda Bay]] and walls nearly four kilometres long. Like other Cretan cities it supplied [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] to Hellenistic kings, and its coins show [[e:artemis|Artemis]] and the hero Apteros. Inscriptions record treaties with [[s:teos|Teos]] and other Greek states.
aptera.e: Aptera came under [[e:rome|Rome]] in the conquest of 69 to 67 BCE and prospered as a Roman town, with large cisterns. It was largely abandoned after an earthquake in the 7th century CE.

anglo-corsican-kingdom.t: A two-year union of Corsica with the British crown, created by Pasquale Paoli to escape revolutionary France.
anglo-corsican-kingdom.o: [[e:pasquale-paoli|Pasquale Paoli]] returned to [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]] in 1790 but broke with the [[e:french-revolution|French Revolution]]. In 1794, with British naval help, Corsican forces drove the French from the island; [[e:horatio-nelson|Nelson]] lost the sight of an eye at the [[e:siege-of-calvi|siege of Calvi]]. A Corsican assembly at [[e:corte|Corte]] voted to offer the crown to [[e:george-iii|George III]].
anglo-corsican-kingdom.r: The kingdom had a liberal constitution with an elected parliament, under a British [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]], [[e:gilbert-elliot-1st-earl-of-minto|Sir Gilbert Elliot]], who governed from [[e:bastia|Bastia]]. Paoli expected to lead the government but was sidelined and left for [[e:london|London]] in 1795. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] valued the island as a naval base in the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
anglo-corsican-kingdom.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] victories in [[e:italy|Italy]] in 1796 made the island hard to hold, and [[e:spain|Spain's]] alliance with [[e:france|France]] threatened British naval control. The British evacuated [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]] in October 1796, and it returned to the [[s:french-first-republic|French First Republic]].

athens.t: The city-state of Attica that created democracy, led the Delian League and produced the drama, philosophy and architecture at the heart of Classical Greek culture.
athens.o: Athens was inhabited continuously from the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]], and the Acropolis held a Mycenaean palace. In the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] the communities of [[e:attica|Attica]] were unified under Athens, a process the [[e:greeks|Greeks]] credited to [[e:theseus|Theseus]].
