Kings gave way to annual archons drawn from the aristocracy, and the city adopted [[e:draco-lawgiver|Draco]]'s written laws in 621 BCE.
athens.r: [[e:solon|Solon's]] reforms of 594 BCE ended debt bondage; [[e:peisistratus|Peisistratus]] then ruled as tyrant, and [[e:cleisthenes|Cleisthenes]] founded democracy in 508 BCE. Athens defeated [[e:persia|Persia]] at [[e:battle-of-marathon|Marathon]] and [[e:battle-of-salamis|Salamis]], then led the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. Under [[e:pericles|Pericles]] it built the [[e:parthenon|Parthenon]] and staged the plays of [[e:aeschylus|Aeschylus]], [[e:sophocles|Sophocles]] and [[e:euripides|Euripides]], funded by [[e:silver|silver]] from [[e:laurion|Laurion]].
athens.e: Defeat by [[s:sparta|Sparta]] in 404 BCE ended its empire, though it led the [[s:second-athenian-league|Second Athenian League]] until [[e:battle-of-chaeronea-338-bce|Chaeronea]] in 338 BCE. Under Macedonian and Roman influence it remained a centre of philosophy. After it sided with [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates]], [[e:sulla|Sulla]] sacked Athens in 86 BCE.

amphictyonic-league.t: Ancient religious association of Greek peoples that managed the sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi and repeatedly declared sacred wars that drew in the great powers.
amphictyonic-league.o: An amphictyony was a league of neighbours sharing a sanctuary. This one began at the shrine of [[e:demeter|Demeter]] at [[e:anthela|Anthela]] near [[e:battle-of-thermopylae|Thermopylae]] and extended its care to [[s:delphi|Delphi]]. Its role became prominent in the [[e:first-sacred-war|First Sacred War]], traditionally c. 595-585 BCE, when members destroyed the town of [[e:kirrha|Kirrha]] for abusing pilgrims and then reorganised the [[e:pythian-games|Pythian Games]] in 582 BCE.
amphictyonic-league.r: Twelve peoples, among them the Thessalians, Phocians, [[e:boeotia|Boeotians]], [[e:dorians|Dorians]] and [[e:ionians|Ionians]], each sent two delegates (hieromnemones) to a council meeting twice a year at [[e:anthela|Anthela]] and [[s:delphi|Delphi]]. The council looked after temple property and finances, the [[e:pythian-games|Pythian Games]] and the sacred land, and could fine or declare war on offenders. Powerful states used its votes to dress political aims as piety.
amphictyonic-league.e: The [[e:third-sacred-war|Third Sacred War]] against [[e:phocis|Phocis]] (356-346 BCE) brought [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II of Macedon]] onto the council, and the Fourth (339 BCE) led to his victory at [[e:battle-of-chaeronea-338-bce|Chaeronea]]. The [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]] dominated it in the 3rd century BCE. Augustus reorganised its membership, and it lingered as a religious body into the 2nd century CE.
amphictyonic-league.re: Ancient Greek religion (cult of Apollo and Demeter)

achaean-league.t: Federation of Peloponnesian cities that grew under Aratus and Philopoemen to unite the whole Peloponnese before its destruction by Rome in 146 BCE.
achaean-league.o: An older league of the small cities of [[e:achaea|Achaea]] on the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]] had collapsed under Macedonian rule. In 280 BCE four cities, [[s:dyme|Dyme]], [[s:patrae|Patrae]], Tritaia and Pharai, refounded it. [[e:aratus-of-sicyon|Aratus]] brought in [[s:sicyon|Sicyon]] in 251 BCE and seized [[e:acrocorinth|Acrocorinth]] from the Macedonians in 243 BCE, making the league a major power.
achaean-league.r: Members kept local government but shared citizenship, coinage, weights and foreign policy. Assemblies met at [[s:aegium|Aigion]], electing an annual general ([[e:strategos|strategos]]), who could not serve consecutive terms. [[e:polybius|Polybius]], himself an Achaean, praised it as a model of federal union. Under [[e:philopoemen|Philopoemen]] it absorbed [[s:sparta|Sparta]], [[s:messene|Messene]] and [[s:elis|Elis]], uniting the [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]] by 191 BCE.
achaean-league.e: War with [[e:cleomenes-iii|Cleomenes III]] forced [[e:aratus-of-sicyon|Aratus]] to invite back [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] later used disputes over [[s:sparta|Sparta]] to intervene; in 146 BCE the league declared war, and [[e:lucius-mummius-achaicus|Lucius Mummius]] destroyed [[s:corinth|Corinth]]. The league was dissolved, revived later only as a minor body.

abydos.t: Milesian colony at the narrowest point of the Hellespont, where Xerxes bridged the strait and where legend placed the love of Hero and Leander.
abydos.o: Settlers from [[s:miletus|Miletus]] founded Abydos c. 680 BCE on the Asian shore of the [[e:hellespont|Hellespont]], at the narrows opposite [[s:sestos|Sestos]], with the agreement of the Lydian king [[e:gyges-of-lydia|Gyges]]. Its position controlled the crossing between [[e:europe|Europe]] and [[e:asia-roman-province|Asia]] and the passage of ships to the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]].
abydos.r: Abydos lived from trade and fishing. In 480 BCE [[e:xerxes-i|Xerxes]] built his boat bridges across the strait near the city. It joined the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] but revolted in 411 BCE, becoming a Spartan base, and the [[e:battle-of-abydos|Battle of Abydos]] was fought off its shore that year. Greek legend set the story of [[e:hero-and-leander|Leander]], who swam to Hero at [[s:sestos|Sestos]], here.
abydos.e: In 200 BCE [[e:philip-v-of-macedon|Philip V]] of the [[s:antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia|Antigonid Kingdom of Macedonia]] besieged Abydos; rather than surrender, many citizens killed their families and themselves. [[e:rome|Rome]] later freed it, and it joined the province of Asia in 129 BCE.

ancient-veneti.t: Iron Age people of north-eastern Italy, centred on Ateste and Patavium, famed for horse-breeding and bronze work, who became Rome's peaceful allies and gave their name to Venice.
ancient-veneti.o: The [[s:veneti|Veneti]] emerged in the plain between the Po, the [[e:adige|Adige]] and the [[e:alps|Alps]] in the early 1st millennium BCE, forming the [[e:este-veneto|Este]] culture from about 1000 BCE. Greek and Roman writers linked them to the Eneti of [[s:kingdom-of-paphlagonia|Paphlagonia]] or to Trojan refugees under [[e:antenor|Antenor]], legends [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]] later embraced, but archaeology shows a mainly local development.
ancient-veneti.r: Their main centres were [[e:este-veneto|Ateste]] (Este), [[e:padua|Patavium]] ([[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]]), [[e:vicenza|Vicetia]] and [[e:altinum|Altinum]], each probably self-governing. They wrote [[e:venetic|Venetic]], an [[e:indo-european-languages|Indo-European]] language, in an alphabet adapted from Etruscan, known from hundreds of votive inscriptions. [[e:bronze|Bronze]] situlae decorated with processions and banquets, amber trade from the Baltic, and celebrated [[e:horse-breeding|horse-breeding]] marked their culture; the healing goddess [[e:reitia|Reitia]] had a major sanctuary at Este.
ancient-veneti.e: Hostile to the [[e:gaul|Gauls]], the [[s:veneti|Veneti]] allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] from the 3rd century BCE and were absorbed gradually and without conquest. [[e:latin|Latin]] replaced [[e:venetic|Venetic]], and Caesar's grant of citizenship in 49 BCE completed integration. Their name lived on in the Roman region of [[e:venetia|Venetia]] et [[s:histria|Histria]] and, through it, in [[e:venice|Venice]] and the [[e:veneto|Veneto]].

cr.a: Dbachmann; derivative work by Ewan ar born translator: Manlleus (ca)

antipatrid-kingdom-of-macedonia.t: Macedon under Cassander, son of Antipater, who ended Alexander the Great's line, founded Thessalonica and briefly passed the throne to his sons.
antipatrid-kingdom-of-macedonia.o: After the regent [[e:antipater|Antipater]] died in 319 BCE, his son [[e:cassander|Cassander]] fought [[e:polyperchon|Polyperchon]] and [[e:olympias|Olympias]] for [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] and won control by 316 BCE, executing [[e:olympia|Olympias]]. He married Alexander's half-sister [[e:thessalonike-of-macedon|Thessalonike]]. Around 310 BCE he had [[e:alexander-iv-of-macedon|Alexander IV]] and his mother [[e:roxana|Roxane]] killed, and in 305 BCE took the title of king.
antipatrid-kingdom-of-macedonia.r: [[e:cassander|Cassander]] ruled from [[s:pella|Pella]] with the support of the Macedonian aristocracy, controlling much of [[e:greece|Greece]] through garrisons and friendly governments, such as that of [[e:demetrius-of-phalerum|Demetrius of Phalerum]] at [[s:athens|Athens]]. He refounded [[s:thebes|Thebes]] and founded [[e:thessaloniki|Thessalonica]] and [[s:potidaea|Cassandreia]], the latter on the site of Potidaea. He was an ally of [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]], [[e:seleucus-i-nicator|Seleucus]] and Ptolemy against [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus]] I.
antipatrid-kingdom-of-macedonia.e: [[e:cassander|Cassander]] died in 297 BCE. His son [[e:philip-iv-of-macedon|Philip IV]] died soon after, and the brothers [[e:antipater|Antipater]] II and Alexander V fought over the throne. [[e:demetrius-i-of-macedon|Demetrius Poliorcetes]], called in by Alexander V, murdered him in 294 BCE and took [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]], ending the dynasty and opening the way for the [[s:antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia|Antigonid Kingdom of Macedonia]].

cr.a: Marsyas (French original); Kordas (Spanish translation); derivative work by MinisterForBadTimes

audhali-sultanate.t: A highland sultanate north-east of Aden and a founding member of the British-backed Federation of Arab Emirates of the South.
audhali-sultanate.o: The Audhali tribe held the Kawr al-Awadhil plateau and the plain below it, north-east of [[e:aden|Aden]]. Its sultans, based at [[e:zadar|Zara]], emerged as an independent local power around 1800, after the authority of the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] in the south had faded.
audhali-sultanate.r: The sultanate was a tribal state with little formal administration, its people farming the high plateau and controlling routes from the coast inland. It entered British protection in the late 19th century as part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. In 1959 it was one of the six founding members of the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]], and its rulers held posts in the federal government.
audhali-sultanate.e: After the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]] collapsed in 1967, the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over the territory, abolished the sultanate and incorporated it into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

awlad-mbarak-emirate.t: A Hassani Arab emirate of the Hodh in south-eastern Mauritania, a desert-edge power that raided and traded with the Bambara kingdoms of the Sahel.
awlad-mbarak-emirate.o: The Awlad Mbarak were a Hassani warrior group, part of the Arab [[e:banu-hassan|Bani Hassan]] who had spread across the western [[e:sahara|Sahara]]. By the 17th century they dominated the [[e:hodh|Hodh]] region, in present-day south-eastern [[e:mauritania|Mauritania]] and western [[e:mali|Mali]].
awlad-mbarak-emirate.r: Little is documented in detail. The [[e:emir|emirs]] led warrior lineages that took tribute from [[e:berbers|Berber]] scholarly tribes, [[e:fula|Fulani]] herders and [[e:soninke|Soninke]] and [[e:bambara-people|Bambara]] farmers. They traded salt, gum and livestock, and fought or allied with the [[s:kingdom-of-kaarta|Kingdom of Kaarta]] and other Sahelian states.
awlad-mbarak-emirate.e: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] declined in the 19th century under pressure from rival Hassani groups and [[s:kingdom-of-kaarta|Kaarta]]. By around 1860 it had lost its power, and the [[e:hodh|Hodh]] later passed under [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]] and [[s:french-mauritania|French Mauritania]].

arab-kingdom-of-syria.t: A short-lived Arab kingdom, proclaimed in Damascus under Faisal in 1920 and destroyed by France within months.
arab-kingdom-of-syria.o: Faisal, son of the [[e:sharif-of-mecca|Sharif of Mecca]], entered [[e:damascus|Damascus]] in October 1918 with the Arab army of the revolt against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and set up a government under the British-led [[s:occupied-enemy-territory-administration|Occupied Enemy Territory Administration]]. On 8 March 1920 the [[e:syrian-national-congress|Syrian National Congress]] proclaimed him king of an independent [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] including [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanon]] and [[e:palestine|Palestine]].
arab-kingdom-of-syria.r: The government drew on Arab nationalist officers and notables, many of them former Ottoman officials. The Congress drafted a constitution for a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]], with [[e:hashim-al-atassi|Hashim al-Atassi]] as prime minister. The state's control was limited to the inland cities, and its finances depended on British [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] that ended in 1919.
arab-kingdom-of-syria.e: The [[e:san-remo-conference|San Remo conference]] gave [[e:france|France]] the mandate for [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] in April 1920. France sent an ultimatum, and on 24 July 1920 its army defeated the Syrian force at [[e:battle-of-maysalun|Maysalun]], where the war minister [[e:yusuf-al-azma|Yusuf al-Azma]] was killed. Faisal was expelled and became king of [[e:iraq|Iraq]] in 1921.

amb-state.t: The Tanoli chiefship of Tanawal on the upper Indus, one of the last princely states of Pakistan, abolished in 1969.
amb-state.o: The [[e:tanoli|Tanolis]], a tribe of the [[e:hazara|Hazara]] hills, held Tanawal on the left bank of the [[e:indus|Indus]]. Around 1772 their chiefs established a ruling house based at Amb and later at [[e:derbent|Darband]]. [[e:paynda-khan-tanoli|Paynda Khan Tanoli]] resisted the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]] in the early 19th century.
amb-state.r: Under the British, Amb was a small internally autonomous state on the [[e:north-west-frontier-province|North-West Frontier]], with the Nawab ruling the trans-[[e:indus|Indus]] enclave while the family held Tanawal as an estate in British [[e:hazara|Hazara]]. The population was Muslim and spoke [[e:hindko|Hindko]] and [[e:pashto|Pashto]].
amb-state.e: Nawab Muhammad Farid Khan acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1947. The state was abolished in 1969 and merged into the [[e:north-west-frontier-province|North-West Frontier Province]], and much of its lowland, including old [[e:derbent|Darband]], was later flooded by the [[e:tarbela-dam|Tarbela Dam]].

araucania.t: The lands of the Mapuche south of the Biobío river, which resisted Spanish conquest for three centuries and kept their independence until the 1880s.
araucania.o: When [[e:pedro-de-valdivia|Pedro de Valdivia]] advanced south from [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] in 1550, the [[e:mapuche|Mapuche]] of the region between the [[e:biobio-river|Biobío]] and [[e:tolten-river|Toltén]] rivers rose against him. Under leaders such as [[e:lautaro|Lautaro]] and [[e:caupolican|Caupolicán]] they defeated and killed [[e:valdivia|Valdivia]] at [[e:battle-of-tucapel|Tucapel]] in 1553, beginning the long [[e:arauco-war|Arauco War]].
araucania.r: The [[e:mapuche|Mapuche]] had no central state. Each lineage was led by a lonko, and groups united under war leaders called toqui in times of conflict. After the victory at [[e:battle-of-curalaba|Curalaba]] in 1598, Mapuche forces destroyed the Spanish towns south of the [[e:biobio-river|Biobío]]. At the [[e:parliament-of-quillin|Parliament of Quillín]] in 1641 [[e:spain|Spain]] recognised the river as the frontier, and later parlamentos regulated trade and peace. The Mapuche adopted horses and [[e:cattle|cattle]] and traded across the [[s:andecavi|Andes]] into the pampas.
araucania.e: Independent [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] carried out the [[e:occupation-of-araucania|Occupation of Araucanía]] from 1861 to 1883, while [[e:argentina|Argentina's]] [[e:conquest-of-the-desert|Conquest of the Desert]] subdued the [[e:mapuche|Mapuche]] east of the [[s:andecavi|Andes]]. Mapuche lands were confiscated and confined to reservations, and land claims remain a major political issue.

ayyubid-yemen.t: Yemen as a dominion of Saladin's family, which ended its many local dynasties and made Ta'izz a royal centre.
ayyubid-yemen.o: In 1174 [[e:saladin|Saladin]] sent his brother [[e:turan-shah-ibn-ayyub|Turan-Shah]] with an army to [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]]. He defeated the [[s:mahdid-dynasty|Mahdid dynasty]] at [[e:zabid|Zabid]], took [[e:aden|Aden]] from the [[s:zurayid-dynasty|Zurayid dynasty]] and pressed the [[s:hamdanid-sultanate-of-yemen|Hamdanid sultanate of Yemen]], uniting the lowlands and much of the south under the [[s:ayyubid-empire|Ayyubid Empire]].
ayyubid-yemen.r: [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]] was ruled by Ayyubid princes as a valuable dependency, profiting from [[e:aden|Aden's]] customs and the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] trade. [[e:tughtakin-ibn-ayyub|Tughtakin ibn Ayyub]], ruler from 1182 to 1197, consolidated control, took Sanaa and made [[e:taiz|Ta'izz]] an important base. The [[e:ayyubid-empire|Ayyubids]] promoted [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni Islam]], founded [[e:madrasa|madrasas]] and introduced Kurdish and Turkic troops. The Zaydi [[e:imam|imams]] resisted in the northern highlands.
ayyubid-yemen.e: In 1229 the last Ayyubid ruler, [[e:al-masud-yusuf|al-Mas'ud Yusuf]], left for [[e:egypt|Egypt]], appointing his commander [[e:nur-al-din-umar-ibn-rasul|Nur al-Din Umar ibn Rasul]] as deputy. [[e:nur-al-din|Nur al-Din]] soon declared independence, founding the [[s:rasulid-dynasty|Rasulid dynasty]].

auteini.t: People of western Ireland named by Ptolemy, usually placed in Galway or Mayo and possibly linked with the later Uaithni.
auteini.o: The Auteini, or Autini, are listed in [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 on the west coast of Ireland, between the [[s:nagnatae|Nagnatae]] to the north and the [[s:gangani-ireland|Gangani (Ireland)]] to the south, roughly in modern [[e:galway|Galway]] or [[e:county-mayo|Mayo]]. Ptolemy's Irish data came from earlier maritime reports and are imprecise.
auteini.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or society. Their name is often compared with the Uaithni, a population group recorded in early medieval Ireland in north [[e:county-tipperary|Tipperary]] and [[e:limerick|Limerick]], which could indicate a later movement south or a mistaken placing by Ptolemy, but the identification remains conjecture.
auteini.e: The Auteini do not appear in later records. The west of Ireland where Ptolemy placed them later formed part of the [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Kingdom of Connacht]].

ayyubids-of-hisn-kayfa.t: The last surviving branch of the Ayyubid dynasty, ruling the Tigris town of Hasankeyf for nearly three centuries.
ayyubids-of-hisn-kayfa.o: In 1232 the Ayyubid sultan [[e:al-kamil|al-Kamil]] took [[e:hasankeyf|Hisn Kayfa]] and Amid from the [[s:artuqids-of-hasankeyf|Artuqids of Hasankeyf]] and gave them to his son [[e:as-salih-ayyub|al-Salih Ayyub]]. When al-[[s:salihids|Salih]] Ayyub went on to [[e:egypt|Egypt]], a junior line of the family remained in Hasankeyf.
ayyubids-of-hisn-kayfa.r: [[e:as-salih-ayyub|Al-Salih Ayyub's]] son [[e:turanshah|Turanshah]] left [[e:hasankeyf|Hasankeyf]] in 1249 to take the throne in [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and was murdered by the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] in 1250. The princes who stayed survived as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:mongols|Mongols]], the [[e:ilkhanate|Ilkhanids]], the [[s:qara-qoyunlu|Qara Qoyunlu]] and the [[s:aq-qoyunlu|Aq Qoyunlu]]. They built in Hasankeyf, including the [[e:el-rizk-mosque|El Rizk]] mosque of [[e:al-adil|al-Adil]] Sulayman in 1409, and ruled a mixed Kurdish, Arab and Christian population.
ayyubids-of-hisn-kayfa.e: The dynasty was ended in the early 16th century as the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] took over the region from the [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]], its last princes being absorbed into the Ottoman system. Much of [[e:hasankeyf|Hasankeyf]] was flooded by the [[e:ilisu-dam|Ilisu Dam]] in 2020.

acalan.t: A Chontal Maya trading kingdom on the Candelaria river in Campeche, where the last Aztec ruler Cuauhtemoc was executed in 1525.
acalan.o: Acalan, meaning 'place of canoes' in [[e:nahuatl|Nahuatl]], was the land of the [[e:chontal-maya|Chontal Maya]] (Mactun) along the Candelaria river south of the [[e:laguna-de-terminos|Laguna de Términos]]. Its dynasty, recorded in the Chontal text of the [[e:paxbolon-maldonado-papers|Paxbolon-Maldonado papers]], traced its origins to the 14th century, when its rulers settled at Itzamkanac.
acalan.r: Acalan was a merchant state whose canoes carried [[e:cacao|cacao]], cloth, salt and other goods along the Gulf coast between central [[s:mexico|Mexico]] and [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]], and its ruler was said to be the wealthiest merchant of the land. Itzamkanac was a large town with many temples, and the kingdom controlled scattered dependent settlements.
acalan.e: In 1525 [[e:hernan-cortes|Hernán Cortés]] passed through on his march to [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] and executed Cuauhtemoc there. Acalan submitted to Spanish rule under [[e:paxbolonacha|Paxbolonacha]], and in 1557 the population was moved to Tixchel on the coast; Itzamkanac was later abandoned.

a-group-chiefdom-of-qustul.t: An A-Group chiefdom in Lower Nubia whose rich royal tombs at Qustul rivalled those of predynastic Egypt.
a-group-chiefdom-of-qustul.o: The [[e:a-group-culture|A-Group]] people lived in [[e:lower-nubia|Lower Nubia]], between the First and Second Cataracts, from about 3800 BCE. By c. 3300 BCE a ruling elite had emerged around [[e:qustul|Qustul]], near the modern Egypt-[[e:sudan|Sudan]] border, growing rich as middlemen in the trade between [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and the south in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], [[e:ebony|ebony]], [[e:incense|incense]] and animal skins.
a-group-chiefdom-of-qustul.r: Cemetery L at [[e:qustul|Qustul]] contains large tombs with Egyptian stone vessels, imported pottery and gold. A carved [[e:incense|incense]] burner shows a crowned figure resembling an Egyptian king, which led some scholars to argue that pharaonic kingship began here; most now see an elite sharing Upper Egyptian symbols. The [[e:a-group-culture|A-Group]] made fine, thin-walled painted pottery and lived by herding, farming and trade.
a-group-chiefdom-of-qustul.e: Around 3000 to 2900 BCE the kings of [[s:early-dynastic-egypt|Early Dynastic Egypt]] campaigned into [[e:nubia|Nubia]], and a rock inscription at [[e:gebel-sheikh-suleiman|Gebel Sheikh Suleiman]] records an attack. The [[e:a-group-culture|A-Group]] then disappears and [[e:lower-nubia|Lower Nubia]] appears thinly settled until the [[e:c-group-culture|C-Group]] arrived. [[e:egyptians|Egyptians]] long called the region Ta-Seti, '[[e:land-of-the-bow|Land of the Bow]]'.

autonomous-republic-of-northern-epirus.t: Short-lived republic declared in 1914 by the Greek population of southern Albania, which won autonomy before the First World War overtook it.
autonomous-republic-of-northern-epirus.o: The [[e:balkan-wars|Balkan Wars]] of 1912-1913 left Greek troops in southern [[s:albania|Albania]], a region with a large Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] population that [[e:greeks|Greeks]] called Northern [[e:epirus|Epirus]]. The Protocol of [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] in December 1913 assigned it to the new state of Albania. Rejecting this, local leaders proclaimed an autonomous republic at [[e:gjirokaster|Gjirokaster]] in February 1914, led by [[e:georgios-christakis-zografos|Georgios Christakis-Zografos]].
autonomous-republic-of-northern-epirus.r: The provisional government raised its own armed units, issued stamps and fought Albanian gendarmerie for control of the region. In May 1914 the Protocol of [[s:corcyra|Corfu]], accepted by the Albanian government and the great powers, gave the region extensive autonomy within [[s:albania|Albania]], with Greek-language schools and [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] religious rights.
autonomous-republic-of-northern-epirus.e: The Protocol of [[s:corcyra|Corfu]] was never fully put into effect. With the outbreak of the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] and Albania's collapse, the Greek army occupied the region in October 1914, ending the republic. The area was returned to [[s:albania|Albania]] after the war.

arghun-dynasty.t: A Turko-Mongol dynasty from Kandahar that conquered Sindh from the Sammas in the early 16th century.
arghun-dynasty.o: The [[e:arghun|Arghuns]], Turko-Mongol nobles who had served the [[e:timurid-empire|Timurid]] rulers of [[e:herat|Herat]], held [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] until [[e:babur|Babur]] drove them out in the 1510s. Their leader [[e:shah-beg-arghun|Shah Beg Arghun]] turned south, defeated the [[s:samma-dynasty|Samma dynasty]] in 1520 and established his rule in upper [[e:sindh|Sindh]], with the fortress of [[e:bukkur|Bhakkar]] on the [[e:indus|Indus]] as a key base.
arghun-dynasty.r: [[e:shah-beg-arghun|Shah Beg]]'s son [[e:shah-husain-arghun|Shah Husain Arghun]] extended [[e:arghun|Arghun]] power to [[e:thatta|Thatta]] in lower [[e:sindh|Sindh]] and north to [[e:multan|Multan]], which he took from the [[s:langah-sultanate|Langah Sultanate]]. He opposed the fugitive Mughal emperor [[e:humayun|Humayun]], who wandered in Sindh from 1541 to 1543 and failed to take Arghun strongholds. Arghun rule depended on Central Asian soldiers and was harsh on the local Samma and Soomra nobility.
arghun-dynasty.e: In 1554, as the ailing [[e:shah-husain-arghun|Shah Husain]] lost control, his officer [[e:mirza-isa-tarkhan|Mirza Isa Tarkhan]] seized [[e:thatta|Thatta]] and founded the [[s:tarkhan-dynasty|Tarkhan dynasty]] in lower [[e:sindh|Sindh]]. Shah Husain died childless in 1556, and upper Sindh later fell to the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]].

akshak.t: A northern Sumerian city near Kish whose rulers briefly held kingship and fought Lagash in the Early Dynastic period.
akshak.o: Akshak lay in northern [[e:babylonia|Babylonia]] near the [[e:tigris|Tigris]], probably close to later Upi ([[e:opis|Opis]]), though the site has not been securely identified. It appears in the Early Dynastic III period as one of the cities competing with [[s:kish|Kish]] for dominance in the north.
akshak.r: The [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] records a dynasty of Akshak of six kings, including Puzur-Nirah, said to have held kingship over [[e:sumer|Sumer]]. Contemporary evidence is scarce: [[e:eannatum|Eannatum of Lagash]] claims to have defeated Zuzu, king of Akshak, around 2450 BCE. Nothing is known of its internal government, and its rulers seem to have contested control of the north with [[s:kish|Kish]] and [[s:mari|Mari]].
akshak.e: Akshak was absorbed by [[s:kish|Kish]] and then by the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]] around 2334 BCE. The name survives in later texts mainly as a place name; whether it was the same city as Upi is still debated.

aydinids.t: An Aegean beylik whose fleets under Umur Bey raided the Greek world and provoked a crusade against Smyrna.
aydinids.o: [[e:aydinoglu-mehmed-bey|Mehmed Bey]], a commander in the service of the [[s:germiyanids|Germiyanids]], conquered [[e:birgi|Birgi]], [[e:ephesus|Ayasoluk]] ([[s:ephesus|Ephesus]]) and the upper [[s:smyrna|Smyrna]] citadel from the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] in the first decade of the 14th century and founded his own [[e:beylik|beylik]], with Birgi as capital.
aydinids.r: [[e:aydinoglu-mehmed-bey|Mehmed]]'s son [[e:umur-bey|Umur Bey]] built a fleet at [[s:smyrna|Smyrna]] and raided the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] islands, [[e:greece|Greece]] and the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]], and as an ally of [[e:john-vi-kantakouzenos|John VI Kantakouzenos]] fought in the Byzantine civil war. In 1344 a crusading league took Smyrna's harbour castle, founding [[s:crusader-smyrna|Crusader Smyrna]], and Umur was killed trying to retake it in 1348. [[e:ephesus|Ayasoluk]] prospered from Italian trade, and Isa Bey built the [[e:isa-bey-mosque|Isa Bey Mosque]] there in 1375.
aydinids.e: [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]] annexed the [[e:beylik|beylik]] in 1390, [[e:timur|Timur]] restored it in 1402, and after the resistance of [[e:cuneyd-bey|Cuneyd Bey]] the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] took it finally in 1425-1426.

albici.t: Hardy mountain people of upper Provence who fought for Massalia against Caesar's siege in 49 BCE.
albici.o: The Albici lived in the hills north of [[s:massalia|Massalia]], probably around the plateau of [[e:plateau-dalbion|Albion]] and the area of [[e:riez|Riez]], whose Roman name Alebaece Reiorum may preserve theirs. Caesar describes them as old clients of Massalia.
albici.r: Caesar calls them barbarians living in the mountains above [[s:massalia|Massilia]], under the protection of the Greek city, and praises their courage. No rulers or institutions are recorded.
albici.e: In 49 BCE the Massaliots brought the Albici into the city as defenders against Caesar's [[e:legatus|legates]], but the siege ended in surrender. Their land was then absorbed into [[e:gallia-narbonensis|Gallia Narbonensis]].

alchon-huns.t: A Hunnic people who ruled Kabulistan and Gandhara and invaded northern India, remembered in Indian tradition for the destructive kings Toramana and Mihirakula.
alchon-huns.o: The Alchon [[e:huns|Huns]] emerged in [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] in the late 4th century, probably among the Hunnic groups that followed the [[s:chionites|Chionites]] and [[s:kidarite-kingdom|Kidarites]]. They first issued coins copying the Sasanian king [[e:shapur-ii|Shapur II]], then moved south of the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]], taking [[e:kabul|Kabul]] and later replacing the Kidarites in [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]] in the mid-5th century.
alchon-huns.r: Known mainly from coins with their distinctive elongated skulls and the Bactrian word 'alchono', and from Indian inscriptions, they ruled as warrior kings over a settled population. Around 500 [[e:toramana|Toramana]] invaded the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]], reaching central [[e:india|India]], as recorded at [[e:eran|Eran]]. His son [[e:mihirakula|Mihirakula]] ruled from [[s:sakala|Sakala]] and was remembered by Buddhist writers such as [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] as a persecutor who destroyed monasteries.
alchon-huns.e: [[e:mihirakula|Mihirakula]] was defeated around 528 by the Indian king [[e:yasodharman|Yasodharman]] and possibly by the [[e:gupta-empire|Guptas]], and Alchon power retreated to [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] and [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]]. By the mid-6th century their rule faded, and they were succeeded in the [[e:kabul|Kabul]] region by the [[s:nezak-huns|Nezak Huns]].

abydos-dynasty.t: A small, debated local dynasty at Abydos in the Second Intermediate Period, made real by the 2014 discovery of King Senebkay's tomb.
abydos-dynasty.o: In 1997 the Egyptologist [[e:kim-ryholt|Kim Ryholt]] proposed that a group of kings in the [[e:turin-king-list|Turin King List]] ruled a local kingdom at [[s:abydos|Abydos]] around 1650 BCE, after the collapse of the [[s:middle-kingdom-of-egypt|Middle Kingdom of Egypt]]. The idea remains debated, but it was strengthened in 2014 when [[e:josef-wegner|Josef Wegner's]] team found the tomb of a previously unknown king, [[e:senebkay|Senebkay]], at Abydos.
abydos-dynasty.r: Almost nothing is known of its government. The kings ruled a narrow stretch of [[e:middle-egypt|Middle Egypt]] around [[s:abydos|Abydos]] and [[e:thinis|Thinis]], the cult centre of [[e:osiris|Osiris]]. [[e:senebkay|Senebkay's]] modest tomb reused materials from older monuments, and his skeleton bears battle wounds, perhaps from fighting the [[s:fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt|Hyksos]].
abydos-dynasty.e: The kingdom probably fell by around 1600 BCE, absorbed by the [[s:sixteenth-dynasty-of-egypt|Theban Sixteenth Dynasty]] of [[e:egypt|Egypt]] or overrun by the [[s:fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt|Hyksos]].

artuqids-of-mardin.t: The longest-lived branch of the Artuqid dynasty, ruling the hilltop city of Mardin for three centuries under Seljuk, Ayyubid and Mongol overlords.
artuqids-of-mardin.o: [[e:ilghazi|Ilghazi]], son of the [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] commander [[e:artuq-ibn-ekseb|Artuq]], took [[e:mardin|Mardin]] in the early 12th century and made it the base of his branch of the family. In 1118 he also gained [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]], and in 1119 he destroyed the army of the [[s:principality-of-antioch|Principality of Antioch]] at the [[e:battle-of-ager-sanguinis|Field of Blood]].
artuqids-of-mardin.r: His son [[e:husam-al-din-timurtash|Timurtash]] and later rulers held [[e:mardin|Mardin]] and [[e:mayyafariqin|Mayyafariqin]], survived by accepting Zengid, Ayyubid and then Ilkhanid overlordship, and kept their dynasty intact through repeated invasions. Mardin, terraced on a steep hill, gained mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]], notably the [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Isa or [[e:zinciriye-madrasa|Zinciriye Madrasa]] of 1385. The region was home to many [[e:syriac-christians|Syriac Christians]], including the patriarchal monastery of [[e:deyrulzafaran-monastery|Deyrulzafaran]].
artuqids-of-mardin.e: [[e:timur|Timur]] took [[e:mardin|Mardin's]] lower city in 1394 and 1401. The last [[e:artuqid-dynasty|Artuqids]] were displaced by the [[s:qara-qoyunlu|Qara Qoyunlu]] leader [[e:qara-yusuf|Qara Yusuf]] in 1409, and Mardin later passed to the [[s:aq-qoyunlu|Aq Qoyunlu]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].

archduchy-of-austria.t: The Habsburg heartland on the Danube, raised to an archduchy in 1453, around which the dynasty built its great central European monarchy.
archduchy-of-austria.o: The [[s:duchy-of-austria|Duchy of Austria]] had been held by the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] since 1278. Duke [[e:rudolf-iv-duke-of-austria|Rudolf IV]] forged the [[e:privilegium-maius|Privilegium Maius]] around 1358, claiming the title of archduke. In 1453 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]], himself a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]], confirmed the forgery, giving the rulers of [[e:austria|Austria]] the rank of archduke and special privileges.
archduchy-of-austria.r: The archduchy, divided into [[e:austria|Austria]] below and above the [[e:enns-river|Enns]], was governed from [[e:vienna|Vienna]], where strong estates of nobles, clergy and towns met in diets. Its archdukes were usually also emperors. Much of the nobility turned Protestant in the 16th century but was forced back to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] after 1620. Vienna withstood Ottoman sieges in 1529 and 1683.
archduchy-of-austria.e: From 1526 the archduchy formed the core of the [[s:habsburg-monarchy|Habsburg Monarchy]]. In 1804 [[e:francis-ii|Francis II]] proclaimed the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]], in which the archduchy remained a crown land until 1918; its territory now forms the federal states of [[e:lower-austria|Lower Austria]], [[e:upper-austria|Upper Austria]] and [[e:vienna|Vienna]].

artuqids-of-harput.t: A branch of the Artuqid dynasty at the fortress of Harput, where Belek Ghazi held the King of Jerusalem captive.
artuqids-of-harput.o: [[e:harput|Harput]], a fortress near the upper [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]], came under [[e:artuqid-dynasty|Artuqid]] rule early in the 12th century. Its most famous holder was [[e:belek-ghazi|Belek Ghazi]], a nephew of [[e:ilghazi|Ilghazi]], who captured [[e:joscelin-i-count-of-edessa|Joscelin I]] of the [[s:county-of-edessa|County of Edessa]] in 1122 and King [[e:baldwin-ii-of-jerusalem|Baldwin II of Jerusalem]] in 1123 and imprisoned them there.
artuqids-of-harput.r: Armenian sympathisers briefly seized [[e:harput|Harput]] castle to free the captives in 1123, but [[e:belek-ghazi|Belek]] retook it. He was killed besieging [[e:manbij|Manbij]] in 1124. Harput then belonged to the [[s:artuqids-of-hasankeyf|Artuqids of Hasankeyf]] until a separate line was established in 1185 by [[e:imad-al-din-abu-bakr|Imad al-Din Abu Bakr]]. The small [[e:emirate|emirate]] built mosques, notably the [[e:harput-ulu-mosque|Ulu Cami of Harput]].
artuqids-of-harput.e: Squeezed between the [[e:ayyubid-empire|Ayyubids]] and the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]], the [[e:harput|Harput]] branch was annexed by the Seljuk sultan [[e:kayqubad-i|Kayqubad I]] in 1234.

angevin-empire.t: The vast assemblage of lands ruled by Henry II and his sons, from the Scottish border to the Pyrenees, which collapsed in the wars with Philip II.
angevin-empire.o: [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]] inherited [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]], [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]] and [[e:touraine|Touraine]] from his father [[e:geoffrey-plantagenet-count-of-anjou|Geoffrey Plantagenet]] and [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] through his mother Matilda, gained [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] by marrying [[e:eleanor-of-aquitaine|Eleanor of Aquitaine]] in 1152, and became king of [[e:england|England]] in 1154. He also asserted lordship over Ireland from 1171 and over [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]] through his son Geoffrey.
angevin-empire.r: There was no single government: each land kept its own customs, though Henry built strong royal justice in [[e:england|England]] and moved constantly between his territories. [[e:chinon|Chinon]] was a favourite residence and treasury. [[e:prince-henry-the-navigator|Henry's]] sons rebelled repeatedly, backed by the French kings. [[e:richard-i-of-england|Richard I]] spent most of his reign on [[e:crusade|crusade]] and in [[e:france|France]], building [[e:chateau-gaillard|Château Gaillard]] to guard [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]].
angevin-empire.e: [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] lost [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]], [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]] and [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]] to [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II]] in 1202–1204, and his allies' defeat at [[e:battle-of-bouvines|Bouvines]] in 1214 ended hopes of recovery. [[e:england|England]] kept [[e:gascony|Gascony]], and the term Angevin Empire was coined by modern historians.

armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia.t: An Armenian kingdom on the Mediterranean that allied with Crusaders and Mongols and was the last independent Armenian state of the Middle Ages.
armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia.o: Around 1080, as Byzantine rule in the East collapsed, the Armenian lord [[e:ruben-i-prince-of-armenia|Ruben]] established himself in the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] mountains of [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]]. His [[e:rubenid-dynasty|Rubenid]] descendants expanded into the Cilician plain, and in 1198 [[e:leo-i-king-of-armenia|Leo I]] was crowned king with the blessing of the [[e:holy-roman-emperor|Holy Roman Emperor]] and the pope.
armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia.r: [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]] combined Armenian traditions with Frankish feudal institutions, titles and law, and its nobles intermarried with [[e:crusader-states|Crusader]] families. The port of [[e:ayas-cilicia|Ayas]] carried Venetian and Genoese trade in [[e:silk|silk]] and [[e:spice-trade|spices]]. [[e:hethum-i|Hethum I]] submitted to the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] and travelled to [[e:karakorum|Karakorum]] in 1254, allying with them against the [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluks]]. The kingdom produced fine illuminated [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]], notably those of [[e:toros-roslin|Toros Roslin]], while the Catholicos resided at [[e:hromkla|Hromkla]] and from 1293 at [[e:sis-cilicia|Sis]].
armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia.e: Repeated [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] invasions wore the kingdom down after Mongol power waned. In 1375 the [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluks]] took [[e:sis-cilicia|Sis]] and captured Leo V of the Lusignan line, who died in exile in [[e:paris|Paris]] in 1393. The title King of [[s:armenia|Armenia]] passed to the [[e:house-of-lusignan|Lusignans]] of [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]].

ancalites.t: British people named once by Julius Caesar among those who surrendered to him in 54 BCE, leading him to the stronghold of Cassivellaunus.
ancalites.o: The Ancalites are known only from [[e:commentarii-de-bello-gallico|Caesar's Gallic War]]. In 54 BCE they were among five British peoples, alongside the [[s:iceni|Cenimagni]], [[s:segontiaci|Segontiaci]], [[s:bibroci|Bibroci]] and [[s:cassi|Cassi]], who sent embassies to submit after the [[s:trinovantes|Trinovantes]] had won his protection.
ancalites.r: [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] says that from these envoys he learned the location of [[e:cassivellaunus|Cassivellaunus's]] stronghold, protected by woods and marshes, which he then stormed. Beyond this, nothing is recorded of their rulers, settlements or customs, and their territory is uncertain, though the upper [[e:river-thames|Thames]] valley has been suggested.
ancalites.e: No later source mentions the Ancalites. They were probably absorbed by stronger neighbours such as the [[s:catuvellauni|Catuvellauni]] or the [[s:atrebates-britain|Atrebates (Britain)]] in the century before the Roman conquest of 43.

albania.t: Present-day Albania, a parliamentary republic since the end of communism in 1991 and a NATO member seeking to join the European Union.
albania.o: Mass protests and emigration in 1990 forced the [[s:peoples-socialist-republic-of-albania|People's Socialist Republic of Albania]] to permit opposition parties. After the first multi-party elections, the country was renamed the Republic of Albania in April 1991. In 1992 the [[e:democratic-party-of-albania|Democratic Party]] of [[e:sali-berisha|Sali Berisha]] won power, ending communist rule.
albania.r: Albania is a parliamentary republic with a president elected by parliament. Religion returned to public life after decades of state atheism, and private enterprise and emigration transformed society. The collapse of pyramid investment schemes in 1997 caused near-anarchy and an international intervention. In 1999 Albania sheltered hundreds of thousands of refugees from [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]]. Politics has been dominated by the rivalry of the Democratic and [[e:socialist-party-of-albania|Socialist]] parties.
albania.e: Albania joined [[e:nato|NATO]] in 2009, became an EU candidate in 2014 and opened accession negotiations in 2022. [[e:edi-rama|Edi Rama's]] [[e:socialist-party-of-albania|Socialists]] have governed since 2013, and tourism has become a major industry.
albania.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

andorra.t: A Pyrenean co-principality created by a medieval agreement in 1278, still ruled jointly by the bishop of Urgell and the president of France.
andorra.o: Andorra's valleys had been held by the counts of Urgell and then the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of Urgell, whose rights were disputed by the counts of Foix. In 1278 Bishop [[e:pere-durtx|Pere d'Urtx]] and Count [[e:roger-bernard-iii-of-foix|Roger-Bernard III of Foix]] signed the first [[e:pareatges-of-andorra|Pareatge]], agreeing to share [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], and a second agreement followed in 1288.
andorra.r: The co-princes ruled through local representatives, and the valleys governed themselves through parishes and, from 1419, the [[e:consell-de-la-terra|Consell de la Terra]]. Andorrans lived from herding, farming and smuggling, kept Catalan as their language and [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] as their faith, and avoided entanglement in the wars of their neighbours.
andorra.e: The Foix rights passed to the kings of [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre]] and then the French crown, and so to the presidents of [[e:france|France]]. In the 20th century tourism and low taxes transformed the economy. A constitution in 1993 made Andorra a parliamentary co-principality, and it joined the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] that year.

aetolian-league.t: Federal state of the Aetolians of west-central Greece that became one of the great powers of Hellenistic Greece and controlled the oracle of Delphi.
aetolian-league.o: The [[e:aetolians|Aetolians]] lived in mountain villages north of the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]], scorned by [[e:thucydides|Thucydides]] as primitive. By 367 BCE an Aetolian federation was acting as a state, with its religious centre at the sanctuary of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] at [[e:thermon|Thermon]]. Its prestige soared when it helped repel the Gallic invasion of [[s:delphi|Delphi]] in 279 BCE.
aetolian-league.r: The league had a general assembly of all citizens meeting at [[e:thermon|Thermon]] and elsewhere, a large council and an annual general ([[e:strategos|strategos]]) assisted by a committee, the apokletoi. It expanded by granting citizenship or alliance to distant cities, controlled the votes of the [[s:amphictyonic-league|Amphictyonic League]] and was notorious for licensed raiding and piracy. Leaders such as Dorimachus and [[e:scopas|Scopas]] fought [[e:philip-v-of-macedon|Philip V of Macedon]].
aetolian-league.e: Allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] against Philip V in 211 BCE, the [[e:aetolians|Aetolians]] felt cheated after [[e:battle-of-cynoscephalae|Cynoscephalae]] in 197 BCE and invited [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] to [[e:greece|Greece]]. Defeated at Thermopylae in 191 BCE, the league accepted a peace in 189 BCE that left it a subordinate ally of Rome.

amisos.t: Amisos, a Greek port on the central Black Sea coast, later a royal city of the Pontic kings and the ancestor of Samsun.
amisos.o: Greek colonists, traditionally from [[s:miletus|Miletus]], founded Amisos in the 6th century BCE on a bay of the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] between the mouths of the [[e:kizilirmak|Halys]] and the [[e:yesilirmak|Iris]]. The city traded with the interior of [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]] and became one of the leading ports of the southern coast.
amisos.r: Amisos was a self-governing Greek city that received Athenian settlers in the 5th century BCE, when it was briefly renamed Peiraieus. It recognised Persian and then Hellenistic overlords while keeping its institutions, minting coins and exporting grain, [[e:timber|timber]] and metals.
amisos.e: From the accession of [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]] in 120 BCE Amisos was a royal city of the [[s:kingdom-of-pontus|Kingdom of Pontus]], adorned by the king. The Roman general [[e:lucius-licinius-lucullus|Lucullus]] captured it in 71 BCE, and it later flourished as a free city under [[e:rome|Rome]].

autrigones.t: A people of northern Burgos and western Bizkaia, whose towns Virovesca and Flaviobriga linked the Meseta to the Cantabrian Sea.
autrigones.o: The Autrigones occupied the land from the upper [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] to the coast around [[e:castro-urdiales|Castro Urdiales]], in modern [[e:burgos|Burgos]], Álava and [[s:lordship-of-biscay|Bizkaia]], from the later [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. They bordered the [[s:cantabri|Cantabri]], [[s:turmodigi|Turmodigi]], [[s:caristii|Caristii]] and [[s:berones|Berones]], and their language was probably Celtic.
autrigones.r: They lived in hillforts and lowland settlements, farming and herding, with towns such as [[e:briviesca|Virovesca]] (Briviesca) and Tritium Autrigonum named by Pliny and Ptolemy. Their political organisation is unknown.
autrigones.e: They came under [[e:rome|Rome]] during the 1st century BCE, and after the [[e:cantabrian-wars|Cantabrian Wars]] their territory became part of [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Hispania Tarraconensis]]. The Flavian emperors founded the port of [[e:castro-urdiales|Flaviobriga]] on their coast, modern [[s:duchy-of-castro|Castro]] Urdiales.

acadia.t: The French colony of the Maritime region, whose farmers built dykes on the Bay of Fundy and whose later expulsion by Britain became a defining tragedy.
acadia.o: In 1604 [[e:pierre-dugua-de-mons|Pierre Dugua de Mons]] and [[e:samuel-de-champlain|Samuel de Champlain]] wintered on [[e:saint-croix|Saint Croix]] Island, and in 1605 moved across the [[e:bay-of-fundy|Bay of Fundy]] to found [[e:port-royal-acadia|Port-Royal]]. Raided by English colonists from [[e:virginia|Virginia]] in 1613, granted to [[e:scotland|Scotland]] as [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]] in 1621 and occupied by Scottish settlers from 1629, the colony returned to [[e:france|France]] in 1632 and slowly took root.
acadia.r: Acadia was thinly governed, and in the 1640s rival lieutenants [[e:charles-de-menou-daulnay|Charles de Menou d'Aulnay]] and [[e:charles-de-la-tour|Charles de La Tour]] fought a small civil war. Settlers reclaimed salt marshes with dykes and sluices called aboiteaux, growing wheat and raising [[e:cattle|cattle]] around [[e:port-royal-acadia|Port-Royal]], [[e:grand-pre|Grand-Pré]] and [[e:beaubassin|Beaubassin]]. Close ties with the [[e:mikmaq|Mi'kmaq]], members of the [[s:wabanaki-confederacy|Wabanaki Confederacy]], and trade with [[e:new-england|New England]] defined Acadian life.
acadia.e: English forces held Acadia from 1654 to 1670 and seized [[e:port-royal-acadia|Port-Royal]] for good in 1710. The [[e:treaty-of-utrecht|Treaty of Utrecht]] in 1713 ceded the peninsula to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] as the [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Colony of Nova Scotia]], and in 1755 the British began deporting the [[e:acadians|Acadians]].

alta-california.t: The northern frontier of New Spain and then Mexico, settled through Franciscan missions and presidios before passing to the United States in 1848.
alta-california.o: Fearing Russian and British advances on the Pacific coast, [[e:spain|Spain]] sent the [[e:portola-expedition|Portolá expedition]] north in 1769. [[e:franciscans|Franciscans]] under [[e:junipero-serra|Junípero Serra]] founded a mission at [[e:san-diego|San Diego]] that year, and [[e:monterey-california|Monterey]], founded in 1770, later became the capital. Alta [[e:california|California]] was formally separated from [[e:baja-california|Baja California]] in 1804 as a province of [[s:new-spain|New Spain]].
alta-california.r: Twenty-one missions along [[e:el-camino-real-california|El Camino Real]] gathered [[e:indigenous-peoples-of-california|Native Californians]] into labour communities, with devastating losses from disease and coercion. Presidios and a few pueblos such as [[e:los-angeles|Los Angeles]] and [[e:san-jose-california|San Jose]] held the Spanish presence. After [[s:mexico|Mexico]] won independence in 1821, the missions were secularised in the 1830s and their lands passed to [[e:californios|Californio]] ranchers, whose [[e:cattle|cattle]] hides and tallow were traded to [[e:new-england|New England]] ships.
alta-california.e: [[e:californios|Californio]] politics were turbulent, with revolts against governors sent from [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]]. During the [[e:mexican-american-war|Mexican-American War]] the [[s:california-republic|California Republic]] briefly appeared in 1846 and US forces occupied the province. The [[e:treaty-of-guadalupe-hidalgo|Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo]] ceded it to the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1848; statehood followed in 1850 amid the Gold Rush.

cr.a: previous version Ignaciogavira; current version HansenBCN, designs from SanchoPanzaXXI

arab-federation.t: A union of the two Hashemite kingdoms, Iraq and Jordan, formed in February 1958 as a rival to Nasser's United Arab Republic and lasting under six months.
arab-federation.o: On 1 February 1958 [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] merged into the [[s:united-arab-republic|United Arab Republic]] under [[e:gamal-abdel-nasser|Gamal Abdel Nasser]]. In response, the Hashemite cousins King [[e:faisal-ii-of-iraq|Faisal II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-iraq|Kingdom of Iraq]] and [[e:hussein-of-jordan|King Hussein]] of the [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan]] proclaimed the Arab Federation on 14 February 1958.
arab-federation.r: [[e:faisal-ii-of-iraq|Faisal II]] was head of state with [[e:hussein-of-jordan|Hussein]] as his deputy, and each kingdom kept its own monarch and much of its own government. A federal parliament, joint army and common foreign policy were planned, and the capital was to alternate between [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]] and [[e:amman|Amman]]. [[e:nuri-al-said|Nuri al-Said]] became federal prime minister. [[e:iraq|Iraq's]] oil wealth was expected to support [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]], which had lost British [[e:subsidy|subsidies]].
arab-federation.e: On 14 July 1958 the Iraqi monarchy was overthrown and [[e:faisal-ii-of-iraq|Faisal II]] killed. [[e:hussein-of-jordan|Hussein]] formally dissolved the federation on 2 August 1958, and the new [[s:republic-of-iraq|Republic of Iraq]] withdrew from it.

azerbaijan-peoples-government.t: A Soviet-backed autonomous government in Iranian Azerbaijan in 1945 to 1946, whose fall was one of the first crises of the Cold War.
azerbaijan-peoples-government.o: Soviet troops occupied northern [[e:iran|Iran]] in 1941. In September 1945 the [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] [[e:democratic-party-uganda|Democratic Party]] was founded in [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] under [[e:jafar-pishevari|Ja'far Pishevari]], a veteran communist, with Soviet encouragement. In November and December 1945 it held elections to a national assembly and formed a government in Tabriz, while Soviet forces prevented Iranian troops from intervening.
azerbaijan-peoples-government.r: The government declared autonomy within [[e:iran|Iran]] rather than full independence. It made Azerbaijani Turkic the official language of schools and administration, founded a university in [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], began land distribution and organised its own militia. It ruled with the support of the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], whose troops remained in Iran beyond the agreed withdrawal date, leading to the Iran crisis of 1946 at the new [[e:united-nations|United Nations]].
azerbaijan-peoples-government.e: After Prime Minister [[e:ahmad-qavam|Ahmad Qavam]] promised the [[e:soviet-union|Soviets]] an oil concession, Soviet troops withdrew in May 1946. In December 1946 the Iranian army entered [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]], the government collapsed and Pishevari fled to the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], where he died in 1947.

aussa-sultanate.t: The leading Afar state, centred on the Aussa oasis of the lower Awash, which defeated an Egyptian expedition and kept autonomy into the 20th century.
aussa-sultanate.o: After the collapse of the [[s:imamate-of-aussa|Imamate of Aussa]], the [[e:mudaito-dynasty|Mudaito]] clan of the [[e:afar|Afar]] took power in the oasis around 1734 under Kedafu, founder of a new dynasty. The sultanate controlled the irrigated lands of the lower [[e:awash-river|Awash]] river, an island of farming in the deserts of the [[e:afar-triangle|Afar Triangle]].
aussa-sultanate.r: The sultan ruled with clan leaders over pastoral [[e:afar|Afar]] and the farming population of the oasis, applying Islamic law alongside Afar customary law. The sultanate controlled [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] and [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]] between the coast and the highlands. In 1875 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Mahammad Hanfadhe destroyed an Egyptian expedition led by [[e:werner-munzinger|Werner Munzinger]], securing its independence.
aussa-sultanate.e: [[e:aussa|Aussa]] accepted the overlordship of the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]] under [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]] but kept wide autonomy. Its sultan sided with [[e:italy|Italy]] during the 1936 invasion, and the sultanate was later reabsorbed into [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]]. The dynasty continued under [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:alimirah-hanfare|Alimirah Hanfare]], a major figure in [[e:afar|Afar]] politics until his death in 2011.

avar-khaganate.t: Steppe empire centred on the Carpathian basin that dominated central Europe's Slavs, besieged Constantinople and lasted until Charlemagne broke it.
avar-khaganate.o: The [[e:avars|Avars]] came from the Eurasian steppe and reached the Byzantine frontier in 558. In 567 their [[e:khagan|khagan]] Bayan I allied with the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombards]] to destroy the [[s:kingdom-of-the-gepids|Kingdom of the Gepids]], and after the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] left for [[e:italy|Italy]] in 568 the Avars took the whole Carpathian basin.
avar-khaganate.r: The [[e:khagan|khagan]] ruled a mounted warrior elite over [[e:slavs|Slavs]], [[e:gepids|Gepids]] and others. Byzantine tribute in gold financed the state, and [[e:avars|Avar]] raids reached [[e:italy|Italy]] and [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]]. In 626 they besieged [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] with Persian support and failed, and many Slav subjects broke away. Later Avar graves show cast bronze belt fittings with griffins and tendrils, and earthwork rings served as royal centres.
avar-khaganate.e: From 791 [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] [[s:franks|Franks]] attacked; in 795–796 they seized the treasure of the Ring. [[e:avars|Avar]] leaders accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and Frankish overlordship, and the [[s:first-bulgarian-empire|First Bulgarian Empire]] took the east. The last mention of Avars comes in 822, and their land later passed to the [[e:magyars|Hungarians]].

atzele.t: Latgalian borderland in north-eastern Latvia, contested between the crusaders and the Rus' of Pskov in the early 13th century.
atzele.o: Atzele, called Adzele in Latvian and Ochela in Rus' sources, lay in the north-eastern corner of modern [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]], around [[e:aluksne|Alūksne]]. It was a Latgalian district bordering Estonian [[s:ugandi|Ugandi]] and the lands of [[e:pskov|Pskov]].
atzele.r: Its people farmed and lived in communities centred on hillforts. The district was part of the Rus' tribute zone, and [[e:pskov|Pskov]] and Novgorod sent expeditions through it. Little is recorded of its rulers.
atzele.e: After the Livonian crusaders conquered neighbouring lands, Atzele was divided in 1224 between the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of Riga and the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]] and became part of [[s:terra-mariana|Terra Mariana]]. [[e:aluksne|Alūksne]] castle was later built in the area by the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]].

argentine-confederation.t: The loose union of Argentine provinces dominated by Juan Manuel de Rosas, which gave Argentina its 1853 constitution before Buenos Aires reunited the nation.
argentine-confederation.o: The [[e:federal-pact|Federal Pact]] of 1831 between [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]], [[e:santa-fe-argentina|Santa Fe]] and [[e:entre-rios-province|Entre Ríos]], later joined by the other provinces after the defeat of the [[s:unitarian-league|Unitarian League]], created the Argentine Confederation. There was no national government; the governor of Buenos Aires conducted foreign relations on behalf of the provinces.
argentine-confederation.r: [[e:juan-manuel-de-rosas|Juan Manuel de Rosas]], governor of [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] from 1829 to 1832 and from 1835 to 1852 with total public power, dominated the confederation. His police, the [[e:la-mazorca|Mazorca]], terrorised Unitarian opponents. He resisted an Anglo-French [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]] of the [[e:rio-de-la-plata|River Plate]] from 1845 to 1850. After [[e:justo-jose-de-urquiza|Justo José de Urquiza]] defeated him at [[e:battle-of-caseros|Caseros]] in 1852, a congress adopted the Constitution of 1853, still in force, and the government sat at [[e:parana-entre-rios|Paraná]].
argentine-confederation.e: [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] rejected the constitution and formed the separate [[s:state-of-buenos-aires|State of Buenos Aires]]. After [[e:bartolome-mitre|Bartolomé Mitre's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-pavon|Pavón]] in 1861, the nation reunited as the [[s:argentine-republic|Argentine Republic]]. The Constitution of 1853 remains the basis of [[e:argentina|Argentina's]] present constitution.

alderney.t: The northernmost of the inhabited Channel Islands, a self-governing part of the Bailiwick of Guernsey with its own States and a long history as a fortress.
alderney.o: Alderney was part of the [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Duchy of Normandy]] and stayed loyal to the English crown when [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] lost mainland Normandy to [[e:france|France]] in 1204. Like the other [[e:channel-islands|Channel Islands]] it remained a possession of the crown in its role as Duke of Normandy, never part of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]].
alderney.r: The island was governed under Norman customary law, and from 1584 to 1825 held by hereditary governors. The British built a chain of Victorian forts and the breakwater at Braye. During the German occupation of 1940 to 1945 the population was evacuated and the [[e:nazism|Nazis]] built labour camps there.
alderney.e: Alderney's residents returned in 1945. Since 1949 [[s:bailiwick-of-guernsey|Guernsey]] has run some of its public services, while Alderney keeps its own elected States within the Bailiwick of Guernsey, a British Crown Dependency.

ausetani.t: An Iberian people of the plain of Vic in Catalonia, whose name survives in the later County of Osona.
ausetani.o: The Ausetani lived on the plain of Vic and the surrounding hills in central [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] from about the 5th century BCE. Their chief town was [[e:vic|Ausa]], on the site of modern Vic, and the fortified settlement of L'Esquerda lay nearby.
ausetani.r: Little is known of their institutions beyond [[e:livy|Livy's]] narrative. They lived from farming and herding, and minted coins with the Iberian legend Ausesken. During the [[e:second-punic-war|Second Punic War]] they sided with [[e:carthage|Carthage]], and their leader Amusicus fled to [[e:hasdrubal-barca|Hasdrubal]] when the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] besieged their town for thirty days.
ausetani.e: After further resistance during [[e:cato-the-elder|Cato]]'s campaign of 195 BCE, they were absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]]. [[e:vic|Ausa]] became the Roman town of Ausa, later Vicus Ausonensis, and their name lived on in the medieval [[s:county-of-osona|County of Osona]].

allobroges.t: Powerful Gallic people between the Rhône and the Isère, conquered by Rome in 121 BCE, whose envoys exposed the Catilinarian conspiracy.
allobroges.o: The Allobroges held the land between the [[e:rhone|Rhône]], the [[e:isere-river|Isère]] and [[e:lake-geneva|Lake Geneva]], in the modern Isère and [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]]. Their chief town was [[e:vienna|Vienna]] ([[e:vienne|Vienne]]), and [[e:geneva|Genava]] ([[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]]) stood on their northern border. [[e:livy|Livy]] notes them on [[e:hannibal|Hannibal's]] route through the [[e:alps|Alps]] in 218 BCE.
allobroges.r: They were a warlike people governed by a nobility, rich in [[e:cattle|cattle]] and controlling routes into the [[e:alps|Alps]]. In 123 BCE they sheltered [[e:teutomalius|Teutomalius]], king of the [[s:salyes|Salyes]], which gave [[e:rome|Rome]] its pretext for war.
allobroges.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] defeated them in 121 BCE, and their land became part of [[e:gallia-narbonensis|Gallia Narbonensis]]. In 63 BCE their envoys revealed [[e:catiline|Catiline's]] plot to [[e:cicero|Cicero]], but in 61 BCE they rose under [[e:catugnatus|Catugnatus]] and were crushed. [[e:vienne|Vienne]] became a wealthy Roman colony.

autonomous-republic-of-cochinchina.t: A French-sponsored separatist republic in southern Vietnam, set up in 1946 to keep the south apart from Ho Chi Minh's government.
autonomous-republic-of-cochinchina.o: As [[e:france|France]] returned to [[e:indochina|Indochina]] after the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]], High Commissioner [[e:georges-thierry-dargenlieu|Thierry d'Argenlieu]] proclaimed the Autonomous Republic of [[s:french-cochinchina|Cochinchina]] on 1 June 1946, while negotiations with [[e:ho-chi-minh|Ho Chi Minh's]] [[s:democratic-republic-of-vietnam|Democratic Republic of Vietnam]] were taking place in France. Its first president was [[e:nguyen-van-thinh|Nguyen Van Thinh]].
autonomous-republic-of-cochinchina.r: The republic, based in [[e:ho-chi-minh-city|Saigon]], was dominated by French interests and a small southern Francophile elite. It had little popular support and was denounced by Vietnamese nationalists as a French puppet. [[e:nguyen-van-thinh|Nguyen Van Thinh]], unable to govern effectively, committed suicide in November 1946, and his successors were equally weak.
autonomous-republic-of-cochinchina.e: As [[e:france|France]] changed strategy to work with [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]], the republic was renamed the Provisional Government of [[s:republic-of-vietnam|South Vietnam]] in 1947 and in 1948 merged into the [[s:provisional-central-government-of-vietnam|Provisional Central Government of Vietnam]]. In 1949 [[s:french-cochinchina|Cochinchina]] was formally attached to the [[s:state-of-vietnam|State of Vietnam]].

alawite-state.t: A French-created state for the Alawite mountains and coast of Syria, separated from the rest of Syria between 1920 and 1936.
alawite-state.o: In 1920 [[e:france|France]] established the Territory of the [[e:alawites|Alawites]], covering the coastal mountains and the port of [[e:latakia|Latakia]], where the Alawites, a heterodox Shia community long marginalised under the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], were the majority in the countryside. The territory became the Alawite State in 1922.
alawite-state.r: Governed by French officials with an Alawite-dominated representative council, the state withdrew from the [[s:syrian-federation|Syrian Federation]] in 1924 and was renamed the Government of [[e:latakia|Latakia]] in 1930. [[e:france|France]] recruited many [[e:alawites|Alawites]] into its colonial army. Road-building and land reform were undertaken, but the coastal towns, largely [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] and Christian, favoured union with [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
alawite-state.e: Under the 1936 [[e:franco-syrian-treaty-of-independence|Franco-Syrian treaty]] the state was incorporated into the [[s:syrian-republic|Syrian Republic]], despite petitions by some Alawite notables asking to remain separate, and it was fully integrated in 1937.

autonomous-governorate-of-estonia.t: Self-governing Estonian province created by Russia's Provisional Government in 1917, whose assembly prepared the declaration of Estonian independence.
autonomous-governorate-of-estonia.o: After the [[e:february-revolution|February Revolution]], [[e:russia|Russia's]] Provisional Government decreed on 12 April 1917 that the [[s:governorate-of-estonia|Governorate of Estonia]] would be joined with the Estonian-speaking northern districts of the [[s:governorate-of-livonia|Governorate of Livonia]], uniting the Estonian people in one autonomous province. [[e:jaan-poska|Jaan Poska]], mayor of [[s:reval|Reval]], became its commissar.
autonomous-governorate-of-estonia.r: For the first time [[e:estonians|Estonians]] governed their own land. An elected provincial assembly, the [[e:estonian-provincial-assembly|Maapäev]], met in July 1917, and a Provincial Government led by [[e:konstantin-pats|Konstantin Päts]] was formed. Estonian replaced German as the language of administration, and national regiments were organised.
autonomous-governorate-of-estonia.e: After the Bolshevik coup, the [[e:estonian-provincial-assembly|Maapäev]] declared itself the sovereign power in [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] on 28 November 1917 before being dispersed by local Bolsheviks. As German troops advanced and the Bolsheviks withdrew, the [[e:estonian-salvation-committee|Salvation Committee]] declared the Republic of [[e:estonia|Estonia]] on 24 February 1918; the Germans then occupied the country until November.

cr.a: Original: Unknown author Vector: SKopp, PeepP and ‍others

azerbaijan-ssr.t: Soviet Azerbaijan, a republic of the USSR from 1920 to 1991, centred on oil-rich Baku and shaped by the conflict over Nagorno-Karabakh.
azerbaijan-ssr.o: In April 1920 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] entered [[e:baku|Baku]], and the Bolsheviks overthrew the [[s:azerbaijan-democratic-republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]], proclaiming the [[e:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] Soviet Socialist Republic. In 1922 it joined the [[s:transcaucasian-sfsr|Transcaucasian SFSR]], which became part of the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], and in 1936 it became a full union republic.
azerbaijan-ssr.r: [[e:baku|Baku's]] oil fields were vital to the Soviet economy, especially in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. The republic included the [[e:nagorno-karabakh-autonomous-oblast|Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast]] and the [[e:nakhchivan-autonomous-soviet-socialist-republic|Nakhchivan ASSR]]. Soviet rule brought industrialisation, mass literacy and a switch from Arabic to [[e:latin|Latin]] and then Cyrillic script, but also collectivisation and [[e:joseph-stalin|Stalin]]'s purges. [[e:heydar-aliyev|Heydar Aliyev]] led the republic's [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Communist Party]] from 1969 to 1982.
azerbaijan-ssr.e: From 1988 the [[e:karabakh-movement|Karabakh movement]] led to war with [[e:armenians|Armenians]], and Soviet troops killed over a hundred civilians in [[e:baku|Baku]] in January 1990. [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] declared independence in August 1991, and the USSR's dissolution in December 1991 created the Republic of [[e:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]].

autonomous-albanian-republic-of-korce.t: Albanian autonomous region set up under French military protection during the First World War, which gave Korçë its own schools, money and stamps.
autonomous-albanian-republic-of-korce.o: During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] French forces of the [[e:macedonian-front|Salonika front]] occupied [[e:korce|Korçë]] in late 1916. To secure the area against Greek irregulars and win local support, the French commander signed the [[e:protocol-of-korce|Protocol of Korçë]] in December 1916 with Albanian notables, creating an autonomous Albanian province under French protection, with [[e:themistokli-germenji|Themistokli Gërmenji]] as prefect of police.
autonomous-albanian-republic-of-korce.r: A council of Christian and Muslim Albanian representatives ran the town and surrounding villages, and Albanian became the language of administration and schools, including the first Albanian secular secondary school. The republic issued its own stamps and banknotes and flew an Albanian flag with French colours. Real authority lay with the French army.
autonomous-albanian-republic-of-korce.e: [[e:france|France]] ended the autonomy in February 1918 and governed the district militarily, Gërmenji having been executed by a French court in 1917. In 1920 French troops withdrew and handed [[e:korce|Korçë]] to the Albanian government created at [[e:lushnje|Lushnjë]], ensuring it stayed in [[s:albania|Albania]] rather than [[e:greece|Greece]].

cr.a: Auteur inconnu; derivative work by Titimaster

adab.t: A Sumerian city on the Iturungal canal, devoted to the mother goddess Ninhursag and known mainly from its temple and administrative archives.
adab.o: Adab, modern Bismaya, was occupied from the early third millennium BCE and became an independent city-state in the [[e:early-dynastic-period|Early Dynastic period]]. A late literary tradition credits a king of Adab, [[e:lugal-anne-mundu|Lugal-Anne-mundu]], with vast conquests, but these stories cannot be confirmed by contemporary records.
adab.r: Its main temple, the E-sar, belonged to [[e:ninhursag|Ninhursag]] in her local form Digirmah. Excavations by [[e:edgar-james-banks|Edgar Banks]] for the [[e:university-of-chicago|University of Chicago]] in 1903 to 1905 found temple remains, statues and tablets, and many more Adab texts later entered collections through looting. They show a temple-centred economy of barley, livestock and craft workshops typical of Sumerian cities. Meskigal governed the city first under [[e:lugal-zage-si|Lugal-zage-si]] and then under [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon]].
adab.e: Adab lost its independence to the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]] around 2334 BCE and rebelled more than once against Akkadian kings. It remained a provincial city under the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]] and faded in the early second millennium BCE.

aundh-state.t: A small Maratha state of the Deccan ruled by the Pant Pratinidhi family, remembered for the Aundh Experiment in village self-government.
aundh-state.o: Aundh was granted in 1699 to [[e:parshuram-trimbak|Parshuram Trimbak]], appointed [[e:pant-pratinidhi|Pratinidhi]] (viceregent) by the [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] king [[e:rajaram-i|Rajaram]]. His [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] family held the hereditary title of Pant Pratinidhi and the lands attached to it.
aundh-state.r: The rulers governed a dry [[e:deccan|Deccan]] territory near [[e:satara|Satara]]. [[e:bhawanrao-pant-pratinidhi|Bhawanrao Pant Pratinidhi]], who reigned from 1909 to 1947, promoted the surya namaskar exercise and the arts, and in 1938, with the advice of [[e:mahatma-gandhi|Gandhi]], introduced the [[e:aundh-experiment|Aundh Experiment]], handing power to village [[e:panchayat|panchayats]] under a constitution drafted with [[e:maurice-frydman|Maurice Frydman]].
aundh-state.e: Aundh merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]] in 1960, in [[e:satara|Satara]] district.

agder.t: Petty kingdom on Norway's southern tip whose king, according to the sagas, fought Harald Fairhair at Hafrsfjord.
agder.o: Agder, the southernmost coast of [[e:norway|Norway]], was a small kingdom in the [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]]. The sagas link it with the [[s:vestfold|Vestfold]] dynasty through Queen [[e:asa-haraldsdottir|Åsa]], daughter of a king of Agder and mother of [[e:halfdan-the-black|Halfdan the Black]].
agder.r: Agder faced the [[e:skagerrak|Skagerrak]] and [[e:denmark|Denmark]] and lived by farming, fishing and sea trade. Its rulers are known only from late saga tradition, and the boundaries of the kingdom are uncertain.
agder.e: [[e:heimskringla|Heimskringla]] says that Kjotve the Rich, king of Agder, joined the western coalition defeated by [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] at [[e:battle-of-hafrsfjord|Hafrsfjord]], traditionally around 872. Agder then passed into the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]].

arababni.t: An obscure Muslim principality of the medieval Ethiopian interior, named by Arab writers among the seven Muslim kingdoms of Abyssinia.
arababni.o: Arababni is known only from the 14th-century account of [[e:al-umari|al-Umari]], who placed it among the Muslim states of [[e:ethiopia|Abyssinia]], apparently between [[e:ifat-sultanate|Ifat]] and [[s:hadiya-sultanate|Hadiya]]. Nothing is known of its foundation, and its exact location remains uncertain.
arababni.r: [[e:al-umari|Al-Umari]] presents it as a small agricultural state paying tribute to the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]] after the campaigns of [[e:amda-seyon-i|Amda Seyon]] in the 1330s. No rulers or institutions are recorded.
arababni.e: Arababni vanishes from the sources in the 15th century, probably absorbed into neighbouring provinces during the long wars between the emperors and the Muslim sultanates.

alaiye-beylik.t: A small Turkish principality at Alanya on the Mediterranean coast, ruled by a branch of the Karamanids under the great Seljuk citadel.
alaiye-beylik.o: [[e:alanya|Alanya]] was built up by the Seljuk sultan [[e:kayqubad-i|Kayqubad I]] after 1221 as a winter capital and naval base. After Seljuk authority collapsed in the late 13th century, local Turkish lords, later linked to the [[s:karamanids|Karamanids]], took over the city and its surrounding coast.
alaiye-beylik.r: The rulers lived in the Seljuk citadel and used its shipyard and [[e:red-tower-alanya|Red Tower]]. [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] visited in the 1330s and met its ruler Yusuf Bey. The town traded [[e:timber|timber]] and other goods with [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and [[e:venice|Venice]]. In 1427 its ruler sold [[e:alanya|Alanya]] to the [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] sultan [[e:barsbay|Barsbay]], though Mamluk control did not last, and the Karamanid line returned.
alaiye-beylik.e: The Ottoman commander [[e:gedik-ahmed-pasha|Gedik Ahmed Pasha]] took [[e:alanya|Alanya]] in 1471 from its last ruler, Kilij Arslan, who received a domain elsewhere.

aru-kingdom.t: A Karo and Malay kingdom on the east coast of North Sumatra, rival of Malacca and Aceh for control of the Strait of Malacca.
aru-kingdom.o: Haru appears in Chinese records from the 13th century and in the Javanese [[e:nagarakretagama|Nagarakretagama]] of 1365. Its centre lay near modern Medan, where the sites of Kota Rentang and [[e:kota-cina|Kota Cina]] have yielded Chinese ceramics and coins and South Indian-style Buddhist and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] statues from an earlier trading settlement.
aru-kingdom.r: Aru drew on [[e:karo-batak|Karo Batak]] peoples of the interior and on Malay coastal trade, exporting forest products, [[e:camphor|camphor]] and horses. Ming envoys visited, and [[e:zheng-he|Zheng He's]] fleets called in the early 15th century. Its rulers adopted [[e:islam|Islam]], though Malay sources such as the [[e:malay-annals|Malay Annals]] describe the people as raiders who challenged [[e:malacca|Malacca]] at sea.
aru-kingdom.e: After [[e:malacca|Malacca]] fell to the Portuguese in 1511, Aru was caught between [[s:portuguese-malacca|Portuguese Malacca]], the [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor Sultanate]] and the [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]]. [[e:aceh|Aceh]] attacked repeatedly and finally conquered it in 1613 under [[e:iskandar-muda|Iskandar Muda]]. Its lands later formed the core of the [[s:deli-sultanate|Deli Sultanate]].
aru-kingdom.re: Sunni Islam, earlier Hinduism and Buddhism

cr.a: Giovanni Battista Ramusio or Giacomo Gastaldi

aulerci-eburovices.t: Branch of the Aulerci around Évreux in Normandy who killed their own council rather than stay out of the war against Caesar.
aulerci-eburovices.o: The Eburovices were part of the [[e:aulerci|Aulerci]] group of peoples and held the land between the [[e:seine|Seine]] and the [[e:eure|Eure]], around the oppidum later called [[e:evreux|Mediolanum Aulercorum]].
aulerci-eburovices.r: Caesar records that in 56 BCE they and the [[s:lexovii|Lexovii]] murdered their senators, who opposed war, and joined the coalition of [[e:viridovix|Viridovix]] of the [[s:unelli|Unelli]]. The episode shows that they were governed by a council of nobles.
aulerci-eburovices.e: The coalition was defeated by [[e:quintus-titurius-sabinus|Quintus Titurius Sabinus]] in 56 BCE, and the Eburovices joined the general revolt again in 52 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:evreux|Mediolanum Aulercorum]] became a civitas capital, the origin of [[s:county-of-evreux|Évreux]].

alemanni.t: A confederation of Germanic peoples on the upper Rhine and Danube that overran Rome's Agri Decumates and gave its name to Germany in French and Spanish.
alemanni.o: The Alemanni ('all men') are first named in 213, when [[e:caracalla|Caracalla]] fought them on the Main. They formed from [[e:elbe-germanic-peoples|Elbe Germanic]] groups, including Suebian peoples such as the [[e:semnones|Semnones]], who moved towards the Roman frontier. After the [[e:limes-germanicus|Limes]] collapsed around 260 they settled the land between the upper [[e:rhine|Rhine]], the [[e:danube|Danube]] and [[e:lake-constance|Lake Constance]].
alemanni.r: The Alemanni had no single king but many regional kings and princes who sometimes joined forces. They raided [[e:gaul|Gaul]] and [[e:italy|Italy]] repeatedly; Julian defeated a coalition under [[e:chnodomar|Chnodomar]] at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-strasbourg|Strasbourg]] in 357. Many Alemanni also served in the Roman army. They lived in farmsteads and hilltop centres such as the [[e:runder-berg|Runder Berg]] near [[e:bad-urach|Urach]].
alemanni.e: [[e:clovis-i|Clovis I]] and the [[s:franks|Franks]] defeated the Alemanni at [[e:battle-of-tolbiac|Tolbiac]] around 496 and again around 506. Some came under Ostrogothic protection, but by 536 all were under Frankish rule, forming the [[s:duchy-of-alamannia|Duchy of Alamannia]]. Their dialects survive as Alemannic German in [[e:swabia|Swabia]], [[e:alsace|Alsace]] and [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]].
