ayyubid-emirate-of-homs.t: An Ayyubid principality of the descendants of Shirkuh, whose last prince helped defeat the Mongols at the first battle of Homs in 1260.
ayyubid-emirate-of-homs.o: In 1179 [[e:saladin|Saladin]] granted [[e:homs|Homs]] to his cousin Nasir al-Din Muhammad, son of [[e:shirkuh|Shirkuh]], the uncle who had conquered [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. The town remained with this line of the family as a hereditary principality.
ayyubid-emirate-of-homs.r: [[e:homs|Homs]] guarded the gap between the coast and the interior and faced the [[s:county-of-tripoli|County of Tripoli]] and the [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizari]] castles. Asad al-Din [[e:shirkuh|Shirkuh]] II ruled for over fifty years (1186-1240), keeping the town through shifting alliances. His successor [[e:al-mansur-ibrahim|al-Mansur Ibrahim]] fought alongside the [[s:franks|Franks]] against [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and lost at [[e:battle-of-la-forbie|La Forbie]] in 1244. [[e:al-ashraf-musa-emir-of-homs|Al-Ashraf Musa]] lost Homs for a time to [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]].
ayyubid-emirate-of-homs.e: [[e:al-ashraf-musa-emir-of-homs|Al-Ashraf Musa]], restored by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]], switched sides and with [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] troops defeated a Mongol army at [[e:homs|Homs]] in December 1260. After his death in 1262, the Mamluk sultan [[e:baybars|Baybars]] annexed the principality.

albanian-republic.t: Albania's first republic, a presidential regime built by Ahmet Zogu that drew the country closely towards Fascist Italy.
albanian-republic.o: [[e:zog-i|Ahmet Zogu]], a chieftain from [[e:mat-river|Mat]], was driven out by [[e:fan-noli|Fan Noli's]] [[e:june-revolution-albania|June Revolution]] of 1924 but returned in December with support from the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]] and White Russian [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]]. In January 1925 a constituent assembly abolished the [[s:principality-of-albania|Principality of Albania]] and proclaimed a republic with [[e:tirana|Tirana]] as capital, electing Zogu president for seven years.
albanian-republic.r: The 1925 statute gave the president sweeping powers over the government, army and legislation. Zogu disarmed clans, suppressed opponents and built roads and a gendarmerie. Short of money, he turned to [[e:italy|Italy]]: an Italian-controlled national bank and development company were founded, and the [[e:treaties-of-tirana|Treaties of Tirana]] of 1926 and 1927 made [[s:albania|Albania]] an Italian ally.
albanian-republic.e: On 1 September 1928 a constituent assembly proclaimed [[s:albania|Albania]] a monarchy, and Zogu became [[e:zog-i|King Zog]] I of the [[s:albanian-kingdom|Albanian Kingdom]]. The new constitution kept much of the presidential system but made the office hereditary, and the dependence on Italian money continued.
albanian-republic.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

afrasiyabids-of-mazandaran.t: The ten-year rule of Kiya Afrasiyab Chelavi, who murdered the last Bavand ruler and took Amol before falling to the Mar'ashi sayyids.
afrasiyabids-of-mazandaran.o: [[e:kiya-afrasiyab|Kiya Afrasiyab]] of the Chelavi family was a commander and in-law of [[e:fakhr-al-dawla-hasan|Fakhr al-Dawla Hasan]], the last ruler of the [[s:bavand-dynasty|Bavand dynasty]]. In 1349 he murdered Hasan and took control of [[e:amol|Amol]] and much of [[e:mazandaran|Mazandaran]].
afrasiyabids-of-mazandaran.r: [[e:afrasiab|Afrasiyab's]] brief rule is known mainly from Mazandarani chronicles such as [[e:zahir-al-din-marashi|Zahir al-Din Mar'ashi's]] history. He tried to win support from the [[e:sufism|Sufi]] followers of [[e:qavam-al-din-marashi|Sayyid Qavam al-Din Mar'ashi]], then turned against them when their influence grew.
afrasiyabids-of-mazandaran.e: In 1359 [[e:kiya-afrasiyab|Afrasiyab]] and his sons were killed fighting the Mar'ashi dervishes, and [[e:qavam-al-din-marashi|Qavam al-Din Mar'ashi]] founded the [[s:marashi-dynasty|Mar'ashi dynasty]] in [[e:amol|Amol]].

atrebates-britain.t: Southern British kingdom founded by the Gallic exile Commius, whose last king Verica fled to Rome and gave Claudius his pretext for invasion in 43.
atrebates-britain.o: [[e:commius|Commius]], king of the [[s:atrebates|Atrebates]] of northern [[e:gaul|Gaul]], first served [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]] and then joined the Gallic revolt of 52 BCE. Around 50 BCE he fled across the [[e:english-channel|Channel]], and coins bearing his name soon appear in central southern [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], where he appears to have founded a dynasty ruling [[e:hampshire|Hampshire]], [[e:berkshire|Berkshire]] and [[s:kingdom-of-sussex|Sussex]].
atrebates-britain.r: Kings claiming descent from [[e:commius|Commius]], notably [[e:tincomarus|Tincomarus]], [[e:eppillus|Eppillus]] and [[e:verica|Verica]], issued gold coins that increasingly copied Roman designs, and Verica's carry a vine leaf and the title REX, signs of friendship with [[e:rome|Rome]]. [[e:calleva-atrebatum|Calleva]], the later Silchester, grew into a planned oppidum with imported wine, [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and tableware. Pressure from the [[s:catuvellauni|Catuvellauni]] under [[e:cunobelinus|Cunobelinus]] and his sons steadily shrank the kingdom.
atrebates-britain.e: Around 41 or 42 [[e:verica|Verica]] was driven out and went to [[e:rome|Rome]] to seek help, which [[e:claudius|Claudius]] used to justify the invasion of 43. Afterwards much of the territory passed to the client [[s:kingdom-of-the-regni|Kingdom of the Regni]] under [[e:togidubnus|Togidubnus]], and [[e:calleva-atrebatum|Calleva Atrebatum]] became a civitas capital of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

albanian-kingdom.t: Albania's only native monarchy, the kingdom of Zog I, which modernised the country's laws while falling ever deeper under Italian control.
albanian-kingdom.o: On 1 September 1928 a constituent assembly turned the [[s:albanian-republic|Albanian Republic]] into a kingdom, and President [[e:zog-i|Ahmet Zogu]] became Zog I, King of the [[e:albanians|Albanians]], a title chosen to suggest claims beyond the state's borders. [[e:tirana|Tirana]] remained the capital, and the strong presidential powers of 1925 passed to the crown.
albanian-kingdom.r: [[e:zog-i|Zog]] ruled as an authoritarian moderniser, introducing civil and penal codes based on Italian, French and Swiss models, separating religion from the state and banning the face veil in 1937. Schools, roads and a small army were built, largely with Italian loans and advisers, and [[e:italy|Italy]] controlled the oil concessions and the national bank. Revolts, such as that at [[e:fier|Fier]] in 1935, were suppressed.
albanian-kingdom.e: [[e:benito-mussolini|Mussolini]] invaded on 7 April 1939, and resistance collapsed within days. [[e:zog-i|Zog]] fled with [[e:geraldine-of-albania|Queen Geraldine]] and their newborn son, never to return. [[e:italy|Italy]] turned the country into the [[s:albanian-kingdom-1939-1943|Albanian Kingdom]] (1939-1943) under King [[e:victor-emmanuel-iii|Victor Emmanuel III]].
albanian-kingdom.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

cr.a: Orange Tuesday (Later version was uploaded by AceDouble)

ammon.t: Ammon, an Iron Age kingdom of the Jordanian plateau around Rabbah, modern Amman, whose name lives on in Jordan's capital.
ammon.o: The Ammonites formed a kingdom in the 10th century BCE or earlier, on the plateau around the upper [[e:jabbok|Jabbok]] river, with its capital at [[e:amman|Rabbah]], the citadel of modern Amman. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] portrays King [[e:nahash-of-ammon|Nahash]] as an enemy of [[e:saul|Saul]].
ammon.r: Ammonite kings ruled a farming and herding land guarded by watchtowers, under the national god [[e:milcom|Milkom]]. Inscriptions such as the [[e:amman-citadel-inscription|Amman Citadel inscription]] and the [[e:tell-siran-bottle|Tell Siran bottle]], which names King Amminadab, show a language close to [[e:hebrew|Hebrew]]. Ammon prospered as a loyal [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]].
ammon.e: Under the [[s:chaldean-empire|Chaldean Empire]], King [[e:baalis|Baalis]] plotted against Babylonian rule in [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]]. A Babylonian campaign in 582 BCE ended Ammon's independence, and the land became a province. [[e:amman|Rabbah]] was refounded as [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]] by the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]].

andosini.t: A Pyrenean people subdued by Hannibal on his march to Italy in 218 BCE, often linked with the name of Andorra.
andosini.o: The Andosini are known only from [[e:polybius|Polybius]], who lists them among the peoples between the [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] and the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] that [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] conquered in 218 BCE. They are usually placed in the high valleys around modern [[s:andorra|Andorra]], whose name is often thought to derive from theirs.
andosini.r: Nothing is known of their society beyond a probable mountain economy of herding and small-scale farming.
andosini.e: After [[e:hannibal|Hannibal's]] campaign their territory was left under the Carthaginian officer Hanno. Following the Roman victories in the north-east and [[e:cato-the-elder|Cato]]'s campaign of 195 BCE, the area passed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]], and the Andosini are not mentioned again.

athgarh-state.t: A small princely state near Cuttack in Odisha, one of the Orissa Tributary States ruled by local Rajas until 1948.
athgarh-state.o: Tradition places the founding in the late 12th century, when a family in the service of the kings of Puri received land near the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]]. Its name means 'eight forts'.
athgarh-state.r: Athgarh was a small agricultural state just west of [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]]. It paid tribute to the [[s:gajapati-kingdom|Gajapati Kingdom]], the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and, from 1803, the British, who grouped it among the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]]. Little detailed history is recorded.
athgarh-state.e: Athgarh merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now part of [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]] district.

cr.a: Regierung von Britisch-Indien. Kartograph J. G. Bartholomew (gest. 1920)

asakura-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Asakura lords of Echizen, whose castle town of Ichijodani was a cultural centre until Oda Nobunaga destroyed it in 1573.
asakura-clan-domain.o: [[e:asakura-toshikage|Asakura Toshikage]], a retainer of the [[e:shiba-clan|Shiba]] governors of [[e:echizen-province|Echizen]], used the [[e:onin-war|Onin War]] to take control of the province, seizing power from his masters around 1471. He built his seat in the narrow valley of [[e:ichijodani|Ichijodani]].
asakura-clan-domain.r: [[e:asakura-toshikage|Toshikage]] is credited with an early house code that urged merit over birth and ordered [[e:vassal|vassals]] to live in the castle town. Five generations of Asakura made [[e:ichijodani|Ichijodani]] a prosperous town that welcomed refugee courtiers, poets and scholars from war-torn [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]]. The domain remained largely stable while neighbouring provinces fell into chaos.
asakura-clan-domain.e: [[e:asakura-yoshikage|Asakura Yoshikage]] sheltered the future [[e:shogun|shogun]] [[e:ashikaga-yoshiaki|Ashikaga Yoshiaki]] and allied with the Azai against [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. After defeat at [[e:battle-of-anegawa|Anegawa]] in 1570, Nobunaga invaded in 1573, burned [[e:ichijodani|Ichijodani]] and forced Yoshikage to kill himself. Its excavated streets are now a historic site.

ambarri.t: Gallic people of the lower Saône and Ain, clients of the Aedui whose appeal for help helped draw Caesar into Gaul in 58 BCE.
ambarri.o: Their name means those on both sides of the [[e:saone|Arar]], the ancient Saône. [[e:livy|Livy]] lists the Ambarri among the peoples who followed [[e:bellovesus|Bellovesus]] into northern [[e:italy|Italy]] in the legendary migrations of around 600 BCE. In Caesar's day they lived east of the Saône, near the [[e:rhone|Rhône]] confluence.
ambarri.r: Caesar calls them friends and kinsmen of the [[s:aedui|Aedui]], on whom they depended. No rulers or towns are recorded.
ambarri.e: When the migrating [[s:helvetii|Helvetii]] plundered their fields in 58 BCE, the Ambarri complained to Caesar, adding to his reasons to attack. After the conquest their territory was divided among neighbouring civitates, and the name survives only in a few place names in the Ain.

aram-damascus.t: Aram-Damascus, the strongest Aramaean kingdom, which led Syria against Assyria and dominated Israel under King Hazael.
aram-damascus.o: After the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]], Aramaean groups took over the [[e:damascus|Damascus]] oasis, once Egyptian Upi. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] credits [[e:rezon|Rezon]], a fugitive officer of [[s:aram-zobah|Aram-Zobah]], with founding the kingdom in the 10th century BCE, and under [[e:ben-hadad-i|Ben-Hadad I]] it became the leading power of southern [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
aram-damascus.r: Its kings ruled from [[e:damascus|Damascus]] over the oasis and the [[e:hauran|Hauran]], controlling [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] from [[e:arabia|Arabia]]. [[e:hadadezer-of-damascus|Hadadezer]] led the coalition with [[s:hamath|Hamath]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Kingdom of Israel]] against [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] at [[e:battle-of-qarqar|Qarqar]] in 853 BCE. The usurper [[e:hazael|Hazael]] then conquered much of Israel and destroyed [[s:gath|Gath]]; the [[e:tel-dan-stele|Tel Dan stele]] probably records his victories.
aram-damascus.e: King [[e:rezin|Rezin]] allied with [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Israel]] against [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]], whose king appealed to Tiglath-Pileser III of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]]. The [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyrians]] took [[e:damascus|Damascus]] in 732 BCE, killed Rezin and made Aram an Assyrian province.

autariatae.t: Large Illyrian tribal people of the central Balkans who overpowered the Triballi before being broken by Celtic invaders and Macedon.
autariatae.o: The Autariatae lived in the upper [[e:drina|Drina]] and [[e:lim-river|Lim]] valleys, in modern western [[s:serbia|Serbia]], [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]] and [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]], by the 5th century BCE. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] calls them once the greatest and best of the [[e:illyrians|Illyrians]].
autariatae.r: Little is known of their government; they appear as a warrior people of the interior. They fought their neighbours the [[e:ardiaei|Ardiaei]] over salt springs, and in the 4th century BCE defeated the [[s:triballi|Triballi]] and pushed east.
autariatae.e: Around 310 BCE Celtic incursions and a plague weakened them, and the Macedonian king [[e:cassander|Cassander]] resettled some 20,000 of them near Mount Orbelus. Their remnants were absorbed by the [[s:scordisci|Scordisci]] and other neighbours, and the name disappears in the 3rd century BCE.

alan-kingdom-in-hispania.t: The short-lived realm of the Iranian-speaking Alans in Lusitania and Carthaginiensis, destroyed by the Visigoths within a decade.
alan-kingdom-in-hispania.o: The [[s:alans|Alans]], nomads from the steppe north of the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]], crossed the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 406 with [[e:vandals|Vandals]] and [[s:suebi|Suebi]] and entered [[e:hispania|Hispania]] in 409. In 411, when the invaders divided the provinces by lot, the Alans took [[s:lusitania|Lusitania]] and [[s:carthaginiensis|Carthaginiensis]], the largest share.
alan-kingdom-in-hispania.r: They formed a warrior aristocracy ruling over a Hispano-Roman population, living from tribute and plunder rather than building lasting institutions. Their king [[e:addac|Addax]] led them in [[e:hispania|Hispania]]. Very little is known of their administration, and [[e:hydatius|Hydatius]] is the main source.
alan-kingdom-in-hispania.e: From 416 the Visigothic king [[e:wallia|Wallia]], acting for [[e:rome|Rome]], campaigned against them, and in 418 [[e:addac|Addax]] was killed. The surviving [[s:alans|Alans]] joined the [[e:vandals|Hasding Vandals]] under [[e:gunderic|Gunderic]], whose kings in [[e:africa|Africa]] styled themselves kings of the Vandals and Alans.

ambliyara-state.t: A minor Rajput chiefship of the Mahi Kantha country in northern Gujarat.
ambliyara-state.o: Ambliyara was one of the petty estates of the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|Mahi Kantha]] region, held by a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family whose separate holding dates from around 1619. Its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
ambliyara-state.r: The ruler held a small group of villages, paid tribute through the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]] and was supervised by the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|British Mahi Kantha Agency]]. Few further details are recorded in standard works.
ambliyara-state.e: Ambliyara was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

apracharajas.t: A local dynasty of Bajaur in the hills of Gandhara, known from its Buddhist reliquary inscriptions.
apracharajas.o: The Apracharajas, kings of the Apracas, ruled in the [[e:bajaur|Bajaur]] region north of [[e:peshawar|Peshawar]] from the mid-1st century BCE. They appear to have begun as local chiefs who served as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:indo-scythians|Indo-Scythians]] and later of the [[s:indo-parthian-kingdom|Indo-Parthian Kingdom]]. The founder known from inscriptions is [[e:vijayamitra|Vijayamitra]].
apracharajas.r: The dynasty is known almost entirely from inscriptions in Kharoshthi on Buddhist relic containers, which record the dedication of relics by kings, queens and generals. The reliquaries use several eras, including the [[e:azes-i|Azes]] era and an era of the [[e:greeks|Greeks]], and are important evidence for the chronology of the period. [[e:aspavarma|Aspavarma]], a son of [[e:indravarma|Indravarma]], issued coins.
apracharajas.e: The Apracharajas disappear from the record in the 1st century, probably absorbed by the expanding [[s:kushan-empire|Kushan Empire]]. Their reliquaries, now in museums, are among the best sources for early [[e:gandhara-art|Gandharan]] [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]].

au-lac.t: A short-lived kingdom of the Red River delta, famous for the spiral citadel of Co Loa and the legend of King An Duong's magic crossbow.
au-lac.o: Au Lac was formed around 257 BCE when [[e:an-duong-vuong|Thuc Phan]], a leader of the [[e:au-viet|Au Viet]] people from the northern uplands, overthrew the last Hung king of [[s:van-lang|Van Lang]] and joined the two peoples under his rule as King An Duong. He built his capital at [[e:co-loa-citadel|Co Loa]], north of present-day [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]].
au-lac.r: [[e:co-loa-citadel|Co Loa]], with three concentric ramparts and moats enclosing about 600 hectares, is the largest pre-Han fortified site in [[e:southeast-asia|Southeast Asia]], and excavations there have found thousands of bronze arrowheads. The kingdom rested on [[e:rice|rice]] farming and [[e:dong-son-culture|Dong Son]] bronze working, and the Lac lords of the older order seem to have kept local power under the new king.
au-lac.e: Around 179 BCE [[e:zhao-tuo|Zhao Tuo]], ruler of [[s:nanyue|Nanyue]], conquered Au Lac; legend says his son married [[e:an-duong-vuong|An Duong]]'s daughter [[e:my-chau|My Chau]] and stole the secret of the magic [[e:crossbow|crossbow]]. The land was absorbed into Nanyue, and after 111 BCE into the Han empire, beginning a long era of Chinese rule.

amphipolis.t: Athenian colony on the Strymon river, key to the timber and gold of Thrace, whose loss to Sparta in 424 BCE exiled the historian Thucydides.
amphipolis.o: The site, a loop of the lower [[e:struma|Strymon]] called Ennea Hodoi (Nine Ways), had long attracted [[s:athens|Athens]]; a first attempt to settle it ended in disaster around 465 BCE. In 437 BCE [[e:hagnon|Hagnon]] founded Amphipolis there with Athenian and allied settlers, controlling the river crossing and the route to the [[e:timber|timber]] and gold and [[e:silver|silver]] mines of [[e:mount-pangaion|Mount Pangaion]].
amphipolis.r: Amphipolis was a mixed community in which Athenians were a minority among other Greek settlers, which weakened loyalty to [[s:athens|Athens]]. It governed itself through an assembly and magistrates, honoured [[e:hagnon|Hagnon]] as founder and later the Spartan [[e:brasidas|Brasidas]], and grew rich on [[e:timber|timber]] for shipbuilding, precious metals and trade with [[e:thrace|Thrace]] and [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]].
amphipolis.e: [[e:brasidas|Brasidas]] captured it in 424 BCE; both he and the Athenian [[e:cleon|Cleon]] died in battle there in 422 BCE. Independent afterwards and never recovered by [[s:athens|Athens]], it fell to [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] in 357 BCE. It became a leading Macedonian city and mint, and in 167 BCE capital of one of the [[s:four-macedonian-republics|Four Macedonian Republics]].

al-andalus-umayyad-province.t: Iberia as a province of the Umayyad Caliphate of Damascus, ruled by governors from 711 until Abd al-Rahman I founded an independent emirate.
al-andalus-umayyad-province.o: In 711 [[e:tariq-ibn-ziyad|Tariq ibn Ziyad]] crossed from [[e:north-africa|North Africa]] with a mainly [[e:berbers|Berber]] army and defeated the Visigothic king [[e:roderic|Roderic]] near the [[e:guadalete|Guadalete]]. His superior [[e:musa-ibn-nusayr|Musa ibn Nusayr]] followed in 712, and within a few years most of the peninsula had been conquered, often by treaties with local lords such as [[e:theodemir-visigoth|Theodemir]] of [[s:tudmir|Tudmir]].
al-andalus-umayyad-province.r: [[e:al-andalus|Al-Andalus]] was governed by walis appointed from [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] or [[e:damascus|Damascus]], first from [[e:seville|Seville]] and from around 716 from [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]]. Christians and [[e:jews|Jews]] kept their faith in return for tribute. Raids pushed into [[e:gaul|Gaul]] until [[e:abd-al-rahman-al-ghafiqi|Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi]] was defeated near [[e:poitiers|Poitiers]] in 732. Tensions between [[e:arabs|Arabs]] and [[e:berbers|Berbers]] erupted in the Berber revolt of 740, after which Syrian troops under [[e:balj-ibn-bishr|Balj]] settled in the south.
al-andalus-umayyad-province.e: Rival Arab factions fought for power in the 740s and 750s. After the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]] overthrew the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyads]] in 750, the Umayyad prince Abd al-Rahman reached [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]], took [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in 756 and founded the [[s:emirate-of-cordoba|Emirate of Córdoba]].

allied-occupied-germany.t: Defeated Germany under the rule of the four Allied powers, divided into zones that grew into two German states.
allied-occupied-germany.o: After [[e:germany|Germany's]] unconditional surrender in May 1945, the [[e:berlin-declaration-1945|Berlin Declaration]] of 5 June 1945 transferred supreme authority to the [[s:united-states|United States]], the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], the [[s:united-kingdom|United Kingdom]] and [[e:france|France]]. Germany was divided into four occupation zones, [[e:berlin|Berlin]] into four sectors, and the lands east of the [[e:oder-neisse-line|Oder-Neisse line]] passed to Polish and Soviet administration.
allied-occupied-germany.r: The Allied Control Council coordinated policy under the [[e:potsdam-agreement|Potsdam Agreement]]: denazification, demilitarisation, democratisation and [[e:war-reparations|reparations]]. The major Nazi leaders were tried at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]]. Millions of Germans expelled from the east had to be resettled. Cooperation broke down as the [[e:cold-war|Cold War]] began: the western zones introduced the [[e:deutsche-mark|Deutsche Mark]] in 1948, and the [[e:soviet-union|Soviets]] blockaded [[e:west-berlin|West Berlin]], answered by the [[e:berlin-airlift|Berlin Airlift]].
allied-occupied-germany.e: In May 1949 the western zones became the [[s:federal-republic-of-germany|Federal Republic of Germany]], and in October 1949 the Soviet zone became the [[e:east-germany|German Democratic Republic]]. Allied rights over [[e:germany|Germany]] as a whole ended only with reunification in 1990.

alempois.t: One of the smallest ancient Estonian lands, a district of central Estonia known only from the chronicle of the Livonian crusade.
alempois.o: Alempois appears in [[e:henry-of-livonia|Henry of Livonia's]] chronicle as a small Estonian district near [[s:sakala|Sakala]] and [[s:nurmekund|Nurmekund]] in central [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]]. Its exact boundaries are uncertain.
alempois.r: It probably consisted of one or two parishes led by elders and shared the culture of the neighbouring Estonian counties. Nothing else is reliably known.
alempois.e: Alempois was taken during the crusaders' conquest of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]], completed in 1224, and came under the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]] and later the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]].

assuwa.t: Assuwa, a short-lived league of western Anatolian lands that rose against the Hittites c. 1430 BCE and may have given Asia its name.
assuwa.o: Assuwa was a coalition of 22 lands in north-western [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], including [[e:wilusa|Wilusiya]] and Taruisa, often linked with [[e:troy|Troy]]. It formed in the 15th century BCE in resistance to Hittite expansion westward.
assuwa.r: Known almost only from the annals of [[e:tudhaliya-i|Tudhaliya I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]], the league was led by Piyama-[[e:kurunta|Kurunta]] and his son Kukkuli. A bronze sword of [[e:aegean|Aegean]] type, inscribed with Tudhaliya's dedication after the victory over Assuwa, was found at [[e:hattusa|Hattusa]] in 1991.
assuwa.e: [[e:tudhaliya-i|Tudhaliya I]] defeated the coalition and deported thousands of soldiers and [[e:chariot|chariots]]. Kukkuli rebelled again and was killed. The name may survive in the Greek and Roman name [[e:asia|Asia]].

apollonia-pontica.t: Milesian colony on the Black Sea coast of Thrace whose colossal statue of Apollo was carried off to Rome in 72 BCE.
apollonia-pontica.o: Settlers from [[s:miletus|Miletus]] founded Apollonia c. 610 BCE on a peninsula and island on the western [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast, at modern Sozopol in [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]]. Named after [[e:apollo|Apollo]], it became one of the leading Greek cities of the Thracian coast.
apollonia-pontica.r: Apollonia traded wine, oil and fine pottery with the [[e:thracians|Thracians]], including the [[s:odrysian-kingdom|Odrysian Kingdom]], for grain, metals and honey. Its coins carried an anchor. In the 5th century BCE it set up a bronze statue of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] by [[e:calamis|Calamis]], about 13 metres high. It was governed as an oligarchy and later a democracy.
apollonia-pontica.e: In 72 BCE [[e:marcus-terentius-varro-lucullus|Marcus Lucullus]] captured Apollonia during the [[e:third-mithridatic-war|Third Mithridatic War]] and took the [[e:apollo|Apollo]] statue to the [[e:capitoline-hill|Capitol]] in [[e:rome|Rome]]. The city then came under Roman control and survives as Sozopol.

alwar-state.t: A Kachhwaha Rajput state of north-eastern Rajasthan, founded by the Naruka chief Pratap Singh in breakaway from Jaipur.
alwar-state.o: [[e:pratap-singh-prabhakar|Pratap Singh]], a Naruka [[e:kachhwaha|Kachhwaha]] noble of [[e:jaipur|Jaipur]], built up his own holding around [[s:rajgarh-state|Rajgarh]] and took the fort of Alwar in 1775, founding an independent state around 1770–75. He exploited the decline of the [[e:jats|Jats]] of [[s:bharatpur-state|Bharatpur]] and of Mughal power.
alwar-state.r: [[e:bakhtawar-singh-of-alwar|Bakhtawar Singh]] allied with the British against the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] in 1803 and received protection. Alwar had a 15-gun salute and a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] ruling class over a mixed [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and [[e:meos|Meo]] Muslim peasantry. [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:jai-singh-prabhakar|Jai Singh]] (1892–1937), a gifted but erratic ruler, was removed by the British in 1933 after a Meo uprising and misgovernment.
alwar-state.e: [[e:tej-singh-prabhakar|Tej Singh]] acceded to [[e:india|India]], and in March 1948 Alwar became the capital of the [[s:matsya-union|Matsya Union]], which joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1949.

asahan-sultanate.t: Malay sultanate on the east coast of Sumatra that grew rich from colonial plantations before its fall in the revolution of 1946.
asahan-sultanate.o: Tradition holds that Asahan was founded around 1630 by [[e:abdul-jalil-of-asahan|Abdul Jalil]], a son of [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:iskandar-muda|Iskandar Muda]] of the [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]] by a local woman, at the mouth of the Asahan river. For two centuries it was a minor coastal state under Acehnese and later Siak overlordship, trading with its [[e:batak|Batak]] hinterland.
asahan-sultanate.r: The sultan ruled from [[e:tanjungbalai|Tanjung Balai]] over Malay river communities and collected duties on forest products, [[e:rice|rice]] and slaves brought down from the [[e:batak|Batak]] highlands. [[e:dutch|Dutch]] control from 1865 turned Asahan into part of the plantation belt of [[e:east-sumatra|East Sumatra]], where tobacco, [[e:rubber|rubber]] and [[e:oil-palm|oil palm]] estates brought the court large concession revenues.
asahan-sultanate.e: The sultanate lived on as a self-governing domain of the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]]. During the social revolution in [[e:east-sumatra|East Sumatra]] in March 1946, the Malay aristocracy was attacked by revolutionary groups and the sultanate collapsed, its territory passing to the [[s:indonesia|Republic of Indonesia]].

ayutthaya-kingdom.t: The great Siamese kingdom on the Chao Phraya that for four centuries dominated mainland Southeast Asia's trade and welcomed merchants from Persia to Japan.
ayutthaya-kingdom.o: In 1351 [[e:ramathibodi-i|U Thong]], a ruler with links to Lavo and [[s:suphannaphum|Suphannaphum]], founded Ayutthaya on an island where the [[s:lavo-kingdom|Lopburi]], [[e:pa-sak-river|Pa Sak]] and [[e:chao-phraya-river|Chao Phraya]] rivers meet, and reigned as Ramathibodi I. The site gave access to the sea and to [[e:rice|rice]] lands of the central plain.
ayutthaya-kingdom.r: Ayutthaya's kings combined [[e:theravada-buddhism|Theravada Buddhist]] kingship with Khmer-style royal ritual. [[e:borommatrailokkanat|Borommatrailokkanat]] organised government into civil and military ministries and the sakdina ranking of land and status. The capital became a cosmopolitan port with Portuguese, [[e:dutch|Dutch]], Japanese, Chinese and Persian quarters; under [[e:narai|Narai]] it exchanged embassies with [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]]. It absorbed [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]], sacked [[e:angkor|Angkor]] in 1431 and fought long wars with [[s:myanmar|Burma]].
ayutthaya-kingdom.e: [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]] of the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] conquered Ayutthaya in 1569, but [[e:naresuan|Naresuan]] restored independence in 1584. In 1767 Konbaung armies sacked and burned the city, ending the kingdom. [[e:taksin|Taksin]] rallied resistance from [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi]], and the ruins of Ayutthaya are now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

awadh-state.t: The kingdom of the Nawabs of Awadh, whose courts at Faizabad and Lucknow were famed for refinement, until its British annexation helped spark 1857.
awadh-state.o: In 1722 the Mughal emperor [[e:muhammad-shah-mughal-emperor|Muhammad Shah]] appointed [[e:saadat-ali-khan-i|Saadat Ali Khan]], a Shia noble from [[e:nishapur|Nishapur]], as governor of [[e:awadh|Awadh]]. As Mughal power weakened, he and his nephew [[e:safdar-jang|Safdar Jang]] made the governorship hereditary, ruling the rich middle [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]] from [[e:faizabad|Faizabad]] and, from 1775, [[e:lucknow|Lucknow]].
awadh-state.r: [[e:shuja-ud-daula|Shuja ud-Daula]]'s defeat at [[e:battle-of-buxar|Buxar]] in 1764 made [[e:awadh|Awadh]] a subsidiary ally of the [[e:east-india-company|British East India Company]], which stationed troops at its expense. [[e:asaf-ud-daula|Asaf ud-Daula]] built the [[e:bara-imambara|Bara Imambara]] in [[e:lucknow|Lucknow]], and the court patronised [[e:urdu|Urdu]] poetry, kathak dance, thumri music and a celebrated cuisine. [[e:ghazi-ud-din-haidar-shah|Ghazi ud-Din Haidar]] took the title of king in 1819 with British encouragement. Shia [[e:islam|Islam]] was the court religion.
awadh-state.e: Governor-General [[e:lord-dalhousie|Dalhousie]] annexed [[e:awadh|Awadh]] in 1856, alleging misrule, and exiled [[e:wajid-ali-shah|Wajid Ali Shah]] to [[e:kolkata|Calcutta]]. Resentment among Awadhi soldiers and landholders fed the 1857 rebellion, in which [[e:begum-hazrat-mahal|Begum Hazrat Mahal]] led resistance at [[e:lucknow|Lucknow]].

azerbaijan.t: The independent Republic of Azerbaijan on the Caspian Sea, an oil and gas producer whose post-Soviet history has been dominated by the Karabakh conflict.
azerbaijan.o: The [[s:azerbaijan-ssr|Azerbaijan SSR]] declared independence on 30 August 1991, confirmed by a constitutional act on 18 October 1991, and became fully sovereign with the dissolution of the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] in December. It claimed descent from the [[s:azerbaijan-democratic-republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]] of 1918-1920, whose flag it readopted, while war with Armenian forces over [[e:nagorno-karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh]] was already under way.
azerbaijan.r: After defeat in the [[e:first-nagorno-karabakh-war|First Karabakh War]] and a 1994 ceasefire that left Armenian forces holding [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]] and surrounding districts, [[e:heydar-aliyev|Heydar Aliyev]], president from 1993, built a strong presidential system, passed to his son [[e:ilham-aliyev|Ilham Aliyev]] in 2003. The 1994 Contract of the Century and the [[e:baku-tbilisi-ceyhan-pipeline|Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan]] pipeline, opened in 2005, brought oil wealth and Western investment. The state is secular, with a Shia majority.
azerbaijan.e: In the 2020 war Azerbaijan regained much of the lost territory, and a 2023 offensive brought all of [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]] under its control, prompting the flight of its Armenian population. Peace talks with [[s:armenia|Armenia]] continue.

anlo.t: The leading Ewe state on the coast of south-eastern Ghana, centred on Anloga by the Keta lagoon, a trading and military power until British annexation.
anlo.o: Anlo tradition traces its people to [[e:notsie|Notsie]], in modern [[e:togo|Togo]], from which the [[e:ewe-people|Ewe]] escaped the tyranny of King [[e:agokoli|Agokoli]] and dispersed, probably in the 17th century. Under their leader Sri I the Anlo settled the sandbar between the sea and the [[e:keta|Keta]] lagoon and made [[e:anloga|Anloga]] their capital, gradually becoming the most important of the coastal Ewe states.
anlo.r: The paramount ruler, the [[e:awoamefia|Awoamefia]], was a sacred figure who lived largely in seclusion, while war leaders and lineage heads handled daily affairs. The army was organised in three wings. Anlo traded fish, salt and slaves with Europeans at [[e:keta|Keta]], where the [[e:danes|Danes]] built [[e:fort-prinzenstein|Fort Prinzenstein]] in 1784, and it fought long wars with the Ga, Ada and [[s:akwamu|Akwamu]]. Shrine societies such as [[e:yewe|Yewe]] were influential.
anlo.e: British forces campaigned in the region in the 1860s and 1870s, and after the defeat of the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] in 1874 Anlo was annexed to the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]], despite resistance into 1878. The [[e:awoamefia|Awoamefia]] remains the traditional ruler of the Anlo state.

annazid-dynasty.t: A Kurdish dynasty that controlled the Zagros passes between Iraq and Iran from its base at Hulwan for over a century.
annazid-dynasty.o: [[e:abul-fath-muhammad-ibn-annaz|Abu'l-Fath Muhammad ibn Annaz]], chief of the Kurdish Shadhanjan tribe, established himself at [[e:hulwan|Hulwan]] on the road from [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]] to [[e:hamadan|Hamadan]] around 990, as [[e:buyid-dynasty|Buyid]] authority weakened. The Annazids competed with the [[s:hasanwayhid-dynasty|Hasanwayhid dynasty]], taking over much of their territory after 1015.
annazid-dynasty.r: The Annazids were tribal rulers who controlled key passes, collecting tolls and tribute and playing [[s:buyid-dynasty|Buyids]], [[s:kakuyid-dynasty|Kakuyids]] and other neighbours against each other. [[e:abul-shawk-faris|Abu'l-Shawk Faris]] extended their power to [[e:dinavar|Dinavar]] and [[e:kermanshah|Kermanshah]], but family feuds were frequent. Their towns included [[e:hulwan|Hulwan]], Dinavar and [[e:shahrizor|Shahrizor]].
annazid-dynasty.e: The arrival of the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] in the 1040s brought repeated invasions, and the Annazids became Seljuk [[e:vassal|vassals]]. They lost their last strongholds around 1117.

astrakhan-khanate.t: A Tatar khanate at the mouth of the Volga, a successor of the Golden Horde whose annexation in 1556 gave Russia the whole Volga route.
astrakhan-khanate.o: The Astrakhan Khanate formed in the 1460s around the town of [[e:astrakhan|Xacitarxan]] near the [[e:volga|Volga]] delta, under khans descended from [[e:kuchuk-muhammad|Küchük Muhammad]] of the [[s:great-horde|Great Horde]]. It became fully independent after the Great Horde's destruction in 1502.
astrakhan-khanate.r: The khanate was small and relatively weak, controlling the fisheries and trade of the lower [[e:volga|Volga]], including the [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] towards the Caspian and [[e:persia|Persia]]. Its population of [[e:tatars|Tatars]] and [[e:nogais|Nogais]] lived largely by herding and trade. Its khans were frequently dependent on the [[s:nogai-horde|Nogai Horde]] or the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]], and several were installed by these neighbours.
astrakhan-khanate.e: After taking [[e:kazan|Kazan]], [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV]] turned south: Russian forces installed a client khan, [[e:dervish-ali|Dervish Ali]], in 1554 and annexed the khanate in 1556. [[e:astrakhan|Astrakhan]] became a Russian fortress city and gateway to the Caspian and the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]].

ayyubid-emirate-of-aleppo.t: The Ayyubid principality of northern Syria whose rulers built much of the Citadel of Aleppo as it stands today.
ayyubid-emirate-of-aleppo.o: [[e:saladin|Saladin]] took [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] from the [[s:zengid-dynasty|Zengids]] in 1183 and in 1186 gave it to his son [[e:az-zahir-ghazi|al-Zahir Ghazi]], whose line ruled it until the Mongol invasion.
ayyubid-emirate-of-aleppo.r: [[e:az-zahir-ghazi|Al-Zahir Ghazi]] rebuilt the Citadel of [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] with its sloping glacis, monumental gate and water supply, and endowed [[e:madrasa|madrasas]]. His widow [[e:dayfa-khatun|Dayfa Khatun]], a niece of [[e:saladin|Saladin]], governed as regent from 1236 to 1242, one of the few women to rule in medieval [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], and founded the [[e:madrasa-al-firdaws|Firdaws]] madrasa. Aleppo kept treaties with [[e:venice|Venice]] and the [[s:principality-of-antioch|Principality of Antioch]] and flourished on trade. [[e:al-nasir-yusuf|Al-Nasir Yusuf]] took [[e:damascus|Damascus]] in 1250, ruling most of [[e:syria|Syria]].
ayyubid-emirate-of-aleppo.e: [[e:hulagu-khan|Hulagu's]] [[e:mongols|Mongols]] stormed [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] in January 1260 and massacred many inhabitants. [[e:al-nasir-yusuf|Al-Nasir Yusuf]] fled, was captured and was later killed by the Mongols. After [[e:battle-of-ain-jalut|Ain Jalut]], Aleppo passed to the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]].

aksumite-yemen.t: Yemen under Ethiopian Christian rule, best known for Abraha, who repaired the Marib Dam and, by tradition, marched on Mecca with an elephant.
aksumite-yemen.o: In 525 the [[s:aksumite-empire|Aksumite Empire]] under [[e:kaleb|King Kaleb]] crossed the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] to avenge the [[e:massacre-of-najran|Christians of Najran]], defeated the Himyarite king Yusuf and installed [[e:sumyafa-ashwa|Sumyafa Ashwa]], a local Christian, as [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]]. Within a few years the Aksumite general [[e:abraha|Abraha]] overthrew him and made himself ruler, nominally under [[e:aksumite-empire|Aksum]].
aksumite-yemen.r: [[e:abraha|Abraha]] governed in practice independently from Sanaa. His inscriptions record the restoration of the [[e:marib-dam|Marib Dam]] in 548 and a diplomatic conference attended by envoys of the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]], [[e:persia|Persia]] and the Arab kings. He built a great church in Sanaa and campaigned deep into central [[e:arabia|Arabia]]; Muslim tradition remembers his failed expedition against [[e:mecca|Mecca]] in the Year of the Elephant.
aksumite-yemen.e: [[e:abraha|Abraha's]] sons Yaksum and Masruq were unpopular. The Himyarite noble [[e:sayf-ibn-dhi-yazan|Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan]] sought help from [[e:persia|Persia]], and around 570 a Sasanian force under [[e:wahriz|Wahriz]] defeated the Ethiopians, opening the period of [[s:sasanian-yemen|Sasanian Yemen]].

aq-qoyunlu.t: The 'White Sheep' Turkmen confederation that rose from Diyarbakir to rule Iran under Uzun Hasan before giving way to the Safavids.
aq-qoyunlu.o: The Aq Qoyunlu were led by the Bayandur clan among the [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] tribes pasturing around [[e:diyarbakir|Diyarbakir]] in the late 14th century. Their chief [[e:qara-yuluk-osman|Qara Yuluk Osman]] fought the [[s:kadi-burhan-al-din-state|Kadi Burhan al-Din state]] and the [[s:qara-qoyunlu|Qara Qoyunlu]], sided with [[e:timur|Timur]], and was rewarded with Diyarbakir.
aq-qoyunlu.r: [[e:uzun-hasan|Uzun Hasan]] defeated the [[s:qara-qoyunlu|Qara Qoyunlu]] ruler [[e:jahan-shah-qara-qoyunlu|Jahan Shah]] in 1467 and the [[e:abu-said-mirza|Timurid Abu Sa'id]] in 1469, making [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] his capital and ruling [[e:iran|Iran]], [[e:iraq|Iraq]] and eastern [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. He allied with [[e:venice|Venice]] against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], but [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] defeated him at [[e:battle-of-otlukbeli|Otlukbeli]] in 1473. His son [[e:yaqub-aq-qoyunlu|Ya'qub]] kept a Persianate court that patronised poets and painters, while tribal chiefs held real military power.
aq-qoyunlu.e: After [[e:yaqub-aq-qoyunlu|Ya'qub]]'s death in 1490 the confederation split among rival princes. Ismail, grandson of [[e:uzun-hasan|Uzun Hasan]] through his daughter, defeated them in 1501 and founded the Safavid state; the last Aq Qoyunlu ruler, Murad, was driven out in 1503.

africa-proconsularis.t: Rome's richest African province, centred on rebuilt Carthage, the granary of Rome and a heartland of Latin Christianity.
africa-proconsularis.o: After destroying [[e:carthage|Carthage]] in 146 BCE, the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]] made its territory the province of [[e:africa|Africa]], governed from [[s:utica|Utica]]. In 46 BCE [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] added Numidian lands as [[e:africa-nova|Africa Nova]], and under Augustus the two were joined as Africa Proconsularis, governed by a senatorial proconsul. Carthage was refounded as a Roman colony and became the capital.
africa-proconsularis.r: The province supplied much of [[e:rome|Rome's]] grain and, later, [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and fine red pottery, and its cities, such as [[e:dougga|Thugga]], [[e:el-djem|Thysdrus]] and [[s:leptis-magna|Leptis Magna]], were full of temples, baths and amphitheatres. Punic and [[e:berbers|Berber]] survived beside [[e:latin|Latin]]. In 238 a revolt at Thysdrus proclaimed the governor [[e:gordian-i|Gordian I]] emperor. [[e:africa|Africa]] became a centre of Latin [[e:christianity|Christianity]], home of [[e:tertullian|Tertullian]] and [[e:cyprian|Cyprian]], and was divided by the [[e:donatism|Donatist]] schism.
africa-proconsularis.e: [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]] split the province around 303, creating [[s:byzacena|Byzacena]] and [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]]. The [[e:vandals|Vandals]], who had crossed from [[e:spain|Spain]] in 429, took [[e:carthage|Carthage]] in 439, founding the [[s:vandal-kingdom|Vandal Kingdom]]. Justinian's reconquest restored Roman rule in 534.

appenzell-ausserrhoden.t: The Reformed half of Appenzell, created in 1597, which became one of the most industrialised rural areas of early modern Europe.
appenzell-ausserrhoden.o: When the [[s:canton-of-appenzell|Canton of Appenzell]] was divided in 1597, the outer districts, which had adopted the Reformed faith, formed Ausserrhoden. Without the old capital, its [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]] met alternately in [[e:trogen|Trogen]] and [[e:hundwil|Hundwil]], and government business was shared between Trogen and [[e:herisau|Herisau]].
appenzell-ausserrhoden.r: From the 17th century the villagers spun and wove linen and later [[e:cotton|cotton]] at home, and merchant families such as the Zellwegers of [[e:trogen|Trogen]] grew rich in international trade. Government lay with the [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]] and councils, and the half-canton shared a vote with Innerrhoden at the federal [[e:tagsatzung|Diet]].
appenzell-ausserrhoden.e: In 1798 it was absorbed into the canton of [[e:canton-of-santis|Säntis]] of the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]], and in 1803 it was restored as a half-canton. Ausserrhoden abolished its [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]] in 1997 and remains a Swiss canton.

azzi-hayasa.t: Azzi-Hayasa, a mountain confederation of north-eastern Anatolia that fought the Hittites in the 14th century BCE.
azzi-hayasa.o: Hayasa and Azzi were lands in the highlands of the upper [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and the [[e:erzurum|Erzurum]] region. They appear in Hittite records from the 15th century BCE as a federation of mountain communities beyond the Hittite frontier.
azzi-hayasa.r: Little is known of its internal structure. [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] made a treaty with Hukkana of Hayasa and gave him his sister in marriage, with strict rules about Hittite customs. Some scholars connect Hayasa with the Armenian name for [[s:armenia|Armenia]], Hay, though this is disputed.
azzi-hayasa.e: [[e:mursili-ii|Mursili II]] fought Anniya of Azzi in long campaigns, and Hayasa disappears from the record in the 13th century BCE. The highlands later formed part of [[s:nairi|Nairi]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]].

austrian-delagoa-bay.t: The Habsburg monarchy's only African colony, a brief trading venture on Delagoa Bay led by the adventurer William Bolts.
austrian-delagoa-bay.o: [[e:william-bolts|William Bolts]], a former [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] servant, persuaded the Austrian government of [[e:maria-theresa|Maria Theresa]] to back a trading venture to the East under the imperial flag. In 1777 he landed at [[e:delagoa-bay|Delagoa Bay]] and signed agreements with local [[e:tsonga-people|Tsonga]] rulers, including the [[s:tembe-kingdom|Tembe Kingdom]], to establish trading posts.
austrian-delagoa-bay.r: The Austrian posts, run by agents of Bolts's company and later the [[e:imperial-asiatic-company-of-trieste|Imperial Asiatic Company of Trieste]], traded cloth and metal goods for [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]]. The settlement was tiny and dependent on the goodwill of local rulers, and it was meant to link Austrian trade with [[e:india|India]] and [[e:china|China]].
austrian-delagoa-bay.e: Portugal, which claimed the bay, sent a naval force in 1781 that expelled the Austrians and built a fort. Bolts's company soon failed, and [[e:austria|Austria]] made no further colonial attempts in [[e:africa|Africa]].

alodia.t: The southernmost Christian kingdom of Nubia, centred on Soba near modern Khartoum, which lasted for nearly a thousand years.
alodia.o: Alodia (Alwa) arose by around 500 in the region of the Blue and [[e:white-nile|White Niles]] and the [[e:butana|Butana]] plain, once the heartland of the [[s:kushite-empire|Kushite Empire]] of [[e:meroe|Meroë]]. Its capital was [[e:soba|Soba]], on the [[e:blue-nile|Blue Nile]]. Around 580 the Miaphysite [[e:bishop|bishop]] [[e:longinus-missionary|Longinus]], who had earlier converted [[s:nobadia|Nobadia]], brought [[e:christianity|Christianity]] to the court.
alodia.r: Alodia was the largest of the Nubian kingdoms, with farmland, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and trade routes to the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] and [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]]. The 10th-century Egyptian writer [[e:ibn-sulaym-al-aswani|Ibn Sulaym al-Aswani]] described it as richer and more populous than [[s:makuria|Makuria]], with many churches at [[e:soba|Soba]] and a ruler governing through subordinate kings. Soba's excavated churches and imported glass and pottery confirm its wealth.
alodia.e: From the 12th century Alodia declined, losing territory to Arab nomads. Around 1504 [[e:soba|Soba]] fell to an alliance of the [[s:abdallab-sheikhdom|Abdallab]] [[e:arabs|Arabs]] and the [[e:funj-sultanate-of-sennar|Funj]], founding the [[s:funj-sultanate|Funj Sultanate]]. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] faded, though memories of Soba lived on in Sudanese tradition.

acarnanian-league.t: Federation of the Acarnanian towns of western Greece, a long-standing enemy of the Aetolians and an ally first of Athens and later of Macedon.
acarnanian-league.o: [[e:acarnania|Acarnania]], between the [[e:ambracian-gulf|Ambracian Gulf]] and the Achelous river, was a land of small towns and villages. By the mid-5th century BCE they were acting together as a league with its meeting place at Stratos. Hostility to Corinth's colonies in the region pushed them into alliance with [[s:athens|Athens]], whose general [[e:phormio|Phormio]] campaigned with them in the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]].
acarnanian-league.r: The league had a federal assembly, council and elected general ([[e:strategos|strategos]]), and struck federal coins. Its members were mainly farmers and herders known as skilled slingers and fighters. Ancient writers considered the [[e:acarnania|Acarnanians]] conservative and fiercely loyal to allies, especially in their long struggle against the expanding [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]].
acarnanian-league.e: [[e:aetolia|Aetolia]] and [[e:epirus|Epirus]] partitioned [[e:acarnania|Acarnania]] in the mid-3rd century BCE, but the league was restored around 230 BCE and sided with [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]]. [[s:leucas|Leucas]] served as the federal capital from 197 BCE until [[e:rome|Rome]] detached it from the league in 167 BCE. The league faded under Roman rule; after [[e:battle-of-actium|Actium]] in 31 BCE [[e:augustus-roman-emperor|Augustus]] moved much of its population to his new city of [[e:nicopolis-epirus|Nicopolis]].

albanian-kingdom-1943-1944.t: Nominally independent Albanian state set up by Germany after Italy's surrender in 1943, which kept Kosovo but was defeated by the Communist Partisans.
albanian-kingdom-1943-1944.o: When [[e:italy|Italy]] capitulated in September 1943, German troops occupied the [[s:albanian-kingdom-1939-1943|Albanian Kingdom]] (1939-1943). Seeking local support, [[e:germany|Germany]] declared [[s:albania|Albania]] independent, convened a national assembly and set up a Regency Council headed by [[e:mehdi-frasheri|Mehdi Frashëri]], with Albanian governments led successively by figures such as [[e:rexhep-mitrovica|Rexhep Mitrovica]].
albanian-kingdom-1943-1944.r: The regime claimed neutrality and kept the Albanian-inhabited lands of [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] and western Macedonia added in 1941, while [[e:germany|Germany]] controlled the military situation. Some nationalists of the [[e:balli-kombetar|Balli Kombëtar]] cooperated with the Germans against the Partisans, and an SS division was recruited in Kosovo. Many [[e:jews|Jews]] in [[s:albania|Albania]] were sheltered by Albanian families and survived.
albanian-kingdom-1943-1944.e: [[e:enver-hoxha|Enver Hoxha's]] Partisans won the civil war and took [[e:tirana|Tirana]] on 17 November 1944 as German forces withdrew. The communists then founded what became the [[s:peoples-socialist-republic-of-albania|People's Socialist Republic of Albania]], and [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] returned to [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]].
albanian-kingdom-1943-1944.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

akatziri.t: A steppe people north of the Black Sea who were drawn into Attila's empire and later appear among the forerunners of the Khazars.
akatziri.o: The Akatziri are first mentioned by the Byzantine envoy [[e:priscus|Priscus]] in the 440s as a people of the Pontic steppe ruled by many chiefs. [[e:jordanes|Jordanes]] later described them as a strong people who lived by herding and hunting. Their origins and language are unknown; they were probably a Hunnic or early Turkic group.
akatziri.r: Around 448 the Eastern Roman emperor [[e:theodosius-ii|Theodosius II]] tried to bribe their chiefs to turn against [[e:attila|Attila]], but the gifts went to the wrong chief, Kuridachus, who betrayed the plan. Attila then subdued them and set his eldest son [[e:ellac|Ellac]] over them as king, bringing them firmly into the [[s:hunnic-empire|Hunnic Empire]].
akatziri.e: After the collapse of Hun power in the 450s and 460s, the Akatziri disappear from the record, displaced or absorbed by the [[e:saragurs|Saragurs]], [[s:sabirs|Sabirs]] and [[s:onogurs|Onogurs]]. Some historians link them to the later [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]], though the connection is unproven.

aqrabi-sheikhdom.t: A tiny sheikhdom west of Aden whose land included the peninsula where Britain built the Little Aden oil refinery.
aqrabi-sheikhdom.o: The Aqrabi tribe held a small coastal district west of [[e:aden|Aden]], with its seat at Bir Ahmad. They broke from the neighbouring [[s:sultanate-of-lahej|Sultanate of Lahej]] in the 18th century to form their own sheikhdom. Its early history is poorly known.
aqrabi-sheikhdom.r: With only a few thousand inhabitants, the sheikhdom lived from farming, fishing and its position near [[e:aden|Aden]]. In the 1860s [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] bought the [[e:little-aden|Little Aden]] peninsula from the Aqrabi sheikh, and it became part of [[s:aden-settlement|British Aden]]; a large oil refinery opened there in 1954. The sheikhdom was a British-protected state and joined the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]].
aqrabi-sheikhdom.e: In 1967 the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over, and the territory was incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

anuradhapura-kingdom.t: Sri Lanka's longest-lived kingdom, where Theravada Buddhism took root and kings built vast irrigation tanks and giant stupas over 1,400 years.
anuradhapura-kingdom.o: The chronicles say King [[e:pandukabhaya|Pandukabhaya]] founded [[e:anuradhapura|Anuradhapura]] around 437 BCE, succeeding the [[s:kingdom-of-tambapanni|Kingdom of Tambapanni]]. In the 3rd century BCE, under [[e:devanampiya-tissa|Devanampiya Tissa]], the monk [[e:mahinda-buddhist-monk|Mahinda]], son of the [[e:maurya-empire|Maurya]] emperor [[e:ashoka|Ashoka]], brought [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]], and a sapling of the Bodhi tree was planted in the city. Around 161 BCE [[e:dutugemunu|Dutugemunu]] defeated the Tamil ruler [[e:ellalan|Elara]] and united the island.
anuradhapura-kingdom.r: Kings ruled with close ties to the Buddhist sangha; the [[e:mahavihara|Mahavihara]] and Abhayagiri monasteries were rival centres of learning, and the Pali Canon was first written down in the 1st century BCE. Huge stupas such as the [[e:ruwanwelisaya|Ruwanwelisaya]] and [[e:jetavanaramaya|Jetavanaramaya]] rose in the capital. [[e:rice|Rice]] farming depended on great [[e:reservoir|reservoirs]] like [[e:kala-wewa|Kala Wewa]], built by [[e:dhatusena|Dhatusena]], and ports traded with [[e:india|India]], [[e:rome|Rome]] and [[e:china|China]].
anuradhapura-kingdom.e: Repeated invasions from [[e:south-india|South India]] weakened the kingdom. The [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] under [[e:rajaraja-i|Rajaraja I]] took [[e:anuradhapura|Anuradhapura]] in 993, and in 1017 [[e:rajendra-chola-i|Rajendra I]] captured King [[e:mahinda-v|Mahinda V]]. The Sinhalese capital later moved to [[e:polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]], beginning the [[s:polonnaruwa-kingdom|Polonnaruwa Kingdom]].

aizu-domain.t: The Tokugawa branch domain in northern Japan whose loyalty to the shogunate ended in the tragic siege of Wakamatsu castle in 1868.
aizu-domain.o: After the Uesugi were moved to [[e:yonezawa|Yonezawa]] in 1601, [[e:aizu|Aizu]] passed to [[e:gamo-hideyuki|Gamo Hideyuki]] and then to [[e:kato-yoshiaki|Kato Yoshiaki]]. In 1643 the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] gave it to [[e:hoshina-masayuki|Hoshina Masayuki]], half-brother of Shogun [[e:tokugawa-iemitsu|Tokugawa Iemitsu]], with 230,000 koku; his descendants, later surnamed Matsudaira, held it until the end.
aizu-domain.r: [[e:hoshina-masayuki|Masayuki]]'s house code bound his heirs to absolute loyalty to the [[e:shogun|shogun]]. [[e:aizu|Aizu]] was known for strict [[e:samurai|samurai]] education at the Nisshinkan school, and for [[e:lacquerware|lacquerware]] and sake. In 1862 [[e:matsudaira-katamori|Matsudaira Katamori]] became [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] protector, policing the capital with the [[e:shinsengumi|Shinsengumi]] and fighting [[e:choshu-domain|Choshu]] radicals.
aizu-domain.e: Branded an enemy after 1868, [[e:aizu|Aizu]] was the target of the imperial army; the [[s:ouetsu-reppan-domei|Ouetsu Reppan Domei]] formed partly to defend it. [[e:tsuruga-castle|Wakamatsu castle]] fell after a month-long siege, during which young Byakkotai soldiers took their own lives. The clan was exiled to Tonami in the far north.

aruba.t: Island off Venezuela that left the Netherlands Antilles in 1986 to become a separate country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
aruba.o: Arubans had long resented domination by [[s:curacao|Curaçao]] within the [[s:colony-of-curacao|Colony of Curaçao]] and the [[s:netherlands-antilles|Netherlands Antilles]]. Led by [[e:betico-croes|Gilberto 'Betico' Croes]] and his [[e:peoples-electoral-movement-aruba|People's Electoral Movement]], they won a referendum for separation in 1977, and on 1 January 1986 Aruba gained 'status aparte' as an autonomous country in the kingdom, with independence planned for 1996.
aruba.r: Aruba has its own parliament, prime minister, constitution and currency, the florin, while the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] manages defence and foreign affairs and a governor represents the monarch. The closure of the [[e:lago-oil-and-transport-company|Lago]] oil refinery in 1985 forced a rapid turn to tourism, which now dominates. [[e:papiamento|Papiamento]] and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] are official languages. [[e:henny-eman|Henny Eman]] became the first prime minister, followed by leaders such as [[e:nelson-oduber|Nelson Oduber]] and [[e:evelyn-wever-croes|Evelyn Wever-Croes]].
aruba.e: In 1990 Aruba asked to postpone independence, and in 1995 the plan was dropped, leaving it a permanent country within the kingdom. It remains among the most prosperous [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] islands, though heavily dependent on American tourism.

achaemenid-egypt.t: Egypt as a satrapy of the Persian Empire, ruled by Persian kings who were also crowned as pharaohs.
achaemenid-egypt.o: In 525 BCE [[e:cambyses-ii|Cambyses II]] defeated [[e:psamtik-iii|Psamtik III]] of the [[s:twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt|Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt]] at [[e:pelusium|Pelusium]] and took [[e:memphis-egypt|Memphis]], making [[e:egypt|Egypt]] a province of the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]]. [[e:manetho|Manetho]] counts the Persian kings as the Twenty-seventh Dynasty. The Egyptian official [[e:udjahorresnet|Udjahorresnet]] helped Cambyses adopt pharaonic titles.
achaemenid-egypt.r: A Persian [[e:satrapy|satrap]] governed from [[e:memphis-egypt|Memphis]], collecting tribute in grain and [[e:silver|silver]]. [[e:darius-i|Darius I]] had Egyptian laws collected, completed the [[e:nile|Nile]] to [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] canal and built the temple of [[e:temple-of-hibis|Hibis]] in the [[e:kharga-oasis|Kharga Oasis]]. [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] served as the administrative language beside Egyptian, and a garrison of Jewish soldiers at Elephantine left a rich archive of Aramaic papyri. Revolts broke out in 486 BCE and under [[e:inaros-ii|Inaros]], who was supported by [[s:athens|Athens]], around 460 BCE.
achaemenid-egypt.e: After the death of [[e:darius-ii|Darius II]], the Saite noble [[e:amyrtaeus|Amyrtaeus]] rebelled in 404 BCE and freed [[e:egypt|Egypt]], founding the [[s:twenty-eighth-dynasty-of-egypt|Twenty-eighth Dynasty of Egypt]]. [[e:persia|Persia]] reconquered the country in 343 BCE.

akuapem.t: A small Akan and Guan state on the Akuapem ridge north of Accra, formed after the fall of Akwamu and later a centre of Basel Mission Christianity and Twi literacy.
akuapem.o: The Akuapem ridge was home to [[e:guan-people|Guan]]-speaking towns that had been subject to [[s:akwamu|Akwamu]]. In 1733, after [[s:akyem-abuakwa|Akyem Abuakwa]] and its allies broke [[e:akwamu|Akwamu]] power, the ridge towns accepted an Akyem leader, Safori, as their ruler. He became the first Okuapehene, with his capital at [[e:akropong|Akropong]], and the new state joined Guan and [[e:akan|Akan]] communities under one paramount chief.
akuapem.r: Akuapem followed [[e:akan|Akan]] political forms, with a paramount chief, divisional chiefs and the [[e:odwira-festival|Odwira festival]], while [[e:guan-people|Guan]] towns kept their own traditions. Farmers on the ridge later led the expansion of cocoa growing in the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast]]. The [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] Mission settled at [[e:akropong|Akropong]] in 1835, and missionaries such as [[e:johann-gottlieb-christaller|Johann Christaller]] made [[e:akuapem-twi|Akuapem Twi]] the basis of a written Twi language and Bible.
akuapem.e: Akuapem came under British protection and was absorbed into the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]] in 1874. The Okuapehene still reigns at [[e:akropong|Akropong]], and the town remains an important educational and church centre in [[e:ghana|Ghana]].

aowin.t: A gold-producing Akan kingdom of the Anyi people on the forest frontier of modern Ghana and Ivory Coast, best remembered for raiding Kumasi before its defeat by the Ashanti Empire.
aowin.o: Aowin took shape in the 17th century in the forested country west of the [[e:tano-river|Tano]] river, settled by [[e:anyi-people|Anyi]]-speaking [[e:akan|Akan]] groups who had migrated from the north and east. Its rise belongs to the same period of gold-fuelled state building that produced [[s:denkyira|Denkyira]] and [[s:akwamu|Akwamu]], and it held land along the trade paths that ran from the goldfields towards the coast.
aowin.r: Little is documented about its institutions, which are known mainly from [[e:akan|Akan]] oral tradition and scattered European notes. Like its neighbours it was ruled by a king from a royal matrilineage, supported by chiefs of subordinate towns. Its wealth came from alluvial and mined gold and from the slaves and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] carried to coastal forts. Religion was the Akan worship of a creator god, lesser deities and ancestors.
aowin.e: In the early 18th century Aowin forces under [[e:ebiri-moro|Ebiri Moro]] raided [[e:kumasi|Kumasi]], but the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] retaliated and overran the kingdom. Many Aowin moved west and south, where their descendants founded or strengthened the [[e:anyi-people|Anyi]] states of the lagoon country, notably the [[s:kingdom-of-sanwi|Kingdom of Sanwi]] at [[e:krinjabo|Krinjabo]].

aulerci-cenomani.t: Gallic people of Maine, centred on Le Mans, a branch of whom crossed the Alps and founded the Celtic towns of Brescia and Verona.
aulerci-cenomani.o: The [[s:cenomani|Cenomani]] were the largest branch of the [[e:aulerci|Aulerci]] and held the [[e:sarthe|Sarthe]] valley around [[e:le-mans|Vindinum]] (Le Mans). [[e:livy|Livy]] and [[e:polybius|Polybius]] report that part of the people migrated across the [[e:alps|Alps]] around 400 BCE and settled north of the Po, where the Italian Cenomani founded [[e:brescia|Brixia]] ([[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]]) and became allies of [[e:rome|Rome]] against the other [[e:gaul|Gauls]].
aulerci-cenomani.r: Little is known of the Gallic [[s:cenomani|Cenomani]] at home. They struck gold coins and controlled the route between the [[e:loire|Loire]] and the [[e:english-channel|Channel]] coast.
aulerci-cenomani.e: They joined the great revolt of 52 BCE and sent five thousand men to relieve [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]]. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:le-mans|Vindinum]] grew into a walled town, later called Civitas Cenomanorum, from which come the names Le Mans and [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]].

cr.a: Cénomans (peuple celtique de Gaule). Autorité émettrice de monnaie

antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia.t: Kingdom of the Antigonid dynasty, which ruled Macedon and dominated Greece for over a century until defeated by Rome at Pydna in 168 BCE.
antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia.o: [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus I Monophthalmus]] and his son [[e:demetrius-i-of-macedon|Demetrius Poliorcetes]], generals of Alexander, took the royal title in 306 BCE while ruling in Asia. Demetrius seized [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] in 294 BCE but lost it in 288 BCE. His son [[e:antigonus-ii-gonatas|Antigonus II Gonatas]] won the throne after defeating the [[e:gauls|Gauls]] at [[e:lysimachia|Lysimachia]] in 277 BCE, founding a stable dynasty at [[s:pella|Pella]].
antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia.r: [[e:antigonid-dynasty|Antigonid]] kings ruled [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] directly through a landed aristocracy and a citizen army famous for its [[e:sarissa|sarissa]] [[e:phalanx|phalanx]], while controlling [[e:greece|Greece]] through garrisons at [[s:corinth|Corinth]], [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]] and [[e:demetrias|Demetrias]], the 'fetters of Greece'. They patronised philosophy and the arts. [[e:antigonus-iii-doson|Antigonus III Doson]] formed a Hellenic alliance and defeated [[s:sparta|Sparta]] at [[e:battle-of-sellasia|Sellasia]] in 222 BCE.
antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia.e: [[e:philip-v-of-macedon|Philip V]]'s alliance with [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] led to wars with [[e:rome|Rome]]; defeat at [[e:battle-of-cynoscephalae|Cynoscephalae]] in 197 BCE confined him to [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]]. His son [[e:perseus-of-macedon|Perseus]] lost to [[e:lucius-aemilius-paullus-macedonicus|Lucius Aemilius Paullus]] at [[e:battle-of-pydna|Pydna]] in 168 BCE. Rome abolished the monarchy and divided the land into the [[s:four-macedonian-republics|Four Macedonian Republics]].

cr.a: Marsyas (French original); Kordas (Spanish translation); derivative work by MinisterForBadTimes

aurunci.t: Ancient Italic people of the coast between Latium and Campania, whose towns were destroyed by Rome in 314 BCE.
aurunci.o: The Aurunci, called Ausones by the [[e:greeks|Greeks]], lived between the Liri and [[e:volturno|Volturno]] rivers around the [[e:roccamonfina|Roccamonfina]] volcano. Greek writers used 'Ausonia' for much of early [[e:italy|Italy]], which suggests they were once a widespread people. Little is known of their origins or language.
aurunci.r: Known only from Roman and Greek sources, the Aurunci lived in hill towns such as Ausona, [[e:minturnae|Minturnae]], Vescia and [[e:suessa-aurunca|Suessa Aurunca]]. They fought [[e:rome|Rome]] and the [[e:latin|Latins]] in the late 6th and early 5th centuries BCE, and in the 4th century came under Roman protection; in 337 BCE, under attack from the [[s:sidicini|Sidicini]], they abandoned their town of Aurunca for Suessa.
aurunci.e: After they joined [[e:rome|Rome's]] enemies during the [[e:samnite-wars|Samnite Wars]], Rome destroyed the towns of Ausona, [[e:minturnae|Minturnae]] and Vescia in 314 BCE, massacring much of the population. Roman colonies followed at [[e:suessa-aurunca|Suessa Aurunca]] in 313 BCE and Minturnae in 296 BCE, and the people disappeared from history.

acco.t: Acco, a Canaanite harbour town on the bay of Haifa, a vassal of Egypt in the Amarna age and forerunner of the later port of Acre.
acco.o: Akka grew on Tel Akko, beside the mouth of the Na'aman river, in the [[e:middle-bronze-age|Middle Bronze Age]], when it was surrounded by massive earth ramparts. It is named in Egyptian execration texts and in the list of towns conquered by [[e:thutmose-iii|Thutmose III]].
acco.r: As a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] it was governed by local kings who traded with [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] and the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] through its harbour. Its rulers Zurata and Zatatna appear in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]], accused by neighbours of plotting with [[e:egypt|Egypt's]] enemies.
acco.e: Acco's Canaanite kingdom ended in the upheavals of the 12th century BCE. The city later came under Phoenician rule, was renamed [[s:barca|Ptolemais]] by the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]], and survives as [[e:acre|Acre]].

aceh-sultanate.t: The powerful Muslim sultanate of northern Sumatra, rival of Portuguese Malacca, centre of Islamic scholarship, and fierce opponent of the Dutch.
aceh-sultanate.o: [[e:aceh|Aceh]] grew from a small port near the old [[s:lamuri|Lamuri]] kingdom. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:ali-mughayat-syah|Ali Mughayat Syah]], ruling from about 1514, united the north of [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]], conquering [[s:pedir|Pedir]] in 1524 and expelling the Portuguese from [[e:samudera-pasai-sultanate|Samudera Pasai]]. His capital, later called [[e:banda-aceh|Kutaraja]] and now [[s:kingdom-of-banda|Banda]] Aceh, controlled the northern entrance to the [[e:strait-of-malacca|Strait of Malacca]].
aceh-sultanate.r: [[e:aceh|Aceh]] dominated the [[e:pepper|pepper]] trade and sought Ottoman help against the Portuguese in the 1560s. Under [[e:iskandar-muda|Iskandar Muda]], 1607 to 1636, it conquered much of [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]] and the peninsula but failed to take [[e:malacca|Malacca]] in 1629. Scholars such as [[e:hamzah-fansuri|Hamzah Fansuri]] and [[e:abdurrauf-of-singkil|Abdurrauf of Singkil]] wrote major Malay religious works, and four queens ruled from 1641 to 1699.
aceh-sultanate.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] invaded in 1873, beginning the [[e:aceh-war|Aceh War]], one of the longest colonial conflicts. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:muhammad-daud-syah|Muhammad Daud Syah]] surrendered in 1903, though resistance continued for years. [[e:aceh|Aceh's]] independent past fed later movements for autonomy within [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]].

cr.a: MapGrid (old version SKopp, Zscout370 and Ranking Update)

abdera.t: Thracian coastal city refounded by refugees from Teos, birthplace of the philosophers Democritus and Protagoras.
abdera.o: A first settlement at [[s:abdera-800|Abdera]] by [[s:clazomenae|Clazomenae]] c. 654 BCE was driven out by [[e:thracians|Thracians]]. Around 545 BCE citizens of [[s:teos|Teos]], fleeing the Persian general [[e:harpagus|Harpagus]], refounded the city on the Thracian coast east of the [[e:nestos|Nestos]] river.
abdera.r: [[s:abdera-800|Abdera]] grew rich from trade with the Thracian interior, minting [[e:silver|silver]] coins with a griffin, and paid one of the highest tributes in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. It produced [[e:democritus|Democritus]], founder of atomism, and the sophist [[e:protagoras|Protagoras]]. Despite them, Abderites were the butt of Greek jokes about stupidity. The city was later under the influence of the [[s:odrysian-kingdom|Odrysian Kingdom]].
abdera.e: [[s:abdera-800|Abdera]] was weakened by Thracian attacks in the 4th century BCE and annexed by [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-macedon|Kingdom of Macedon]] c. 350 BCE. It survived under Macedonian, Ptolemaic and Roman rule as a smaller town.

arguin.t: Portugal's first fortified trading post in Africa south of the Sahara, set up in 1445 on a small island off the Mauritanian coast.
arguin.o: Portuguese expeditions sponsored by [[e:prince-henry-the-navigator|Prince Henry the Navigator]] reached the Bay of Arguin in 1443. In 1445 a trading post was established on the island, and a fort was built around 1455, the first permanent European factory on the West African coast.
arguin.r: Arguin traded horses, cloth and grain to Saharan traders for gold, slaves and gum arabic, diverting part of the caravan trade to the sea. It was run by a royal monopoly and a garrison, with a chapel and a small community of traders, and [[e:berbers|Berber]] and [[e:sanhaja|Sanhaja]] merchants came to the island to deal.
arguin.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] took Arguin in 1633, and it then passed back and forth between the Dutch, English, French and the [[e:brandenburg-african-company|Brandenburg African Company]], which held it from 1685. [[e:france|France]] took control in 1721. The fort was later abandoned, and the bay is now part of [[e:mauritania|Mauritania's]] [[e:banc-darguin-national-park|Banc d'Arguin National Park]].

awan-dynasty.t: The first known royal house of Elam, which fought and treated with the kings of Akkad and whose last king briefly ruled Susa and the Diyala region.
awan-dynasty.o: Awan was a highland district of western [[e:iran|Iran]], probably north of [[e:susa|Susa]] near modern [[e:dezful|Dezful]] or in Luristan, whose exact site is unknown. An Elamite king list from Susa names twelve kings of Awan, and the [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] says kingship passed briefly to Awan, reflecting its power in the 24th century BCE.
awan-dynasty.r: Kings of Awan led a coalition of Elamite lands and resisted the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]]: [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon]] and [[e:rimush|Rimush]] record victories over [[e:elam|Elam]] and its allies. [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin]] later concluded a treaty, written in Elamite, with a ruler of Awan, probably Hita. The gods [[e:inshushinak|Inshushinak]] and [[e:humban|Humban]] were central to Elamite religion. The last king, [[e:kutik-inshushinak|Puzur-Inshushinak]], built at Susa and left inscriptions in Akkadian and in [[e:linear-elamite|Linear Elamite]], a script largely deciphered only in 2020.
awan-dynasty.e: After [[e:akkad|Akkad's]] collapse [[e:kutik-inshushinak|Puzur-Inshushinak]] expanded as far as [[s:eshnunna|Eshnunna]], but he was driven back by [[e:ur-nammu|Ur-Nammu]] around 2100 BCE. The [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]] took [[e:susa|Susa]], and leadership in [[e:elam|Elam]] passed to the [[s:shimashki-dynasty|Shimashki dynasty]] and the wider [[s:elamite-confederation|Elamite Confederation]].

apum.t: Apum, a north Mesopotamian kingdom ruling from Shamshi-Adad's former capital Shubat-Enlil, until Babylon destroyed it in 1728 BCE.
apum.o: Shubat-[[e:enlil|Enlil]], at [[e:tell-leilan|Tell Leilan]] in the [[e:khabur-river|Khabur]] plains, was the old city of Shehna, renamed by [[e:shamshi-adad-i|Shamshi-Adad]] as the capital of his [[s:kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia|Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia]]. After his death in the 1770s BCE his realm broke apart, and the city became the seat of the local kingdom of Apum.
apum.r: Its kings, such as Haya-abum and [[e:till-abnu|Till-Abnu]], played the great powers against each other, and their palace archives at [[e:tell-leilan|Tell Leilan]] preserve letters and treaties with [[e:assur|Assur]] and other neighbours. The kingdom depended on rain-fed barley farming and the trade routes across the [[e:khabur-river|Khabur]].
apum.e: The [[s:babylonian-empire|Babylonian Empire]] under [[e:samsu-iluna|Samsu-iluna]], [[e:hammurabi|Hammurabi's]] son, sacked Shubat-[[e:enlil|Enlil]] in 1728 BCE and ended the kingdom. The city was abandoned, and excavations by [[e:yale-university|Yale University]] from 1979 recovered its archives.

alavid-dynasty.t: A Zaydi Shia state on the Caspian coast whose imams converted the Daylamites to Islam and opened the way for Daylamite power across Iran.
alavid-dynasty.o: In 864 the people of [[e:ruyan|Ruyan]] and [[e:tabaristan|Tabaristan]], angered by land seizures under [[e:tahirid-dynasty|Tahirid]] governors, invited [[e:hasan-ibn-zayd|Hasan ibn Zayd]], a descendant of the Prophet's grandson Hasan, to lead them. With Daylamite support he took [[e:amol|Amol]] and established a Zaydi [[e:imamate|imamate]], calling himself al-Da'i ila'l-Haqq, 'the summoner to the truth'.
alavid-dynasty.r: The Alavids ruled in the name of a religious mission rather than the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]], governing from [[e:amol|Amol]] with the help of Daylamite and Gilite warriors. [[e:hasan-ibn-zayd|Hasan ibn Zayd]] was succeeded by his brother [[e:muhammad-ibn-zayd|Muhammad ibn Zayd]], killed by the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanids]] in 900. [[e:hasan-al-utrush|Hasan al-Utrush]], known as al-Nasir al-Kabir, restored the state in 914 and converted many [[e:daylamites|Daylamites]] and [[e:gilaks|Gilites]] to [[e:zaydism|Zaydi Islam]], writing works of law still respected by Zaydis.
alavid-dynasty.e: After [[e:hasan-al-utrush|al-Utrush]]'s death in 917 the dynasty became a tool of Daylamite commanders such as [[e:makan-ibn-kaki|Makan ibn Kaki]] and [[e:mardavij|Mardavij]], and it ended around 928. Its converts went on to found the [[s:ziyarid-dynasty|Ziyarid dynasty]] and [[s:buyid-dynasty|Buyid dynasty]].
